News.title: Moment massive WW2 bomb weighing 79 STONE is blown to smithereens at UK quarry in dramatic explosion
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment a huge WW2 bomb discovered at a sand and quarry was blown up in a controlled explosion.

The seven-foot-long, 79 stone device was found by workers at a site in Barton-under-Needwood, Staffordshire.



Emergency services rushed to the scene on August 6, including cops and military teams to tackle the huge ordnance.

Dramatic footage has now emerged showing enormous plumes of smoke billowing into the air as the 1,100lb device was blown to smithereens.



Ahead of the war relic being destroyed by bomb disposal experts, seven residents living nearby were evacuated.

It was blown to bits after experts determined the device was too dangerous to move.

Specialist teams used sand from the quarry to build protective cages around the device before it was pulverised.

A 900m (2,953ft) cordon was initially put in place in the area before this was reduced to 200m.



It was later fully removed so people could return to their homes.

A Heidelberg Materials UK spokesperson said: “Well thankfully that’s not something we have to deal with every day.

“Earlier this week we uncovered an historic WWII bomb at our Barton sand and gravel quarry in Staffordshire.

“After its discovery within the excavation area at the southern end of the quarry near to the River Trent, our emergency procedures came into play and the police and military were soon on site.

“After establishing that the device was unsafe to move, bomb disposal experts used sand from the site to create cages to contain the bomb and subsequently carried out a safe, controlled explosion.



“Well done to our Barton quarry team for their calm and efficient handling of this unexpected event and huge thanks to the teams from East Staffordshire Police and the Ministry of Defence for their professionalism and diligence.”

The unexploded bomb was initially found on Tuesday, August 4.

Cops worked with specialist colleagues from Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) to dispose of the ordnance safely.

All railway lines running between Tamworth and Burton-on-Trent were blocked on August 6.

Some trains were cancelled or delayed by up to an hour prior to the explosion, National Rail said.



The A38 and other roads that were closed were also reopened to traffic following the detonation.

News.title: Plagiarism prof is just a thinking man’s Lee Andrews – beggars belief that woke Cambridge & BBC made him a poster boy
News.content:
JASON ARDAY: Cambridge University’s widely publicised youngest black professor.

Now its youngest black ex-professor after he resigned last week.



On some level, it is hard not to have some sympathy with a sweet-looking chap whose lies have not so much caught up with him, more snowballed over him completely and absolutely.

But those who really deserve our sympathy are the hard-working Cambridge students, whose degrees may forever now be called into question.

And the cerebral candidates whose dream job he snatched by virtue of what appears to be a largely fabricated CV.



And the bleeding-heart liberals who slammed the right-wing Press for trying to bring down a trailblazer.

They have just taken back their collective DEI cause 30 years. Because Arday is little more than a thinking man’s Lee Andrews: A smiling assassin who has single-handedly almost brought down an academic institution.

Make no bones about it, this is Cambridge’s Ratner moment.

His departmental boss, Hilary Cremin, came out to laud his anorexically thin body of “work” as the “best in the world”. Which, as one commentator observed, might not sit well with students of, say, Harvard’s Lawrence D Bobo, Stanford’s Thomas Sowell or the profound insights on race of Britain’s luminary, Heidi Safia Mirza of UCL.

How those Dark Blues must be chuckling to themselves across the River Thames.



At the time of writing, publishers at Simon & Schuster still plan to go ahead with Arday’s memoir, Great And Unfortunate Things.

Presumably, then, it will sit in the fantasy section of Waterstones, near Harry Potter.

Not even JK Rowling in her pomp could have come up with such a tale, though.

Wild claims of running 600 miles in six days and 30 marathons in 35 days, completing the latter feat with a broken leg, one that had ballooned to twice its normal width.

Alas, a photo of him crossing the finish line of said run showed a normal-looking appendage.



And here lies Mr Arday’s biggest problem. As a millennial, he grew up in an age of receipts.

That is to say, anything anyone under-45 has ever done is plastered all over the internet.

Every spit and cough documented for all to see. I mean, there is a literal photo of me spitting on Facebook circa 2007, which is lovely.

Yet very few photos appear to exist of any of this fantasist’s spurious claims.

You’d think Cambridge — who came out on the veritable rampage when the first allegations of plagiarism surfaced — might have done even a cursory background/social media check when they first actively championed this fall guy.



Likewise the BBC, who pompously declare themselves the world’s “most trusted broadcaster”, might have done some due diligence before breathlessly highlighting interviewing him.

The clues about Mr Arday, who denies being a liar, were all there.

After all, a man who scraped two GCSEs in textiles and PE might not be our next Great Mind. But no.

So desperate to find a poster boy were these two veritable institutions, all basic common sense went out the window.

Now, it emerges, Cambridge’s own newspaper is refusing to cover the story. Which is, at best, an embarrassing oversight for what is rapidly becoming the most talked-about news story of 2026, and, at worst, pernicious censorship.



Elevating a man so ill-equipped to deal with the inevitable fallout is cruel. Although if it’s any consolation to Jason, his story makes for a Bafta-winning documentary.

The Tinder Swindler for the internet age: The Professor Who Never Was, perhaps.

Naturally, TikTok and Instagram are going wild with their own hot takes.

One meme showed an AI Jason overtaking Sir Mo Farah to win Olympic gold in 2012, another showed him landing on the moon before Neil Armstrong (not unreasonable given Jason claimed to have been in the series Seven- Up, which first aired decades before his birth) and others are questioning whether he also managed to survive the Titanic.

One meme showed an AI Jason overtaking Sir Mo Farah to win Olympic gold in 2012, another showed him landing on the moon before Neil Armstrong (not unreasonable given Jason claimed to have been in the series Seven-Up, which first aired decades before his birth) and others are questioning whether he also managed to survive the Titanic.



It would all be funny if it wasn’t so unavoidably sad.

SMACKS OF FILM FIONA

PRINCESS Fiona is alive and well.

Ahead of the fifth instalment of Shrek, due for release next summer, up popped this X-rated preview.



Is it just me, or does this dominatrix have a touch of the green ogre about her? Maybe it’s just unfortunate lighting.

Whatever, Melanie Bull, who receives more than £1,000 a month in benefits including disability, is selling sexual services on adult websites as a side hustle.

But hey, whatever floats your boat.

POLITICIAN Jo Galer took a live zoom straight from the toilet. The utterly unbothered New Zealand councillor joined a live-stream meeting from her bathroom, with drying undergarments and laundry on full display.



Thus sharing precisely what she thinks of antipodean politics.

MR BIG BUCKS

ANOTHER fine mess by Thames Water chiefs this weekend.

Six weeks after implementing a hosepipe ban in my West London borough – where environmentalist Sir David Attenborough lives – a water main burst, causing millions of litres of flooding.

Naturally, barely a peep from Thames Water.

And no sign of boots on the ground, despite the fact countless homes have been left without running water.



Oh that’s right. They’re too busy paying Steve Buck, their new chief financial officer, a £1million signing-on fee.

Grrr.

OLD JOKE, RICHARD

AND so, gerbils the world over exhaled a collective sigh of relief*.



Because here’s Richard Gere spotted “getting close” to his latest, much younger co-star Diana Silvers on the set of their new romantic drama, Asymmetry.

Quite how producers and script writers, in this day and age, think it’s OK to cast a 76-year-old opposite a 28-year-old female love interest baffles.

*Only funny if you’re familiar with the notorious urban myth about the Hollywood actor.

SPEED ZONE RUSE

CAN we all stop pretending, please, and admit that 20mph speed limits are little more than money-making ruses.



Lynda La Plante, she of Prime Suspect fame, is the latest to fall foul of such endlessly opportunist cameras.

The 83-year-old, who drives her dog to the park and uses the car to “meet criminals for research”, was done for by confusing signs, and one camera only ten seconds beyond the 20mph sign.

She has now been handed a six-month ban, something she fears might end her writing career.

These cameras aren’t catching Premier League footballers in souped-up Lamborghinis or 17-year-old boy racers.

They’re crippling hard-working, otherwise law-abiding citizens.

News.title: Savile Row tailors in clash with The Beatles over plans for new museum at Fab Four’s old HQ where they played iconic gig
News.content:
PLANS for a Beatles museum have received a dressing-down from tailors.

The Fab Four’s old HQ in London’s Savile Row is set to be a visitor attraction featuring the rooftop where they played their final gig in 1969.



But Mark Henderson, of the Savile Row Bespoke Association, said it could cause “dangerous congestion” and have a “negative impact” on businesses.

He told council planners: “The pavements on the street are narrow — already frequently clogged with visitors.”



The association represents brands including Edward Sexton, who made suits for The Beatles.

Apple Corps, the Fab Four’s record label, plans to open The Beatles at 3 Savile Row next year.



The seven-floor museum would open the roof where John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr played in public for the last time before cops called a halt due to noise complaints.

There’s also a re-creation of the basement studio where Let It Be was recorded.

Reps told Westminster City Council it will be a “local cultural asset (not just a tourist destination)” and an “education platform rooted in music, creativity, and social history”.

The council will decide in due course.



But the plan is backed by surviving Beatles Paul and Ringo.

Paul said previously: “There are so many special memories within the walls, not to mention the rooftop.”

News.title: Club from iconic British movie is gutted after huge fire ‘started deliberately’ as locals ‘absolutely devastated’
News.content:
'ARSON' ATTACK Club from iconic British movie is gutted after huge fire ‘started deliberately’ as locals ‘absolutely devastated’

A WORKING men’s club made famous by an Oscar-nominated movie has been gutted after a huge fire, leaving locals devastated.

The dangerous blaze broke out at Shiregreen Working Men’s Club in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, on Sunday afternoon.



Firefighters bravely battled the flames but despite their best efforts the club – which was used for the finale of the hit 1997 film The Full Monty – has now been left a charred shell.

South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue said at 5.30pm that eight fire engines had been deployed to the scene of the blaze on Shiregreen Lane.



Videos circulating on social media show smoke billowing from the landmark building before flames took hold with the club left a smouldering wreck.

Cops and emergency services confirmed today that the fire was “believed to have been started deliberately”.

Shiregreen Club, or Shiregreen Working Men’s Club as it was at the time, was the location for the finale of the hit 1997 comedy film The Full Monty.

The Full Monty followed six unemployed men from Sheffield who transformed into Chippendale dancers that stripped off so they could raise some cash.



The movie, starring Robert Carlyle and Mark Addy, ended up as one of the best-loved and highest-grossing British films of the 1990s.

A spokesperson for South Yorkshire Police said: “We were called just before 5pm yesterday following a report of a fire at Shiregreen Working Men’s Club.

“It is reported that the fire service was called and eight engines attended.

“The building was unoccupied and no injuries were reported. It is believed that the fire was started deliberately and we have launched an arson investigation.”

Shiregreen Working Men’s Club once stood as a familiar and much-loved social hub for generations of local residents.



The club achieved cinematic fame after being used as the setting for the final, infamous striptease scene in The Full Monty, the Oscar-nominated film set in post-industrial Sheffield.

The scene was shot before a live audience.

It saw characters Gaz, Dave, Gerald and Lomper take to the stage in a last-ditch attempt to earn money after losing their jobs at the steelworks – a moment that would go on to become one of British cinema’s most recognisable endings.



Local women were invited to attend the filming, meaning the crowd captured on screen was made up largely of locals from the surrounding area.

Despite a budget of under £3million, it made over £200million in ticket sales and was later adapted into a musical in 2000 and a play in 2013.

For a time, the club leaned into its newfound fame, even erecting a sign proudly declaring itself the “Home of The Full Monty”.

However, the attention did not translate into long-term survival.

By the mid-2000s, trade had begun to decline, reflecting the wider struggles faced by working men’s clubs across the country before the venue shut its doors for good in 2018.



However, an application to demolish the building to make way for flats was rejected by Sheffield City Council in 2020, after more than 1,000 people signed a petition.

There were plans announced in 2024 to reopen the building as a boxing gym, cafe and community centre but they were later scrapped.

Following the blaze at the iconic location, the fire service said: “Eight fire engines are in attendance at a fire in a derelict building on Shiregreen Lane, Sheffield.

“Please avoid the area and keep windows and doors closed if you live nearby.”

News.title: Ghoulish content creators slammed for visiting Lindsay Clancy’s home where she killed kids after jury’s secretive trip
News.content:
TRUE crime sleuths have sparked outrage by filming drive-by videos of the former home where Lindsay Clancy killed her three children — just days after jurors were given a rare tour of the property.

Clancy is accused of murdering five-year-old daughter Cora, three-year-old son Dawson and eight-month-old son Callan at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.



Prosecutors allege Clancy strangled the children with exercise bands and left them in the basement of the home, while her husband, Patrick, was out picking up dinner.

She then allegedly attempted to take her own life by jumping from a second-floor window.





The former labor and delivery nurse survived the fall and has been left paralyzed from the waist down.

Clancy, 35, has pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges, with her defense arguing that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time and had been prescribed a cocktail of medications.

Jurors were taken to the home to see the layout for themselves and better understand the physical evidence and competing accounts of what happened inside on the night of the killings.

Following the tragedy, Patrick sold the residence in January 2024 for $675,000.



Social media footage obtained by The U.S. Sun shows content creators filming the home while driving past and later sharing the videos on Instagram and TikTok.

One user, named Jamies Just Jammin, wrote, “I debated whether or not I should post this here as this is not what my page is about, but where the entire nation is obsessed with this case I thought some may be interested.

“The Clancy murders happened less than 20 minutes from where I live. I had to go into the town recently for something and drove by the Clancy house. I said a prayer for Cora, Dawson, and Callan.”

But she was slammed by followers on Instagram who felt it was inappropriate.

One wrote underneath, “Ok and? I live 5 min away. Not putting someone’s home on social media though.”



A second wrote, “I dont think driving by the house was necessary..a pix would have been fine.”

“I get everyone’s obsession with this. I am too. My parents live on this side of town and it’s been crazy. A couple bought the house. Probably best to let them have privacy. I can’t imagine living there now,” a third added.

One also told the user to “get a life,” while others were glad to see the footage and admitted they were also “obsessed” with the case.



The female creator wrote back, “There is a whole country very interested in this case, Kristine. Should they ‘get a life’ too? Or are you bigger than everyone?”

Jamie, who posted the video, also claimed she could still see the playground in the backyard at the home.

One follower admitted, “I drove by myself recently. I just had to. It was so heartbreaking seeing where it all happened.”

The creator also shared the clip on TikTok where it was liked by more than 12,000 users.

Another content creator, who goes by @CourtDawgDaniel, has been parking his RV at the courthouse every day and confronting people as they come and go from the trial.



He filmed himself driving the route from the courthouse to the Clancy home earlier this week, before posting the footage on social media.

“We are about to make a turn onto the street the Clancy’s lived on,” Daniel is heard saying in the clip.

“It’s about point one miles up the road on the left, obviously I’m not going to divulge the address online, you know, for privacy concerns for the people that live there now, but I’ll try to drive real slow.”

“Got a bunch of cars behind me, but want to make sure we get a good look at this house. This is it right here,” he added, as the camera panned across.

He then filmed the property, with a boat visible beneath a cover in the driveway, and shared the video on TikTok and Instagram.



One user wrote underneath, “How twisted a guy are you. Get the hell out of their it’s none of ours business old man (sic).”

A third TikToker also posted a video driving down the street and past the house, writing, “3 min. drive from Clancy house to CVS.”

The video was liked by more than 55,000 people, with many debating the case in the comments.

The U.S. Sun has reached out to the new owners of the home.

Other social media users have shared the full address of the property from public court records.



The U.S. Sun obtained filings that show the buyers – a practicing attorney operating out of Plymouth, Massachusetts, alongside another co-owner – acquired the home before subsequently moving the property title into a personal living trust for estate planning.

They also financed the purchase by taking out a $607,500 mortgage through CMG Mortgage INC.

Ahead of Clancy’s murder trial, prosecutors filed a motion requesting a formal jury tour of the private residence.

The prosecution argued that physically seeing the home’s layout was vital for jurors to understand the spatial context of the crime, including the distance between the basement, the main floor, and the second-floor window.

The current homeowners objected and asked the court to block the visit.



However, the judge ultimately overruled them, deciding that the physical context of the home provided necessary evidence for the jury to evaluate the case.

In late July, court officers and police supervised a controlled walk-through where jurors inspected the basement, main living areas, and upper level.

Strict court rules were enforced prohibiting anyone from opening closet doors, touching personal property, or disturbing items inside the house.

Some social media users following the trial have been left stunned that the Clancy family home is still standing, after other properties linked to notorious murder cases have been demolished.

The off-campus home where four University of Idaho students were murdered by Bryan Kohberger was torn down before his trial began.



One Facebook user in a Clancy trial group wrote: “I just can’t understand how anyone could live in this house after what happened there. While I can understand selling it from the father’s POV, finances etc. I just can’t imagine living there.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another said the property should have been demolished and turned into “a memorial or a park/playground in memory of the children.”

A third added, “I could never live there after those babies died. I’d cry and it would break my heart. God bless those people who bought it.”

News.title: Mystery of warship which vanished 118 years ago is finally solved as divers find it off UK coast
News.content:
SEA SOLVE Mystery of warship which vanished 118 years ago is finally solved as divers find it off UK coast

DIVERS have discovered the long-lost wreck of a Royal Navy warship which sank 118 years ago.

HMS Tiger disappeared in 1908, after she strayed into the path of the 10,000-ton HMS Berwick during a training exercise and was sliced in two.



Fewer than half of its 57 crew members survived the deadly collision, which took place just off the Isle of Wight.

For over a century, the exact coordinates of the wreckage have remained a mystery to divers – until today.



Shipwreck historians from ProjectXplore have now discovered the remains of the sunken torpedo destroyer – just as new legislation comes into effect to protect wreckages.

Under the Armed Forces Bill, it will now be an offence to disturb or dislodge items from a wreck without permission.





Divers will be permitted to visit the sites, under a ‘look but don’t touch’ policy.

Automatic legal protections will apply to thousands of graves belonging to sailors and marines.

Minister for the Armed Forces Louise Sandher-Jones MP said: “As well as protecting UK national security, Defence has a role to play in preserving our maritime heritage and the memory of those who gave their lives serving their country.”

She added that the new measures will give sailors who died at sea the “dignity and respect they deserve”.



While dozens of military shipwrecks have been safeguarded from illegal activity since the mid-1980s, only vessels lost within the last 200 years can qualify for protection.

Expanding the Protection of Military Remains Act will ensure wreckages dating as far back as the Spanish Armada – including those of the former enemy – will be protected.



Employees at ProjectXplore – who spent years figuring out the location of HMS Tiger through intensive archival research – have welcomed the amendments.

Leo Fielding and Dan McMullen, co-organisers of ProjectXplore said: “It has been the privilege of a lifetime to research, discover and document the wreck of HMS Tiger.

“We sincerely hope that our work will ensure that HMS Tiger, her story and the memory of those connected with her endure for future generations.

“ProjectXplore welcomes the proposed amendments in the Armed Forces Bill.

“We believe they represent a constructive step forward in protecting the United Kingdom’s maritime heritage and ensuring that wreck sites of historical and archaeological significance are appropriately safeguarded.”



Royal Navy Deputy Fleet Wreck Officer Lieutenant Commander Jen Smith added: “Protecting military wrecks helps to ensure they are preserved for future generations.

“This is beneficial for our rich maritime heritage and the diving community who keep the stories of our lost shipwrecks alive.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It follows the discovery of an even older vessel in June last year, off the coast of Plymouth.

SS Nantes sank in 1888 after colliding with a German sailing vessel, sinking approximately ten hours after the hit as desperate crew members plugged the holes with mattresses.

News.title: China evacuates ONE MILLION people as Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall bringing 100mph gales and grounding 1,000 flights
News.content:
CHINA has evacuated more than one million people as Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall, bringing devastation with it.

Several provinces in the east of the country have been hit by torrential rain and storms with around 100mph gales, stopping 40 per cent of flights.



Dolphin, China’s most powerful typhoon so far this year, packed maximum sustained winds of 151kph (93.8mph) near its centre when it made landfall in Zhejiang, the province to the south and west of Shanghai, on Sunday evening before weakening to a tropical storm.

Its remaining rain clouds continued to soak the eastern provinces including Anhui, Jiangsu and Shandong on Monday.



Many streets in Shanghai, the country’s second most populous city, were flooded, including in the main commercial centres.

The city’s two airports cancelled a total of 943 flights due to the typhoon, reducing capacity by nearly 40 per cent, state broadcaster CCTV said.



China Eastern Airlines said on Monday it was trying to resume flights to Shanghai, Zhejiang and other destinations in an “orderly manner.”

Shanghai also suspended some of its metro lines on Monday, and China Railway Chengdu Group suspended 115 trains, state news agency Xinhua reported.



Many streets in Shanghai’s suburban Jiading and Qingpu districts around the city centre remained waterlogged, according to live-streams shared by residents on social media.

The live videos showed people wading through knee-high murky water.

Hou Lina, 38, who works in sales in Jiading in Shanghai said: “It rained almost all-night last night.



“When I woke up this morning, I found the neighbourhood flooded, and the streets were severely flooded.”

She added: “I’ve lived in Shanghai for 10 years, and this is the first time I’ve experienced such inconvenience from a typhoon.

“This is the first time I’ve encountered such widespread flooding.”



In Shanghai’s Jinshan, the district authority said non-essential businesses and organisations could temporarily halt operations, classes, outdoor events and transit services, amid forecasts of continued strong winds and heavy rain on Monday.

Authorities warned of risks of severe flooding and landslides in some areas.

State broadcaster CCTV reported that authorities in Yueqing, a city in Zhejiang province, searched for people trapped in flooded homes.

Powerful winds and lashing rain flipped over a truck in Zhejiang’s Wenzhou, a video posted on TikTok on Sunday showed.

It was not clear what happened to the driver.



Authorities warned that 74 rivers in the Taihu Lake basin and the coastal areas of eastern Zhejiang have exceeded warning levels, and that flood risks for small and medium-sized rivers in heavy rainfall areas are high.

Dolphin is forecast to move deeper inland to the central provinces of Hubei and Henan in the coming days while also pushing moisture north.

Authorities in the capital Beijing raised warnings for torrential rain and said the city was prepared to activate its flood control response on Tuesday morning.

Beijing is expected to experience “significant rainfall” from Tuesday until Thursday, with authorities warning of the risk of flash floods in the city and landslides in the surrounding mountainous areas.

The typhoon had already travelled 3,728 miles before it made landfall, giving it a life-cycle three times longer than an ordinary typhoon, and bringing with it an ultra-large cloud system that enveloped China’s east, CCTV said in another report.



Dolphin’s impact was also being compared to Doksuri in 2023.

That typhoon crossed the country after causing destruction in southeastern Fujian province, unleashing record-breaking rainfall in Beijing.

As the storm clouds meet colder air in the north, Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei will need to brace for heavy rain into Thursday, CCTV said.

Hong Kong, on China’s southern coast, has seen extreme heat due to Dolphin, recording its hottest day ever on Sunday at 36.9C, the highest since records began in 1884, according to the Hong Kong Observatory, the territory’s weather body.

TSR (Tropical Storm Risk) said it expected the 2026 northwest Pacific typhoon season to be one of the most active on record and to include 28 tropical storms, 20 typhoons and 13 intense typhoons.



TSR said the ongoing strong El Nino event, high activity to date and weaker-than-normal trade winds across the northwest Pacific basin, were key reasons for the intensity of the typhoon season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Elsewhere, Tropical Storm Chan-hom was heading toward Japan’s Pacific coast.

The storm had 51 mph winds on Monday morning and was forecast to strengthen slightly before landfall Tuesday into Wednesday, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

News.title: More than two-thirds of England now in drought
News.content:
Chair of the National Drought Group, Tony Grayling, said that drought conditions will continue to worsen until "significant and sustained rainfall".

The week ahead is forecast to remain mostly dry, as the fifth heatwave of the year intensifies, although there are signs of some rain coming into the UK on Sunday.

"We know the hot and dry weather is taking a real toll on farming and there will be long-lasting impacts on our environment," Grayling said in a statement, adding that "we need everyone's help in using a little less water to make sure our current water reserves last".

The National Drought Group said most of England is now experiencing a flash drought, which "develops very quickly" and is "brought about by a combination of very low rainfall and higher temperatures."

Yorkshire and north-east England have been moved to "prolonged dry weather" status, which is the stage before drought.

Nowhere in England is now under a "normal" status.

Hot weather is continuing, with the UK Health Security Agency issuing amber heat health alerts for all of England apart from the North East from Tuesday at 09:00 BST until Friday at 21:00 BST.

An amber alert means significant impacts "are likely" across health and social care services due to the high temperatures.

The continued hot and dry conditions increase the risk of wildfires. Dozens of firefighters are currently battling a fire in the New Forest, which earlier on Monday was estimated to be the size of 140 football pitches (247 acres).

Scotland and Northern Ireland have not been experiencing drought conditions and are expected to see spells of heavy rain over the week ahead.

Scotland does not declare drought, but monitors "water scarcity".

While conditions have improved in some parts of Scotland following recent rainfall, some eastern areas remain in the two most extreme categories of "moderate" or "significant" scarcity, according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.

News.title: Record 230 people cross Channel in one small boat
News.content:
A small boat has crossed the English Channel carrying 230 people, the largest number to make the journey in a single vessel.

It breaks the previous record set in July, when 165 people made the crossing on a single vessel.

The boat arrived in the UK in the early hours of Monday.

A picture taken off the coast of northern France showed the inflatable boat was so full many passengers had to dangle their legs in the water as it entered the busy shipping route.

A Home Office spokesperson said this latest incident demonstrated the "reckless and dangerous tactics employed by criminal gangs... who continue to put lives at risk by cramming ever greater numbers of people onto unseaworthy vessels".

French rescuers said the 15m (49ft) boat was "buckling" in the water and could have led to a "tragedy".

The boat was already carrying about 50 people when it was seen heading towards a beach to pick more passengers up, the crew in Berck-sur-Mer added.

French maritime officials said 30 migrants were left stranded by the tide during a boarding attempt at Berck beach in northern France.

They were brought to safety by maritime and land-based rescue services, the statement from France's Channel and North Sea Maritime Prefecture said.

The boat carrying 232 people continued its journey, before two passengers requested assistance and were taken to Calais by a French Navy rescue ship, the statement added.

News.title: New weight-loss pill approved for use in UK
News.content:
A daily weight-loss pill made by the drug firm behind the Mounjaro jab has been approved for use in the UK - the first country in Europe to do so.

Foundayo, made by Eli Lilly, is for treating obesity and type 2 diabetes.

But while people will be able to buy it privately with a prescription, the approval by the Medicines and Healthcare productors Regulatory Agency does not automatically mean it will be made available on the NHS.

Foundayo is a form of GLP-1 medication that blunts appetite, and comes after the MHRA approved a pill version of a similar weight-loss drug, Wegovy, in June.

Eli Lilly said while it could immediately be used by the NHS for type 2 diabetes, it would be making an application to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence in England for it to be recommended as a weight loss treatment as well.

Dr Simon Cork, from Anglia Ruskin University, said while the weight-loss benefits of Foundayo were less than other treatments, patients could still expect to see "significant, clinically meaningful changes to their weight".

And he said a key advantage was that it was likely to be cheaper than other weight-loss treatments, which have tended to be tightly restricted by the NHS.

University of Glasgow expert Prof Naveed Sattar agreed it was "good news".

He said another benefit was its convenience, pointing out that unlike the Wegovy pill, which has to be taken on an empty stomach, this pill could be taken at any time of the day.

"The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences," he added.

Experts believe it could help people coming off weight-loss jabs remain slim.

Trials found that patients who had used weight loss jabs and then been given the tablet, also called orforglipron, every day for a year avoided regaining much of the weight they had lost - a known risk when coming off GLP-1 injections.

People on weight loss medication are also advised to eat a healthy diet and get enough exercise.

And, like any medication, there can be side effects to using Foundayo, including nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting.

News.title: Russian court bars only anti-war party from standing in parliamentary elections
News.content:
Russia's only liberal, anti-war party will not be able to take part in next month's parliamentary elections, a Moscow court has ruled.

Yabloko was the only registered party to oppose Russia's war on Ukraine.

The case against it was brought forward by Rodina, a pro-Kremlin nationalist party.

Hundreds of people - mostly very young - on Monday had stood outside the Moscow courthouse where the hearing was taking place in support of Yabloko, singing songs and waving flags.

Videos posted on social media showed that when news of the verdict spread among the crowd, many started chanting: "Shame! Shame!"

The lawsuit by the Rodina party accused Yabloko of publicly supporting an extremist organisation by publishing material on its website in support of the "international LGBT movement", which Russia's Supreme Court designated as extremist in 2023.

Rodina also said Yabloko was guilty of copyright infringement after a senior party member had quoted the lyrics of a Soviet-era song - "Let there always be sunshine" - in an interview.

At the hearing, Russia's financial monitoring service also claimed that Yabloko received money through third parties from foreign countries, including Germany and the US.

The Kremlin-controlled Central Electoral Commission had approved Yabloko's candidate list in late July.

But by then several party members had already been barred from running, including two deputy chairmen and deputy leader Maxim Kruglov, who was sentenced in June to seven years' imprisonment for social media posts about civilian casualties in Bucha, Mariupol and other Ukrainian cities.

And last week, Yabloko had suffered a cyberattack soon after launching a donations appeal for its election campaign fund.

It campaigned under the slogan "For peace and freedom! For a life without fear!" and advocated for a "ceasefire, diplomacy, and peace" and "for a Russia free from fear and political repression".

News.title: Treasury contributed to woman's death, inquest hears
News.content:
The death of a Treasury worker who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers was "materially contributed" to by her employers, an inquest has heard.

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Surrey Coroner's Court heard the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy which would have made clear that if the allegations were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

A spokesperson for the Treasury said it was "considering the findings carefully".

In a statement to the press, Moffat's family said they believed the Treasury failed in its duty of care.

"When she needed support, reassurance and fair treatment, she was left frightened, isolated and convinced her career and reputation had been destroyed," they added.

The inquest, in which a conclusion of suicide was recorded, heard that on 19 May Moffat went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

She was told of allegations she had shared sensitive personal information about colleagues, obtained as part of her job.

Moffat, from London, denied this.

News.title: Consortium including Jeff Bezos advances talks for stake in Liverpool FC
News.content:
A consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has advanced its talks to buy about a 30% stake in Liverpool, BBC Sport has been told.

The group is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed last month that the group had "expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club".

Bhatia is the son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal and had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.

American businessman Bezos, founder of e-commerce giant Amazon, is the fourth-richest person in the world.

According to Forbes, the 62-year-old has an estimated net worth of $256bn (Â£192bn).

FSG, who bought Liverpool in a Â£300m deal in 2010, previously sold a minority stake in the Anfield side to global sports investment firm Dynasty Equity.

BBC Sport contacted FSG about the latest developments, but they had no further comment.

In January, Liverpool became the top-earning Premier League club for the first time, according to analysis from financial firm Deloitte.

The following month the club announced record revenues of Â£703m for 2024-25 financial year.

News.title: From Dubai to a Dublin court - how alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan returned to Ireland
News.content:
Armed police took up positions at the entrances to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin, as the plane carrying Daniel Kinahan approached the city.

On the steps of the building, journalists from Irish and international media tracked the flight online.

The Irish government had sent its jet to Dubai.

It is usually used to transport ministers, but it left the United Arab Emirates (UAE) with a suspected crime boss on board.

The doors of the court opened around half an hour after the aircraft landed at a military airfield nine miles (14km) away.

As reporters went through security, we heard the sound of sirens outside - indicating the arrival of the accused.

The courtroom filled up over the next 45 minutes - as detectives, prosecutors, and some members of the public took up seats along with the media.

From the moment Kinahan entered the dock, until he was led out 13 minutes later, almost everyone was looking towards him - and the proceedings were accompanied by constant typing from the press benches.

Complex international investigations, and diplomacy, had led to this moment.

Kinahan was charged with a single offence - directing the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.

He did not have to enter a plea at this stage of the court process.

But his lawyers have previously told the BBC that the allegations he is a crime boss are false and have no evidential basis.

They also said he had no criminal record or convictions.

News.title: From Stonehenge to the Serpentine - satellite images show impact of hot, dry summer
News.content:
With more parts of England set to join Wales as being officially declared to be in drought, BBC Verify has been gathering satellite imagery showing the impact of this year's extreme summer heat.

From historic sites and parks to reservoirs and golf courses, the hot, dry weather has changed how large parts of the UK usually look.

This year's consecutive heatwaves and above-average temperatures have had a noticeable effect - even compared with last summer which was the UK's warmest on record.

News.title: Nigel Farage says incident at his home 'directly linked' to Ann Widdecombe murder
News.content:
Nigel Farage said an incident at his London home last year was "directly linked" to the murder of Ann Widdecombe, after counter-terror police reopened an inquiry into it last week.

It relates to what Farage described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025, the BBC understands.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation was handled.

At a Monday press conference, the Reform UK leader said: "I understand this is a completely unprecedented move, and yes, this is directly linked to the murder of Ann Widdecombe, and I'm afraid I just can't tell you any more than that at this stage."

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

The drugs were removed from the container and then delivered to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire, where Border Force officers swooped in.

They arrested nine men allegedly connected to the bust, who were later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

News.title: Antiques stolen in 16th Century manor house raid
News.content:
More than 20 antiques were stolen from a National Trust (NT) property during a break-in last month, it has been revealed.

The silver, pewter and brass items were taken from the 16th Century manor house at Baddesley Clinton in Warwickshire, on 30 July.

The most notable piece of the 25 taken was a Georgian silver salver engraved with the coat of arms of the Ferrers, the family who resided at the house for about five centuries, the NT said.

"We very much hope the objects will be returned, so they can be enjoyed by everyone," a spokesperson added.

News.title: Six arrested after woman found dead in north London
News.content:
Six people have been arrested on suspicion of murder following the death of a 23-year-old woman in north London.

Police were called at 09:33 BST on Thursday, following concerns for the welfare of a woman at a residential address on Bollinder Place, Clerkenwell.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and found an unresponsive woman, who was pronounced dead at the scene.

Four women, aged 20, 21, 23, and 26, and two men, aged 21 and 24 were arrested at the scene. All six have since been released on bail while enquiries continue.

Work is ongoing to trace the woman's next-of-kin, who will be supported by specially trained officers once identified.

Ch Supt Jason Stewart said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts remain with the family and friends of the young woman who has lost her life.

"We understand that news of an incident like this will cause concern within the local community."

News.title: Asylum seeker who groomed and raped girl, 13, jailed
News.content:
An asylum seeker who raped a 13-year-old girl after pretending to be a teenager on Snapchat has been jailed.

Abdul Khan attacked the girl in a nature reserve in Clifton, Nottingham, on 14 May last year.

Khan arrived in the UK in the back of a lorry in 2015, Nottingham Crown Court heard, and faces automatic deportation to Afghanistan after he has served two thirds of his sentence.

He was jailed for nine and a half years on Monday after he was convicted of two counts of rape, one count of sexual activity with a child, sexual communication with a child, meeting a child following grooming and perverting the course of justice.

A four-day trial was told Khan, who is believed to be 28 and already serving a 23-month sentence for sexual communication with a different child in Derbyshire, arranged to meet his victim in woodland after telling her on the Snapchat messaging app he was a 14-year-old boy.

When they met in person and it was clear he was not 14, he tried to appease her by claiming to be 16, the court heard.

After activity that jurors found had been consensual, Khan, of HMP Nottingham, twice raped the girl.

Judge Mark Watson said the victim told her father what had happened and he contacted police.

Khan was then linked to the rapes by a mobile phone seized during his arrest over his contact with the child in Derbyshire.

Yet despite DNA evidence subsequently linking him to the attack, Nottinghamshire Police said he continued to deny having met the victim.

Addressing Khan, the judge said: "You deliberately concealed your true identity. She thought she was communicating with a child of her own age.

"It was a lie you have persisted with throughout these proceedings."

News.title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
News.content:
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.

Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.

Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.

In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.

The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.

News.title: Owner of 250-year-old Grade II-listed windmill gave it colourful makeover without permission
News.content:
Dr Eiddwen Jones, 85, is the great-great-great-great-great-granddaughter of Thomas Jones, who she said was the first miller at Llynon mill in 1776.

He managed the property in the village of Llanddeusant, Anglesey, until he died in his nineties.

She said the windmill should be repainted in whitewash as it is a historical building, and traditionally "that's how the mills were".

The author, whose family moved from Anglesey to Flintshire 150 years ago, said she did not agree that the windmill was painted in the first place to celebrate the Eisteddfod.

She has visited the windmill several times throughout her life where Thomas Jones' name is painted inside, and said he "would have turned in his grave, I believe," if he had known about its new appearance.

Jones added that it looked "very impressive in its original colour" when driving towards it.

"It's been made fun of now rather than kept the fact that it was a historical building and that people have been working there for a couple of centuries," she said.

Holt said the mill can be hard to find for visitors, as it is not close to the A55 road.

But the new colours have sparked a lot of interest.

With winters especially proving difficult with fewer people coming, he added: "I have a duty to ensure the future of the mill for the next generation."

He apologised to the local authority, saying he "realises that they [the council] are only doing their job and I know that I have broken the rules".

But he added: "I'm struggling and the winter is hard, but painting the mill has attracted more visitors here and helped me pay the bills."

He is gathering the opinions of visitors to the mill this summer to make a case to the council.

News.title: British couple held in Iran end hunger strike
News.content:
A British couple jailed in Iran after being accused of espionage have ended their hunger strikes after 93 and 84 days respectively.

Craig and Lindsay Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while passing through Iran on a motorcycle journey from Europe to Australia. They were both sentenced to 10 years in jail in February, but Craig Foreman's family said his punishment had been extended by two years after speaking to the media.

The couple from East Sussex, who both deny espionage, went on hunger strike in May when prison authorities prevented them from calling their families.

The family of the couple said they had been protesting against how they and other prisoners were being treated.

A spokesperson for the family said the couple agreed with prison guards to end their strike to be able to speak directly to their loved ones again.

However, the family said contact was yet to be re-established, as of Monday afternoon.

The family had also previously called for the couple to end their hunger strike.

Five people outside the prison joined the pair on their hunger strike for the final five days from Tuesday to Saturday as an act of solidarity, the family added.

Lindsay Foreman's son Joe Bennett and four unnamed others took part in the UK, as well as other prisoners inside Tehran's Evin jail, the family said.

"My mum and Craig have spent months on hunger strike, and even at the point of bringing it to an end they wanted to make it about something bigger than themselves," Bennett, from Folkestone in Kent, said.

"Those final five days became about people standing together around values that should be universal: Truth, justice, kindness, peace and unity."

By the end of the protest, Craig Foreman had been on hunger strike for 93 days, and Lindsay Foreman for 84 days, the family added.

Although they said they were unaware of the condition of the pair, who had consumed just milk and either honey or salt in water during their strikes.

Bennett said the couple also went on a separate hunger strike back in November as a "cry out for help".

Firefighters are working around the clock to tackle a "devastating" fire across internationally protected heathland in the New Forest National Park, a habitat described as being "rarer than rainforests".

More than 120 firefighters were battling the blaze Monday, with crews set to work into the night once again after the fire broke out on Sunday. A van caught fire on the eastbound A31 near Ringwood and the flames spread to the protected heathland, which is home to a number of rare species, according to the New Forest National Park Authority.

Hampshire Fire and Rescue Service, supported by neighbouring services, initially dispatched 26 fire engines and four water carriers to the eastbound A31 after receiving 160 emergency calls reporting an HGV had caught fire.

The fire service said the blaze spread from the vehicle onto the central reservation before moving in a south-easterly direction into nearby heathland towards Backley Bottom, in what remains a "challenging rural location".

open image in gallery Firefighters tackle the fire at a major heathland blaze in the New Forest (Andrew Matthews/PA) ( PA Wire )

Gillie Molland, lead ranger for New Forest National Park Authority, said: “Globally, heathland is more rare than rainforest and takes decades to develop – the New Forest has the most extensive area of lowland heath remaining in Europe.

“It’s home to many nationally and internationally rare species – including all six of the UK’s reptiles, insects, plants and birds such as Dartford warblers and nightjar.

“The loss of rare species and biodiversity is devastating and upsets the delicate ecological balance of the Forest , as well as reducing grazing land available for commoners’ animals.

“Recovery is possible but it can take many years, with some features of mature heathland taking decades to return.

“Some rare heathland species may be lost or recover very slowly if local populations have been affected.”

On Monday afternoon, the fire service was using drones to monitor the spread of the fire – with 10 fire engines and 13 off-road vehicles still involved in the operation.

open image in gallery According to the New Forest National Park Authority, the land affected is protected heathland that is home to a number of rare species ( PA )

It said: “There are more than 120 firefighters on the scene battling the heat and arduous terrain, in order to prevent further fire spread.

“We are monitoring the fire, which is affecting a one square kilometre area of heathland off of the A31, with police drones.

“Currently, we have 10 fire engines and 13 off-road vehicles in attendance, and we plan to maintain this number of vehicles until at least midnight, although it is likely to be required for longer.

“We are grateful for the support from our neighbouring fire services, as well as others from across the country who are working alongside our firefighters with specialist vehicles and equipment, to resolve this incident.

“We know that the A31 is a crucial part of our road network, and in these summer months, many of you will want to go out to enjoy the New Forest, but we ask that you continue to avoid this area, with road closures still in place, whilst our teams work to save this part of our beautiful countryside.”

The fire service has warned people living nearby that it may need to lay hoses across their property as it draws water from a nearby lake.

open image in gallery A major heathland blaze in the New Forest near Ringwood in Hampshire on Sunday evening ( Forestry England/PA )

The statement added: “At present, there is no need for any properties to be evacuated. Should this situation change, affected households will be contacted directly.”

Sue Bassett, a worker at a Shell garage at services on the A31 near to where the fire started, said: “It’s almost scary with the rivers running low on water, it’s a challenge.”

Forestry England said in a statement that it was supporting the emergency services tackling the fire, which it said had spread to Bratley Wood and the surrounding area which includes a Canadian war memorial.

The statement continues: “Incidents like this can be devastating to all of the things that make the New Forest so special.

“Our team will be carefully assessing the impact once the incident is fully resolved.”

A Hampshire Constabulary spokeswoman said that 23 vehicles were left behind by motorists on Sunday, which were moved by police, with the owners asked to call 101 to be reunited with their vehicles.

open image in gallery A Hampshire Constabulary spokeswoman said that 23 vehicles were left behind by motorists on Sunday, which were moved by police, with the owners asked to call 101 to be reunited with their vehicles ( New Forest Police )

A National Highways spokesman said its contractors were on the scene, and added: “There is significant damage to the road surface, road safety barrier and boundary fencing as a result of the fire and a subsequent oil spillage from the burnt-out vehicle.

“All of which will require emergency repairs when safe to do so.

Meanwhile, Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident on Sunday as two large fires in woodland put a strain on resources with several wildfires having broken out in the UK during recent weeks.

News.title: Voices: Shabana Mahmood is getting it right on stopping the boats
News.content:

Ending irregular migration across the English Channel is a process, not an event. In fact, given its stubborn nature, it may never prove possible to completely “stop the boats” in a literal sense. It is a cat-and-mouse phenomenon, in which the authorities and the criminal gangs are constantly trying to outflank and outsmart each other with new techniques and tactics.

Hence the evolution of the inflatable craft deployed to move asylum seekers across the English Channel. The latest record is 230 people crammed into a “mega-dinghy” – 15 metres long (49ft), and buckling under the weight.

Only last month the highest such number detected in a single vessel was 165. The trend is happening as the French authorities have enjoyed more success intercepting dinghies launched off the usual beaches. So, the traffickers have developed a “taxi boat” system whereby a much larger craft travels from further away, running along the coast as its passengers wade in to begin their journeys. No doubt the French and British authorities will develop new countermeasures and pass fresh laws to try and get ahead of the gangs again; the cycle will go on.

Despite her efforts, which seem tireless, the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has been the subject of some harsh criticism about what’s been happening in the English Channel lately; but the truth is worth repeating – the trend is down and the gangs aren’t having it all their own way. In fact, this development is neither a matter for despair nor anger, though both are understandable. It is not the first time the delivery methods of the smugglers have been adapted.

At any rate, it proves, were proof needed, that this is a lucrative multimillion-pound trade, complete with its own supply chains, digital marketing and a dynamic business model. It is also characterised by what the Home Office rightly terms “the reckless and dangerous tactics employed by the criminal gangs facilitating these crossings, who continue to put lives at risk by cramming ever greater numbers of people onto unseaworthy vessels”.

The crucial point is to focus on the numbers of people arriving by all irregular routes. This is falling, as is lawful migration for that matter. The lurid headlines, spurious claims by extremist politicians and dramatic images are all misleading. The reality is that the numbers of people making the perilous cross-Channel journey is in fact down about 40 per cent on the same period last year. Irregular migration remains what it has always been – a small proportion of the total legal inwards flow of people. At around 40,000 a year, irregular arrivals (of whom most but not all are allowed to stay) were dwarfed by the scale of entirely legal post-Brexit numbers in the so-called Boriswave around 2023, a migration event which briefly spiked at close to one million.

It may be unfashionable to argue the point, but the government’s action on irregular migration is having effect, and the statistics bear that out. The Home Office claims that it has prevented 46,000 attempted crossings since Labour came to power, and more resources are being put into detection and prosecution of the gangs. They’ve also been disrupted by police raids across the continent. Illegal working and criminal front businesses in high streets have been targeted, and the backlog of asylum cases left behind by the Conservatives is coming down, speeding up deportations. Also down is the number of asylum hotels.

Evidently, there is no end to the work that needs to be done to bear down on dangerous irregular migration, and there probably always will be while poverty, persecution, crime and the simple desire for a better quality of life impels people to pay for a place on a highly unsafe boat. Changes in asylum procedures now being planned by the government may also act as a disincentive to the crossings – though gaining UK citizenship should surely also be cherished as an act of integration.

There’s no instant way to stop the boats. If there was, then any of the previous half dozen home secretaries who’ve been put under the same pressure from the public and the media would obviously have seized it. Nigel Farage has shown how deeply unserious he is by pretending the Royal Navy can rescue them and then drop them all off back in France.

Besides, not enough is ever made of the positive effects of migration, particularly on economic growth – and in a country with labour and skills shortages, a balance has to be struck. Ms Mahmood is trying to do just that.

Conservative podcaster Tucker Carlson claimed Monday that Israeli figures falsely told him Hunter Biden’s laptop contained graphic images of children.

Carlson, who once used the laptop story to criticize the Biden family while serving as a Fox News anchor, put to rest conspiracy theories about the laptop’s contents in a wide-ranging interview with the former president’s son – specifically the false allegations that the laptop contained abusive images of children.

“Can I just say one thing though, this is what I experienced during that time – the allegation that there was abusive minors proven on the laptop – that came from the Israelis,” Carlson told Biden.

While Biden’s laptop contained nude images of himself and women, there were no explicit images or videos of children. Allegations of such were the result of online conspiracy theories.

The “Tucker Carlson Show” host went further and claimed a man “connected to [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu” had given a producer on his former Fox News show the misinformation about Biden’s laptop directly.

open image in gallery Tucker Carlson accused Israelis of spreading misinformation about the contents on Hunter Biden’s laptop ( The Tucker Carlson Show )

“They were behind that,” Carlson insisted.

The Independent has asked the Israeli government for comment.

Carlson did not provide further details about the alleged exchange with the person connected to Netanyahu.

The Hunter Biden laptop controversy unfolded in 2020 after the New York Post published an article – weeks before the election – alleging emails from the laptop’s hard drive proved corruption among the Biden family. Trump’s former lawyer, Rudy Giuliani, reportedly provided the information to the news outlet.

The story became political drama because some social media platforms blocked access to the article, out of concern that it was Russian disinformation. Conservatives accused social media companies of censorship.

Among those who frequently discussed the laptop story was Carlson, who spent more than 2 hours of airtime on the topic within weeks of the New York Post article coming out, according to an estimate by Media Matters for America.

open image in gallery Carlson, who once campaigned for Trump, has recently broken from the MAGA movement and sought to unify disgruntled conservatives ( AFP/Getty )

Six years later, Carlson sat across from Biden, giving the former president’s son the space to deny accusations associated with the laptop controversy – including those of corruption between himself and his father before the 2020 presidential election.

“Either I’m incredibly, incredibly, incredibly good, in active addiction as a crack addict. Or it doesn’t exist. It truly, literally doesn’t exist. The entire narrative of the ‘Biden crime family’,’” Biden said of the corruption allegations.

Monday’s interview depicted the middle ground between Carlson and Biden, who historically are on opposite sides of the political spectrum under the second Trump administration.

Carlson, once a staunch Trump ally, has broken from the MAGA movement, citing frustrations with Trump’s foreign affairs – particularly related to Iran and Israel. Biden, who spent years at the center of conservative conspiracy theories, has recently embarked on a media campaign, being unabashedly honest about his drug addiction, political positions and more.

Hunter Biden's surprising praise for right-wing Republicans

Much of the interview between Carlson and Biden was about finding common ground.

Early on, Biden admitted there are a handful of conservative figures, such as Rep. Thomas Massie, former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene and podcaster Candace Owens – all of whom have been criticized by Trump – that he admires.

”I love Candace,” Biden said, calling the conservative podcaster “a really, really good person” who is “thoughtful” and “generous.”

While Biden admitted he has differing political views from many, including Carlson, he highlighted that he maintained human relationships with people anyway. At one point, Carlson and Biden joked about a letter of recommendation that Biden wrote for Carlson’s son to go to college – though Carlson’s son did not get accepted to the school.

open image in gallery Biden has recently embarked on a media campaign to share unfiltered opinions and facts about his life and his family as he seeks to find common ground with conservative figures ( Tucker Carlson / X )

Trump is not just 'a symptom of a disease'

Carlson, a newly established critic of Trump, discussed what he sees as the president’s shortcomings with Biden, who accused Trump of increasing the political divide in the United States.

“You know everybody says he’s just a symptom of the disease and the reality is I think he’s one of the most transformational individuals in our political history. All for ill,” Biden said.

He added: “I believe Trump is central to why this disease has gone from a local epidemic to a pandemic in the United States of America.”

Despite his statement, Biden insisted that he does not believe Trump is the source of all evil in the world – which Carlson agreed with.

Carlson admitted he is “implicated” in helping establish Trump’s credibility before the 2024 presidential election.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order that significantly altered the federal guidance for childhood vaccines and call for states to reconsider their requirements for school, upending decades of public health practice.

The move is aimed at pleasing the conspiracy theorists and anti-vaccine activists who embraced his political movement in the years following the Covid-19 pandemic.

Speaking Monday in the Oval Office, the president called the move an “ historic step in our mission to make America healthy again” before going on to regurgitate long-discredited theories about the non-existent link between vaccines and autism.

“My administration is recognizing gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases,” said Trump, who added that the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine that has been used since 1971 would once again be broken up into three separate vaccines despite the lack of any such separate vaccines on the current market.

Citing no evidence, he alleged that the MMR vaccine — long a boogeyman of anti-vaccine activists thanks to a long-discredited study by a disgraced British ex-physician–is dangerous.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump announced sweeping changes to the nation’s childhood vaccine recommendations by signing a new executive order ( AFP/Getty )

“So the MMR, we want to have separate, separate visits, separate times. The vaccine being broken into three separate single doses, and vaccines being administered in separate visits,” he said.

Trump also announced that vaccines for Covid-19, influenza and hepatitis B would no longer be recommended, despite warnings from health experts that not vaccinating against the liver disease could give rise to an epidemic of liver cancer in unvaccinated children infected with the virus.

“Parents can still choose to give their children all of the vaccinations if they wish. It's up to the parents. We're making recommendations that are strong, but it's up to the parents if they wish, and they will be covered by insurance,” he said.

“Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today. In those times, people were much healthier, and of course, the high rates of autism now observed did not exist. So, it is a reason for such epidemic rates of autism, and we're going to bring it back to much closer to where it was.”

There is no evidence linking vaccination rates to autism, yet Trump and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long pushed the theory that vaccines–particularly the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine–is liked to autism spectrum disorder.

This comes despite the fact that multiple studies have debunked the supposed link between childhood vaccinations and children developing autism spectrum disorder. Andrew Wakefield, the physician who published the original study, later had his medical license revoked and The Lancet, which published it, retracted the study.

open image in gallery Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Trump have both targeted vaccines as they talk about autism rates ( Reuters )

The executive order, entitled “Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations,” would divide childhood vaccinations into three distinct categories: immunizations recommended for all children such as the split-up MMR vaccine, diphtheria, tetanus and polio; vaccines for high-risk groups or populations, such as hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccines; and vaccines based on shared clinical decision-making, such as the Covid-19 vaccine and the flu shot.

The order also advises states to review the recommendations and “consider updating relevant laws and regulations that define” immunization requirements.

Zoe Gross, director of advocacy at the Autistic Self-Advocacy Network, said that splitting up the MMR vaccine is a longstanding anti-vaccine talking point since Wakefield’s study.

“So even if autism is not mentioned, that's a pretty big clue that that's what's on his mind and the minds of people influencing him and writing the EO, probably including RFK Jr,” Gross told The Independent.

Trump has for years suggested that vaccines should be administered in smaller doses. But Helen Tager-Flusberg, a professor emerita at Boston University and former president of the International Society for Autism Research, told The Independent that this could have massive consequences.

“It has huge consequences as you say, and it also has terrible consequences for the pediatricians who do their best to serve the public, they have such limited time with each family,” she told The Independent. “They're not going to be able to engage in the kinds of conversations that the president imagines is going to happen with shared responsibility for deciding whether to vaccinate or not. Pediatricians don't have the time for that.”

Trump has made looking into the increase in autism diagnoses a priority for his second administration. The president and Kennedy have suggested that autism is an “epidemic.” But the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention under Kennedy’s stewardship published its biennial study last year suggesting that the increase in autism diagnoses came because of improved screening.

“Differences in the prevalence of children identified with ASD across communities might be due to differences in availability of services for early detection and evaluation and diagnostic practices,” the 2025 report said.

Investigators have released the name of a Madison police officer who shot and killed a 38-year-old Black man in July in a shooting that sparked protests over how authorities treat people of color.

Kiel Baitinger-Peterson, a white officer with nearly 11 years' experience in law enforcement, fired the shots that killed Corey Ruiz on July 22, the Wisconsin Department of Justice's Division of Criminal Investigation said in a statement. Baitinger-Peterson was one of four officers who surrounded Ruiz, who was on a bike, in response to calls about someone who was checking out parked cars and an alleged burglary attempt, police said.

The shooting led to days of protests and calls from the Black community for Madison to address racial justice issues.

“He loved his daughter, he loved his family,” Ruiz’s mother, Elsa Ruiz, said after the shooting, adding that she never imagined she would be burying her son. “He did not deserve to be taken out like that. They took my baby from me.”

Baitinger-Peterson did not reply to an email seeking comment.

Civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who represents the victim’s family, has called for the officer to be charged ( Getty Images )

Jim Palmer, executive director of the Wisconsin Professional Police Association, which is the state’s largest police union and represents Madison officers, responded on behalf of Baitinger-Peterson.

“I am deeply concerned for the safety and privacy of him, his family, and the other officers involved,” Palmer said.

He said those concerns are being taken seriously and “appropriate precautions” are in place.

“I urge everyone to allow the investigation to proceed and to refrain from prejudging the officers or placing them and their families at further risk,” Palmer said.

Baitinger-Peterson and the other three officers who interacted with Ruiz that day have been placed on paid administrative leave while the state investigates the shooting.

There is no timeline for when the state Justice Department investigation will conclude. Dane County District Attorney Ismael Ozanne will review the findings before deciding whether to file charges against Baitinger-Peterson.

Civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who represents Ruiz's family, has called for the officer to be charged.

While bystanders captured the confrontation on video, there is no body camera footage because Madison police officers don't wear them.

The state Justice Department said two officers attempted to use a Taser on Ruiz but weren't successful. Ruiz “brandished a knife and injured” Baitinger-Peterson, it said. Law enforcement agencies haven't divulged the extent of the officer's injuries. They did release an image of a fixed-blade knife that was recovered at the scene.

The protests over the shooting led to several nearby community events being canceled or postponed.
