Sports.title: Jordan Nobbs ready to complete wishlist with Newcastle WSL dream
Sports.content:
Jordan Nobbs says winning promotion to the Women’s Super League with Newcastle would fulfil her ambition for a club from the north-east to be in the top tier.

Nobbs, who has 71 England caps, was born in Stockton-on-Tees and believes women’s football in the region would benefit immensely from top-flight representation. ­Newcastle finished sixth in WSL2 last term, 11 points behind the title ­winners, ­Birmingham, and nine points off the playoffs, but this ­summer they have made their hopes clear with high-calibre signings from the top division, including the striker ­Martha Thomas from Tottenham and the Liverpool duo Leanne Kiernan and Gemma Evans.

Nobbs is clear about the ­target for the new campaign. “It is ­promotion. I know we said it last season [too],” she said. “I’ve always said things don’t happen overnight, [but] that is our goal. You have to say it out loud.

“Looking back on last season, we had some really good performances but nine draws, that’s too many points [dropped]. It’s just about focusing on finding a way to win. We’ve just got to build on the good stuff from last season, I don’t think we’re far off it.

“[Winning promotion with Newcastle], I’ve always said it would be job done. To get a northern team promoted … as I heard from Newcastle I was like, that is exactly what I want to do. In the WSL, I’d ticked as much as I possibly could, so to get a north‑east team, which we all had to leave back in the day, promoted would be an achievement I would love.”

Nobbs began her career with Sunderland and broke into their team in the old top flight, but moved to ­Arsenal when the ­WSL was launched in 2011 and Sunderland’s application to join the breakaway division was rejected. That led to a successful team also including Nobbs’s future England teammates Lucy Bronze and Lucy Staniforth breaking up.

Sunderland did compete in the top tier between 2015 and 2018, but north-east representation in the WSL has been sparse, so Nobbs is pleased to see investment in recent years at Newcastle as well as their WSL2 rivals, who were taken over in June by Bay Collective.

“It’s been a long time coming, but it was something us ­northerners have always wanted,” Nobbs said. “We don’t want the north-east to fizzle out. We want to show the players that have come from there and developed there.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It’s definitely grown in the right ­direction now, which is what we wanted. But the big stepping stone would be getting into the WSL. That would be where we really put the north-east back on the map and I’d love to be a part of that.”

The 33-year-old has enjoyed her role in Tanya Oxtoby’s setup at Newcastle after joining them last July. “With Villa I played a lot of a deeper role and [now] I really love being back in my high position, scoring goals, assisting and [I’m] in my happy place. I feel like I found that little spark again [last season] that was nice.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille who value Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of signing Rodri from City, but they will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint‑Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30‑year‑old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester player Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of securing a deal for the 18-year-old midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post‑World Cup break. The 28-year-old has spent the past season and a half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa respectively, in the aftermath of a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former United head coach Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the United manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg  break down - with Ruben Amorim's AC Milan eyeing swoop for ex-Tottenham man
Sports.content:
Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, became a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the Newcastle deal

Villa director of football Damian Vidagany told German outlet Bild: 'Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans. We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.'

Villa lost 2-1 to Bayern in a pre-season friendly in Hong Kong over the weekend and Palhinha came on as a substitute.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup second-round draw: Chelsea host League One Luton, Tottenham handed London derby and Fulham welcome neighbours AFC Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Five-time winners Chelsea have been handed a home tie against League One side Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

New manager Xabi Alonso will begin the club's bid to win the competition for the first time since 2015 later this month.

Eleven Premier League clubs have entered at the second-round stage, with those involved in European competition this season receiving a bye to the third round.

Tottenham, who avoided relegation on the final day of last season, have also been handed a home draw and will face Championship side Charlton Athletic.

Fulham host League One outfit AFC Wimbledon, Brentford face a potentially tricky trip to Championship side Birmingham City, while Ipswich Town welcome Leicester City.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace hold clear-the-air talks with Dwight McNeil's girlfriend ahead of imminent transfer - after she hit out at club over failed January move
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace hold clear-the-air talks with Dwight McNeil's girlfriend ahead of imminent transfer - after she hit out at club over failed January move

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Crystal Palace co-owner and chairman Steve Parish has moved to clear the air with Dwight McNeil's partner ahead of the Everton player's imminent move to the club, according to reports.

McNeil and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deals. But this isn't the first time McNeil was primed for a move to the Eagles - having nearly joined them on Deadline Day in January.

The Everton winger, 26, had been widely expected to complete a move to the south London club after undergoing a medical ahead of a loan deal with a £20million obligation to buy.

The Eagles had submitted a deal sheet for McNeil's move, but they then failed to complete the relevant paperwork in time.

Everton sources said they fulfilled their part but Palace went quiet on finalising paperwork, effectively pulling out, and the transfer ran out of time.

And Megan Sharpley, girlfriend of McNeil, took to Instagram in a lengthy series of stories to hit out at what went on, including accusing Palace of messing with McNeil's mental health.

In a searing statement she described the 'cruelty' of the football world, saying that McNeil had been 'toyed with until the final minute' and subsequently 'left broken hearted with nothing but confusion'.

McNeil and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deals to Everton and Palace

In February, Dwight McNeil's girlfriend had hit out at the 'cruel' world of football after his deadline day move to Crystal Palace collapsed at the last moment

Sharpley also revealed that McNeil was left 'distressed' and in tears after the move fell through

Now, according to The Times, Parish has reached out to Sharpley to smooth things over so the transfer can move ahead. Both McNeil and Johnson spent Monday having medicals, with four-year deals for both players having been prepared.

As for the original statement, Sharpley said: 'Dwight, I've always been in awe of your job,' she began. 'The way you've committed most of your life to achieve what only the 0.1 per cent achieve.

'I know you love your job, the sport and you know how lucky you are to do what most people only dream of.

'We appreciate our lives, how fortunate we are, and the millions of football fans that keep the game alive and ultimately keep you in a job you adore. You've sacrificed a lot and most people don't have much of an idea of the difficult hardships you've suffered and dealt with in your personal life. And we crack on, that's who we are, we appreciate how blessed our lives are.

'But the world doesn't seem to accept that someone as fortunate as you is allowed to suffer hardships and feel sad. But you're a human, a beautiful incredible 26-year-old human being. And no matter about money or the success you've worked so hard to achieve, you are allowed to feel.

'Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you.'

Sharpley continued: 'To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster, and to be toyed with until the final minute.

'To have 4-and-a-half-years of your life promised to you, traveling, medicals, agreements made... promises made. To have prepared to move your entire life, our life 100 of miles away in the space of a few hours.

'For it to be torn away from you at the last second, with absolutely no explanation. Going from everything - to radio silence, no phone call, no communication and be left, broken hearted with nothing but confusion, has hurt more than I can say.

'I sit with you, knowing in my heart and deep down into my soul that you will bounce back from this. I am your biggest supporter. And I know you will overcome this with a fire in your belly and a motivation that no one can stop. I have already seen it tonight, even whilst you're facing the lowest point of your career.'

Sharpley reaffirmed her support for her partner and revealed he had been left in tears by the collapse of the transfer.

After the lengthy series of Instagram stories from Sharpley, McNeil also spoke on the matter

'We live in a world where everyone is aware how big of a problem mental health is,' she added. 'So in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money, that it's okay to mess and toy with their mental health and that's just 'part of the job'?

'No matter of money, we all deserve to be treated with respect, kindness and fairly. So I really question the industry tonight. I only hope there's more done in the future to protect people from situations like what I've witnessed tonight.

'Football is brutal and yes, it's the nature of the beast, but messing with human beings feelings and emotions shouldn't be acceptable. People only see one side on the media, you don't see the tears, the emotion and the distress I've seen tonight.

'Dwight, to the present, and the future. Every single thing happens for a reason, I will always believe what is meant for you will find you, and with your hard work and determination I'll never doubt only the best will come your way, and I'm so excited to see what you can achieve...

'So here's to carrying on being an Everton player. The support we've had from this club, especially during my illness, has meant a lot on our journey, so let's keep grinding, keep working and grafting for this badge. Let's keep going Dwight, show them who you are. I'm right by your side.'

The emotional post from Sharpley referenced her own illness when she was diagnosed with a large, serious tumour on her ovary and was forced to undergo urgent open surgery in December 2023. McNeil was praised for his unwavering support at the time.

The winger, who has played 128 times for Everton since joining from Burnley in 2022, also weighed in on the situation in regards to his failed move.

Sharing the final story from his partner, McNeil added: 'Whilst even now I'm still left in the dark. What I do know, and have been supported with, I am an Everton player. I will use this as motivation.

'I love you moo, I couldn't thank you enough for all of your love and support.'

Sports.title: City still want Bouaddi, West Ham interested in signing free agent Jamie Vardy as striker prepares to return to England - and Newcastle talks with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg break down: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City not giving up on Bouaddi

Manchester City are continuing discussions with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is keen to join City now rather than wait another season, which was Lille's preference, and the clubs are working towards agreement on a fee.

City still want another midfielder for when Rodri joins Barcelona with talks ongoing over a fee for the Spain captain.

Tottenham are continuing to monitor developments with Omar Marmoush and Savinho while Nottingham Forest want Tijjani Reijnders.

City and Southampton have agreed a season-long loan deal for Divin Mubama, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport. The 21-year-old forward spent last season on loan at Stoke City making 28 appearances in all competitions prior to damaging ankle ligaments in January.

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen to join Man City this summer

Chelsea line up LA Galaxy youngster

Chelsea are close to finalising a deal for 16-year-old LA Galaxy midfielder Vicente Garcia.

The deal is expected to be worth £2.25m plus add-ons and Garcia would join Chelsea when he turns 18 in 2028.

Hojbjerg talks with Toon break down

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, became a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Full story

The Denmark star is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested

Newcastle winger Murphy set for Kaiserslautern

Newcastle United defender Alex Murphy is on the verge of a season-long loan move to Kaiserslautern.

The Republic of Ireland U21 international, who can play centre-back and left-back, is having a medical ahead of joining the Bundesliga 2 club.

Liverpool's Morrison wanted by Groningen

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is attracting interest from FC Groningen among other clubs. The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international will be allowed to leave on loan.

Morrison, who started out at Manchester United, made his international debut in June against Guinea.

Tottenham winger off to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-hyeok is in talks to join Belgian side Westerlo. The 20-year-old, who joined Spurs in 2025, has had loan spells with QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry City since. The South Korea international is expected in Belgium today for his medical.

Hammers knocked back in Parrott pursuit

West Ham have had their opening bid for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott rejected.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Hammers made their opening offer of around £15million over the weekend but it is likely to take a Championship record fee of £17.5m to get their man. They are now formulating a new offer.

RB Leipzig have also contacted Alkmaar in recent days but the Hammers are further advanced.

West Ham are exploring a move for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson and have made an approach for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Tigers turned down in Vipotnik pursuit

Hull have had a bid rejected by Swansea for striker Zan Vipotnik.

The Premier League side's offer is understood to have fallen well short of Swansea's valuation of last season's Championship top scorer.

Palace keen on Khalaili

Crystal Palace's move for Union Saint-Gilloise right wing-back Anan Khalaili is progressing.

The Israeli international saw a £21million move to Inter Milan collapse over a medical issue but has had a number of clubs enquiring since.

Khalaili has had his medical ahead of signing a five-year deal.

Charles edges closer to Fulham switch

Shea Charles is undergoing his Fulham medical this morning ahead of his £30million transfer from Southampton.

Fulham have agreed to pay £27m with a further £3m in add-ons for the 22-year-old after Manchester City declined their option to activate matching rights.

Southampton retain a 20 per cent sell-on while Charles has agreed a five-year deal with an option for a further year.

McNeil and Johnson undergo medicals

Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deal to Everton and Crystal Palace.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

McNeil nearly joined Palace on Deadline Day in January, but the £20m move broke down due to paperwork not being submitted in time.

Johnson has struggled to settle at Palace since joining from Tottenham for £35m in January. Everton have also held an interest in Johnson in previous windows.

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

Hammers approach Vardy

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

Leicester have signed goalkeeper Franco Ravizzoli on a free transfer from Blackpool.

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Araujo completes medical

Ronald Araujo has completed his Liverpool medical ahead of completing a loan move from Barcelona.

The 27-year-old's signing is expected to be announced this afternoon.

The Uruguay defender's loan also includes an option to buy for around £47.1m.

Villa keep tabs on Endrick

Aston Villa are among the growing list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid. The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024.

Read the full story here.

Masuaku closes on Turkey move

Sunderland defender Arthur Masuaku is finalising finalise his move to Konyaspor, in Turkey. A deal between the clubs was agreed over the weekend.

Masuaku joined Sunderland last summer and spent the second half of last season on loan at Lens.

Belgian club Mechelen have agreed a deal to sign Sunderland defender Leo Hjelde.

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

Sunderland are interested in signing Alex Palmer from Ipswich

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side with Anthony Patterson expected to undergo a medical at Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee around £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Sunderland face Ipswich on the opening day of the season.

Ipswich are among the clubs interested in Newcastle's Nick Pope.

Villa on hunt for MacPhee replacement

Burnley set-piece coach Pal Fjelde is in talks to join Aston Villa.

Villa lost Austin MacPhee to Chelsea last month and 32-year-old Fjelde would be his replacement.

Fjelde joined Burnley last year and has also been his home country of Norway’s set piece coach since June 2022.

Austin MacPhee (right) left Villa to join Chelsea this summer

As a player he was a defender and midfielder and played for Norwegian clubs Viking and Bryne, before brief spells with Scottish Premiership side St Mirren and Faroe Islands Premier League side 07 Vestur.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero moves closer to sealing £34m move to Atletico Madrid with Diego Simeone on the cusp of seeing off Arsenal, Inter and Barcelona for Spurs captain
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero moves closer to sealing £34m move to Atletico Madrid with Diego Simeone on the cusp of seeing off Arsenal, Inter and Barcelona for Spurs captain

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Atletico Madrid are moving closer to agreement with Tottenham over a £34million deal to sign Cristian Romero.

The clubs are still understood to be a few million apart on the fixed aspect of the fee and bonus structure still need to be decided.

Atletico with the pull of coach Diego Simeone are understood to be Romero's preference over the other clubs that have been involved.

The Argentine has been the subject of interest from Inter Milan, Spurs' fierce rivals Arsenal and Barcelona.

Atletico are in the throes of selling defender Nahuel Molina to Roma, and he has arrived in Italy ahead of completing his £14.5m move, while Aston Villa are finalising a £16m deal for Atletico left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

Daily Mail Sport understands Premier League champions Arsenal had contacted the agents of the Spurs captain over what the deal would be, but Tottenham are unaware of the Gunners' interest and would be unwilling to consider selling 28-year-old Romero to their north London rivals.

Cristian Romero is moving closer to sealing a £34m move to Spanish side Atletico Madrid

Daily Mail Sport understands the pull of Diego Simeone has seen Atletico lead the race

Inter have agreed a £34m fee with Spurs but have not agreed on personal terms.

The central defender is free to leave Spurs for the right price after the club bolstered their defensive ranks earlier in the transfer window.

The additions of Marcos Senesi on a free transfer and John Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52m mean Roberto de Zerbi is well stocked.

But the idea of selling the club captain to their arch rivals Arsenal would be deemed completely unacceptable by Spurs fans and the club would not countenance it.

Arsenal will be without William Saliba, who suffered a back injury at the World Cup, for months and are considering reinforcements at the back.

But Romero appears destined for a move away from the Premier League having spent the last five years at Tottenham after joining from Atalanta.

He was at the heart of Lionel Scaloni's defence for the Argentina side who beat England in the World Cup semi-final before suffering a 1-0 defeat by Spain in the final last month.

Romero has come close to leaving Spurs before, notably after Ange Postecoglou departed.

He suffered a knee injury during the club's dramatic run-in at the end of last season in which they fought off relegation.

Romero left the pitch in tears during a 1-0 defeat by Sunderland but De Zerbi managed to keep Spurs up without his captain, who recovered in time to play for Argentina.

He came under fire for celebrating in the faces of opposition players during the World Cup and also snubbed Donald Trump after the final defeat, ignoring the US President after collecting his runners-up medal.

After receiving his medal around his neck from Infantino, Romero snubbed Trump by not shaking his hand, instead he walked straight past him to join his team-mates.

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle
Sports.content:
Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan with an option to buy.

The 27-year-old defender flew to Merseyside on Sunday afternoon and has since completed his medical.

The Reds have the option to purchase the Uruguay international at the end of the campaign for £47million.

'I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy,' Araujo said.

'I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my teammates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

'I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

'As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time.'

Liverpool have confirmed the loan signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo

The Uruguayan defender has joined the Anfield club on a season long loan

Andoni Iraola has sought to address his defensive crisis with a number of centre halves injured

Araujo wanted to leave Barca, where he has spent eight years, after talks with coach Hansi Flick made it apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts. He believes he is likely to play more minutes under Reds' new boss Andoni Iraola.

The centre-back gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at the heart of the backline and at right-back.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre-back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, and new signing Jeremy Jacquet is yet to feature this summer.

It leaves captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully fit senior centre-back with their Premier League opener away at Newcastle less than two weeks away.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2020.

He has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona but finds himself down the pecking order in Spain, with the likes of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin ahead of him.

Sports.title: Derby's Saudi takeover COLLAPSES: Championship club now 'off the market' after Turki Alalshikh's group dramatically pulled out despite Football Regulator and EFL approval
Sports.content:
Boxing billionaire Turki Alalshikh has stunned Derby County by pulling out of an investment deal at the 11th hour.

At the end of last week, the deal looked certain to go through after the potential involvement of Alalshikh – a senior Saudi official with an estimated wealth of £2billion – was signed off by English football authorities.

Yet on Monday afternoon Alalshikh sensationally backed away, citing the length of time taken by the football regular to ratify the deal.

On his X account, Alalshikh wrote: ‘I would like to thank everyone at Derby County Football Club, and everyone involved in this process for all their hard work over the past few months.

‘We understood that the IFR (independent football regulator) process takes time and fully respect the importance of that, but unfortunately with the season already started, it would leave us with no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead.

‘After careful consideration, we don't feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future. I personally wish the team and club every success for the season ahead.’

Turki Alalshikh's Lion Sport group has pulled out of taking over Derby County Football Club

A takeover had been approved by the EFL and Football Regulator but will no longer happen

While Alalshikh’s statement suggested talks could be re-opened, Derby’s reaction was far more blunt.

It read: ‘The club can confirm discussions with Lion Sport to buy a controlling interest in Derby County will no longer proceed.

‘The purchase process had been sanctioned by both the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL, notification of which the club received last week.

‘However, today the club received notice that Lion Sport no longer wanted to continue with the purchase.

'For the benefit of any doubt, the club is now off the market and will continue to operate under the loyal, committed and unwavering support of Clowes Developments.’

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace at the High Court following a controversial banner displayed at Selhurst Park last season.

The Nottingham Forest owner on Monday lodged a claim for defamation against his club’s Premier League rivals that dates back to the 1-1 draw between the clubs last August.

The banner depicting Marinakis holding a gun to the head of Forest player Morgan Gibbs-White and carried the words ‘Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.’ Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to such allegations.

Palace were charged by the Football Association last November and while the banner was not specified as the reason for the charge, there are strict rules regarding messaging containing defamatory, political and offensive slogans.

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago, due to UEFA’s rules regarding multi-club ownership. Forest benefited from that decision and were promoted into the Europa League.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is pursuing a defamation case against Crystal Palace

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago

The Gibbs-White/Marinakis banner appeared while that row was still fresh in the clubs’ minds.

Then Oliver Glasner, who led Palace to three trophies before departing at the end of last season, was promptly hired by Forest on a three-year deal. Palace host Forest in the Premier League on October 10.

‘This claim has been issued at Court shortly before the expiry of the one-year limitation period in defamation which could indicate that prior efforts to resolve the dispute have been unsuccessful,’ said Jamie Hurworth, a defamation specialist for law firm Payne Hicks Beach.

‘One of the first steps will be for the Court to determine how a reasonable reader would have interpreted the allegations on the banner which included an image of a gun being held to a player’s head, and whether that allegation is defamatory.

‘There will also be a potentially novel legal issue to address given the banner was held up by Crystal Palace fans, rather than perhaps any allegations being made by or on behalf of the club itself.’

Crystal Palace have declined to comment.

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish
Sports.content:
Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has been desperate for reinforcements in central defence following a difficult injury-hit pre-season - and now Ronald Araujo has arrived from Barcelona

View 3 Images Ronald Araujo has joined Liverpool on loan from Barcelona (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool have completed the signing of Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan deal - which could become a permanent switch if the Reds active the £47.14million option to buy.

‌



The 27-year-old Uruguay international moves from the Nou Camp in one of the more surprising switches of the summer so far. Last term he was still serving as the skipper for the Spanish giants, but has now opted for a move away after seeing his minutes decline.

‌



He is the second defender to arrive at Anfield this summer after Jeremy Jacquet completed his switch from Rennes, further bolstering a backline that already has Virgil van Dijk as its leader. Joe Gomez has been injured in pre-season and has struggled to remain consistently fit.

‌



Araujo has chosen the No 33 shirt - which was last worn a decade ago by Jordon Ibe. The centre-half becomes the fourth Uruguayan to play for the Reds - following in the footsteps of Darwin Nunez, Sebastian Coates and Luis Suarez.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club READ MORE :

Suarez remains one of the greatest Liverpool players of the Premier League era and was quick to reach out to his compatriot, congratulating him on his switch to Anfield.

‌



“We loved watching the English Premier League and everyone in Uruguay gets up early in the morning to catch the games," Araujo told the club's website.

“Of course as a kid I used to watch Luis playing all those fantastic games for Liverpool. We all know what he achieved, the history that he made within this club during his time here. So it’s fantastic.

“From minute one, I’ve been sort of asked about that kind of comparison since I’ve arrived here. I get on really well with him, we’re quite close. Just a few minutes ago I got a good luck message from him saying all the best, you’ve joined a great club and all the very best for your time here.”

‌



View 3 Images Luis Suarez reached out to Ronald Araujo (Image: Getty Images)

Araujo comes into a Liverpool side that have endured a difficult pre-season. On Sunday they squandered a two-goal lead for the second time in a matter of weeks, losing to Monaco in Andoni Iraola's first game at Anfield.

The Reds finished the friendly with youngster Luke Chambers and midfielder Wataru Endo as the centre-back pairing, underlining the need for new arrivals, with £55m signing Jacquet still getting fit.

‌



Iraola was critical post-match and admitted that the team were not capable of sustaining their level for the 90 minutes, raising questions over whether they can implement his philosophy.

"We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes," he said. "Right now we probably don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has been desperate for new signings (Image: Ian Horrocks, Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

‌



"We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game."

Iraola has made it clear that Liverpool need to make signings in the summer transfer window if they are to turn around their disappointing second campaign under Arne Slot. The Reds remain in the market for a world-class attacker, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola the number one target.

It has been a summer of upheaval for Liverpool, who changed manager before Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards decided to quit, piling more pressure onto sporting director Richard Hughes. Meanwhile, FSG have been busy negotiating a 30 per cent investment from a consortium which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup second round draw in full as Chelsea, Newcastle and Leeds discover opponents
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup second round draw in full as Chelsea, Newcastle and Leeds discover opponents

The draw for the second round of the Carabao Cup has been completed, with 11 Premier League sides, including Chelsea, Newcastle and Leeds, entering the competition

View Image The second round of the Carabao Cup will take place later in August (Image: Getty)

Sports.title: What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture
Sports.content:
What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture

Marcus Rashford's future remains the topic of plenty of speculation as he returns to Manchester United after spending last season out on loan

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has rejoined his Manchester United team-mates after a spell out on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

A few months ago, the idea of Marcus Rashford returning to the fold at Manchester United looked far-fetched. Strange things can happen in football, though, and the England international's Old Trafford comeback is right up there

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and looked poised for a permanent move to Spotify Camp Nou. However, the Catalan club let their £26m option expire.

‌



For as long as Ruben Amorim was in the United dugout, a return for the forward looked impossible. However, the arrival of Michael Carrick - a former team-mate of Rashford - has altered the picture.

‌



England's run to the World Cup semi-finals meant a later return for the 28-year-old than for some of his colleagues. Now, though, Rashford's future is very much at the forefront of discussions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Man Utd return

Following United's 1-1 draw with PSG on Saturday, Carrick confirmed that Rashford has returned as part of his first team group, alongside Kobbie Mainoo.

‌



“We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together," United's manager said. “Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

View 3 Images Rashford has joined the United camp in Dublin (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Get Man United's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Manchester United have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, i nspired by the club's heritage and featuring a classic polo collar with iconic adidas details.

‌



As reported by the MEN, the England pair joined Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt, Karl Darlow, JJ Gabriel and Tynan Thompson on a private jet to Dublin. Some of those players could play a part in United's midweek friendly with Leeds, with Martinez also expected in Dublin.

Transfer stance

Rashford is not interested in moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia, thereby limiting his options. He would only join a European side who can offer him Champions League football. There are only so many clubs capable of meeting the forward's demands and one of them, Barcelona, are already out of the running barring a big U-turn.

The fee might not be a huge obstacle, with the MEN suggesting £25m - a little less than the provisional sum agreed with Barca - potentially enough to do it. However, those close to Rashford are said to have suggested United are no longer desperate to sell.

‌



Rashford will be with the rest of the squad for United's final two pre-season friendlies, against Leeds on Wednesday and AC Milan on Saturday, and is expected to be around for the Premier League opener away at Hull on August 22.

View 3 Images Barcelona allowed their £26m transfer option to expire (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer/Getty Images)

Telling gesture

While some fans are prepared to wait and see when it comes to Rashford's future, others have been looking for clues wherever they can find them. One such clue comes on the squad number front, where the forward is set to wear No. 14 next term.

Article continues below

United have already given Matheus Cunha the No. 10 previously worn by the England international and there are no indications it will revert back to its previous owner. Rashford wore No. 14 at Barcelona, though, and the choice can be read as an indication that the club and Carrick consider him part of their plans.

The No. 14 shirt was vacant for United last season. The number was not reused when Christian Eriksen left the club, while previous holders include Jesse Lingard and Javier Hernandez.

Sports.title: Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title
Sports.content:
Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title

Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month

View Image Oleksandr Khyzhniak is a rising star

Oleksandr Khyzhniak, who many believe can follow in mentor Oleksandr Usyk's footsteps, will fight for his first title later this month.

‌



Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month. He will now headline the second boxing event put on by Usyk's promotional company Usyk 17 Promotions on August 22.

‌



The event, to be held at !FESTrepublic in Lviv, will be dedicated to the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence and Usyk said: “Thirty-five years of independent development is actually not a very long time. Twelve of those years have been lived under conditions of war. But look at how much we have already managed to achieve despite everything.

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

"Look at the incredible athletes we have — not only boxers, but Olympic champions and Paralympians. Artists, musicians, scientists. We want to remember our greatest victories, honour those who fought and continue to fight for our freedom, and show the entire world that Ukraine has been, is and will remain a country of strong, talented and unbreakable people.”

Sergey Lapin, who is guiding Khyzhniak in his professional career, added:“A first title fight is both a natural and an important step in Oleksandr’s professional career. He is ready for a new level of competition and to prove his quality in championship fights. For Usyk 17 Promotions, it is especially important that this stage of his journey begins in Ukraine — at our second boxing event in Lviv. Our goal is to build a platform in Ukraine where the strongest boxers can develop, win titles and confidently progress to the international level.”

Article continues below

The fight night's co-main event will feature Pavlo Illiusha while the undercard will include nine Usyk 17 Promotions boxers in Maksym Rudyk, Maksym Zymenko, Dmytro Lovchynskyi, Elvin Aliiev, Bohdan Tolmachov, Mykola Laktionov, Jamal Kuliev, Aider Abduraimov and Matvii Razhba.

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment

Billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is involved in a consortium looking to buy into Liverpool with a statement anticipated soon

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium looking to take a stake in Liverpool (Image: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue)

Jeff Bezos is preparing to take a stake in Liverpool. The billionaire is part of a consortium which also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

‌



Amazon founder Bezos has been one of the richest men in the world for a number of years. He sat fourth on the most recent Forbes billionaires list, with his fortune now estimated to sit at $280bn (just under £208m).

‌



According to Sky News, an official announcement over the deal could arrive this week. The consortium is reportedly led by Amit Bhatia, the former QPR chairman and son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

‌



An investment in Liverpool would just be the latest step for the super-rich businessman, who boasts a huge property empire along with wife Lauren Sanchez. Here, we've taken a deeper dive into what that looks like.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Reports from Realtor.com estimates Bezos' property empire to be worth some $500m (£370m) on its own. The star of the show is his primary home on Indian Creek Island in Florida, an exclusive island with just 34 residences - unsurprisingly belonging to the super-rich.

Three of those belong to Bezos, including a $90m property bought in 2024. While the size of the home means he might not have neighbours in the same sense as you or I, other residents of Indian Creek Island include NFL legend Tom Brady and first daughter Ivanka Trump.

Previously, Bezos lived in Seattle with his former wife Mackenzie Scott and still owns a number of properties in the area. He made a tidy profit on one of his homes in the small town of Hunts Point, buying for $37.5m in 2019 and selling for $63m four years later, per the Puget Sound Business Journal.

‌



View 3 Images Bezos owns property on the exclusive Indian Creek Island (Image: Google Maps)

Learn more £85 LFC Shop Buy Now on LFC Shop Product Description Liverpool FC have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27, inspired by iconic adidas strip worn during the club's 1989/90 title-winning campaign.

The 62-year-old established Amazon in Washington State in the 90s and also purchased properties in the Seattle suburb of Medina. He isn't the only Hunts Point resident with ties to Seattle, with former Seattle Seahawks NFL coach Pete Carroll among the others to buy property there.

‌



Over the last decade, Bezos has also picked up properties in Washington DC and New York City, each worth more than $15m, and a ranch in West Texas. That's nothing compared to his $78m Hawaii property, though, which is believed to include a 4,500-square-foot main house.

However, it's a $165m Beverly Hills home which tops the lot. The California property was developed by movie mogul Jack Warner and previously belonged to record executive David Geffen, with Architectural Digest reporting that it includes tennis courts and its own nine-hole golf course.

View 3 Images Bezos and wife Lauren Sanchez also own properties in Texas and California worth millions of dollars (Image: Google Maps)

‌



It isn't just about property for Bezos either. The bulk of his wealth still comes from his Amazon stake, despite him selling shares worth a reported $13.5bn in 2023, while he has a private investment firm - Bezos Expeditions - which manages his other investments.

These investments include stakes in Uber and Airbnb, among other ventures, with the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute estimating Bezos investments has approximately $107.8bn of assets. The billionaire also took charge of the Washington Post more than a decade ago in a deal worth $250m.

Another significant project of Bezos is Blue Origin, the space technology company he established in 2000. The company, which produces rockets and engines, was described in 2023 by CEO Bob Smith as having "hundreds of millions in revenue as well as billions of dollars in orders".

Article continues below

While Bezos is one of the richest individuals in the world, fellow consortium member Saverin is reportedly worth nearly $24bn himself. The 44-year-old is a co-founder of venture capital firm B Capital and is now based in Singapore.

Sky News reports that the bid values Liverpool at around $6bn. The club was valued at $4.5bn when Dynasty Equity took a small stake in 2023, though the Bezos-Saverin consortium could take a stake of more than 30 per cent.

Sports.title: Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting
Sports.content:
Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting

Arsenal are firm admirers of Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, and they are looking at potentially signing the ex-Manchester City star after missing out on Vinicius Junior

View Image Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez will reportedly push to leave Atletico Madrid this summer, with Arsenal keen on landing the Argentinian. It's claimed, though, the 26-year-old will reiterate his desire to join Barcelona, having previously said it would be his dream to move to the Nou Camp.

‌



Alvarez is due to return for pre-season training this week, with Arsenal keeping a close eye on developments. Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has been a long-term admirer of the former Manchester City forward, who has racked up 49 goals and 17 assists in 106 appearances for Atletico.

‌



However, the La Liga giants club have stood firm with their stance that Alvarez is not for sale, even after his controversial comments during the World Cup.

‌



Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move READ MORE :

Arsenal outline Gabriel Martinelli transfer stance as new club eyes Gabriel Jesus READ MORE :

"I spoke with people at the club, with those I had to speak with and the best thing for everyone is ‌a transfer and I want to fulfil my dream," he said.

"It's not the time to talk about this, but I also can't hide ⁠it. I try to ⁠be an honest person."

‌



Alvarez has been the subject of bids from both Barcelona and Real Madrid, yet his manager Diego Simeone maintains that nothing has shifted and that Atletico have no plans to sanction his exit.

"The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel Gil Marin [Atletico's CEO] explained very well," Simeone said. "We are very happy with Julian, from a sporting perspective, we're very happy to have a player like Julian, and we'll help him continue to grow and improve."

Ahead of his return to Atleti, Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Alvarez will once again make his desire to join Barcelona abundantly clear, despite having already expressed this both privately and publicly, as the saga enters its 'decisive phase'.

‌



This would strongly suggest that Arsenal would be out of the running for his signature should the Spanish giants alter their position.

Atleti have remained resolute thus far, though the Argentine continues to harbour hopes that the club might eventually have a change of heart. The publication warns that 'a major crisis could erupt' between Atleti and the Argentine.

‌



It is further reported that should Atletico ease their stance and agree to open talks, Barcelona 'will submit a new offer'.

Nevertheless, Gil Marin has left no doubt that the club will not be entertaining any offers for their prized asset this summer.

"It wasn't the right day to make such statements; it was a day for [Lionel] Messi and the Argentine national team, not Julian," he previously told EFE about Alvarez's comments regarding his desire to leave.

Article continues below

"Julian has a dream [to sign elsewhere], but we Atletico fans have dreams, too. It is true that he has spoken to us, but it is also true that he is fully aware of our position because we have been very clear. Atleti do not want to transfer him. He is a great player and we are very proud that he plays for us."

Liverpool set to announce new signing but team-mate 'already wants him back' after goodbyes

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
