Argentina country risk climbed to 451 basis points on Friday, 7 August 2026, according to JP Morgan’s EMBI index.

What Happened to Argentina Country Risk

Argentina country risk rose 13 points to 451 basis points on Friday, 7 August 2026.

That was a daily increase of about 3%, following 446 basis points on Thursday.

The move tracked falls in Argentine sovereign dollar bonds amid Wall Street weakness.

One outlet also linked the rise to tensions in the Middle East.

Over five days, the indicator gained only a few percent, not 13%.

The JP Morgan EMBI is the benchmark for this risk measure.

Reading the Number

A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so 451 basis points equals 4.51%.

Country risk, or riesgo pais, shows the extra yield investors demand over US Treasuries.

Higher risk means investors see more chance of default or instability.

The EMBI index tracks dollar bonds issued by emerging market governments.

For Argentina, 451 basis points is high but below past crisis levels.

You can think of it as a premium for lending to Argentina.

What Drove the Move

The main driver was weakness in Argentine sovereign dollar bonds, reports show.

Falls on Wall Street also pressured the indicator on Friday.

One outlet mentioned Middle East tensions as a secondary factor.

Reuters said the peso stayed stable while risk hovered near 451 basis points.

There is no verified source linking the move to doubts over the FX plan.

Bond prices and market expectations for the exchange rate are connected.

The Peso and the Central Bank

The peso traded around 1,499.50 per dollar in the wholesale market on Monday.

Retail rates were near 1,515, close to the historic weak area of 1,500.

The BCRA managed liquidity to support the exchange-rate framework.

Gross reserves fell to USD 48.835 billion after an IMF payment of USD 852 million.

Before that payment, reserves were about USD 49.642 billion.

The central bank moderated reserve purchases to keep the peso stable.

Milei’s Balancing Act

President Javier Milei‘s government aims to keep the dollar below ARS 1,500.

Economy Minister Luis Caputo oversees the FX plan, though no quote is verified.

Market commentary says bond prices imply a higher future exchange rate.

The government balances reserve needs with market pressures.

Reserve purchases support the peso but reduce dollar buffers.

The IMF payment shows Argentina meeting its obligations.

What Investors Should Watch

Watch the EMBI index for daily moves above 460 basis points.

Track bond prices in the OTC market for recovery signs.

Monitor BCRA reserve levels after the IMF payment.

Keep an eye on the peso’s wholesale rate near 1,500.

Any Wall Street selloff could push risk higher again.

Middle East tensions remain a wildcard for global markets.

Why Country Risk Matters for Argentina

High country risk keeps Argentina locked out of cheap borrowing. Lenders demand steep premiums, so debt costs stay heavy.

This raises funding costs for the government and firms. It also pressures the peso and complicates reserve building.

A lower risk score would reopen global credit markets. That would ease financing and support economic stability.

Steady reserves and credible FX policy are key to reducing risk. Calmer global markets also help bring it down.

The Road Ahead

Argentina’s risk gauge recently hovered near 451 basis points. That level reflects persistent investor caution.

Bond prices fell on Wall Street weakness, pushing risk higher. Such moves show how external factors can hurt.

To improve, the country needs consistent reserve gains. A clear exchange-rate plan would also boost confidence.

Progress will be gradual, not dramatic. Sustained policy discipline and global calm could slowly lower the spread.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Argentina country risk?

Argentina country risk is the extra yield investors demand to hold Argentine bonds over US Treasuries, measured by JP Morgan’s EMBI index.

Why did country risk rise to 451 basis points?

It rose due to weakness in Argentine sovereign dollar bonds and falls on Wall Street, with some influence from Middle East tensions.

What does 451 basis points mean in plain terms?

It means investors require a 4.51% higher yield on Argentine bonds compared to US government bonds, reflecting perceived risk.

How did the peso perform during the risk rise?

The peso stayed stable, trading around 1,499.50 per dollar in the wholesale market, with the BCRA managing liquidity.

Sources: JP Morgan EMBI; Infobae; Reuters; Argentine market reports.

World.title: São Paulo Governor Poll Shows Tarcisio Ahead
World.content:
Brazil · Politics

Key Facts — Pollster Ideia; Commissioner: ACSP (Sao Paulo Commercial Association).

— Field dates 5-8 August 2026; 1,800 voters by telephone.

— Margin of error 2.3 percentage points; TSE registration SP-04956/2026.

— First round Tarcisio 50.6%, Haddad 33.6%, Vera Lucia 2.6%.

— Runoff Tarcisio 53.4%, Haddad 37.0%, blank/null 4.0%, undecided 5.6%.

— Tarcisio is the sitting governor running for re-election.

— Haddad is the former finance minister and PT candidate for governor.

A new Ideia/ACSP poll puts Governor Tarcisio de Freitas far ahead of Fernando Haddad in Sao Paulo’s 2026 race.

Sao Paulo’s Octavio Frias bridge; the state elects its governor in 2026. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0)

A fresh Sao Paulo governor poll shows Tarcisio de Freitas leading with 50.6% support. Fernando Haddad trails at 33.6% in the first round, per Ideia for ACSP.

What the Poll Found

The Ideia poll, commissioned by ACSP, tested the Sao Paulo governor race. Tarcisio de Freitas (Republicanos) leads with 50.6% of voter intentions.

Fernando Haddad (PT) gets 33.6%, while Vera Lucia (PSTU) has 2.6%. The poll ran from 5 to 8 August 2026.

It surveyed 1,800 voters by telephone, with a margin of error of 2.3 points. The TSE registration number is SP-04956/2026.

O Globo rounded these numbers to 51% for Tarcisio and 34% for Haddad. The exact figures come from Gazeta do Povo’s breakdown.

Inside the Sao Paulo Governor Poll

This is a state-level poll, not a presidential one, for the 2026 election. Ideia conducted it, and ACSP commissioned the survey.

The poll tested only the governor race, with Tarcisio as the incumbent. Haddad appears as the PT candidate for governor.

Fieldwork happened over four days in early August 2026. The sample includes 1,800 voters across Sao Paulo state.

The margin of error is 2.3 percentage points, meaning results could vary slightly. The TSE registration ensures transparency and compliance.

Tarcisio’s Commanding Lead

Tarcisio de Freitas, the sitting governor, holds a strong 50.6% in the first round. That is nearly 17 points ahead of Haddad.

His lead suggests broad support for his re-election bid. The Republicanos candidate has a clear path to victory.

In a runoff scenario, Tarcisio still leads with 53.4% against Haddad. This shows his support is solid even in a head-to-head.

The blank/null vote is 4.0%, and undecided voters are 5.6%. Tarcisio’s numbers indicate he is the favorite.

Haddad’s Uphill Climb

Fernando Haddad, the former finance minister, trails with 33.6% in the first round. He left the Finance Ministry in March 2026 after serving since January 2023.

Haddad’s PT candidacy faces an uphill battle against the incumbent. His support is significant but far behind Tarcisio.

In the runoff, Haddad gets 37.0%, still 16 points behind Tarcisio. The gap shows he struggles to close the distance.

He needs to win over undecided and blank voters to improve. But the current poll suggests a tough path to victory.

How the Runoff Scenario Looks

If no candidate wins a majority, a runoff would occur between the top two. Tarcisio would face Haddad in that second round.

The poll shows Tarcisio winning the runoff with 53.4% support. Haddad gets 37.0%, with 4.0% blank or null votes.

Undecided voters make up 5.6% in this scenario. These voters could shift the outcome, but Tarcisio’s lead is large.

In a runoff, Tarcisio leads 53.4% to Haddad’s 37.0%. That gap points to a comfortable win.

Why This Race Matters Beyond Sao Paulo

Sao Paulo is Brazil’s richest state, so its governor race has national impact. A Tarcisio win could boost Republicanos’ influence.

Haddad’s performance reflects PT’s strength in a key state. This poll could shape national strategies for 2026.

Tarcisio is seen as a potential presidential candidate for the future. A strong re-election win would solidify his standing.

The poll’s results may influence Lula’s political calculations. But this survey only covers the state race, not the presidency.

What It Signals for 2026 in Brazil

Sao Paulo is Brazil’s richest state and biggest electoral prize. The race is a proxy fight between the Bolsonaro-aligned right and Lula’s PT.

A strong Tarcisio could lift his national profile. The poll shows him at 50.6% versus Haddad’s 33.6% in the first round.

The runoff widens the gap to 53.4% against 37.0%. This early lead suggests momentum for the incumbent governor.

But it is one poll from 1,800 voters with a 2.3 margin. Field dates were 5-8 Aug 2026, so caution is wise.

What to Watch Next

Watch for more polls to confirm or challenge this lead. Haddad’s PT base could mobilize as the campaign heats up.

Tarcisio’s performance may shape his presidential ambitions for 2026. A decisive win would boost his national standing.

The 2.6% for Vera Lucia shows minor third-party impact. Blank and don’t know votes total 9.6% in the runoff.

Keep an eye on TSE filings for full candidate lists. The race remains fluid with months to go.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the margin of error in this poll?

The margin of error is 2.3 percentage points. This means the actual support could be 2.3 points higher or lower than reported.

Who is Tarcisio de Freitas?

He is the current governor of Sao Paulo, running for re-election. He belongs to the Republicanos party.

Who is Fernando Haddad?

He is the former finance minister of Brazil, serving from January 2023 to March 2026. He is the PT candidate for governor.

What does TSE registration mean?

TSE is Brazil’s electoral court, which registers polls for transparency. Registration number SP-04956/2026 confirms the poll’s official status.

Sources: Ideia/ACSP poll; O Globo; Gazeta do Povo; Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

World.title: Chile Security Reform Signed: What Kast’s Plan Means
World.content:
Chile · Politics

Key Facts President José Antonio Kast signed the constitutional reform on Monday, August 10, 2026.

The reform makes public security a constitutional duty of the State.

It creates a new state of exception for grave alterations to public security.

A new registry of criminal organizations will be established.

Separate prison regimes will apply for organized crime and terrorism convictions.

The reform enables seizure and destruction of illicit assets.

The government requested ‘urgencia suma’ for a fast 2-3 month Senate timetable.

President José Antonio Kast signed a constitutional reform on public security Monday, sending it to Congress with fast-track urgency.

Carabineros in formation; the reform would widen the state’s security powers. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0)

Chile security reform took a major step forward on Monday, August 10, 2026. When President José Antonio Kast signed a constitutional reform on public security.

The government sent the bill to Congress with ‘urgencia suma’ (highest urgency), seeking approval within two to three months.

What Kast Signed

President José Antonio Kast signed the constitutional reform at La Moneda on Monday. The bill now heads to the Senate for its first legislative review.

This reform sits within a wider package of more than 30 bills. Kast said these measures will ‘change the way we confront organized crime in Chile.’

The constitutional change requires a 4/7 quorum in both chambers. That means the government must negotiate with opposition parties to pass it.

The signing marks a key step in Kast’s security agenda. It turns public security into a constitutional duty of the State.

Inside the Chile Security Reform

Chile security reform makes public security a constitutional duty of the State. This change gives the government a stronger legal basis for its policies.

The reform creates a registry of criminal organizations. This database will help authorities track and target gang activity.

It also establishes separate prison regimes for organized crime and terrorism convictions. These tougher conditions aim to disrupt criminal operations from inside.

The bill enables seizure and destruction of illicit assets. This targets the financial power of criminal groups.

The New State of Exception

The reform creates a new constitutional state of exception for grave alterations to public security. This allows the armed forces to be deployed in affected zones.

A state of exception is a special legal status during emergencies. It grants temporary powers to authorities to restore order.

This mechanism goes beyond normal police powers. It lets the military support security operations in areas with serious criminal conduct.

The government says this tool is essential for tackling organized crime. Critics worry about potential military overreach in civilian matters.

How It Moves Through the Senate

The reform enters Congress through the Senate, as confirmed by government sources. The minister aims for an ‘exprés’ two-to-three-month timetable.

The government requested ‘urgencia suma’ to fast-track the bill. This procedural tool forces Congress to prioritize the reform.

The Senate must approve the reform with a 4/7 quorum. Then the Chamber of Deputies will review it.

Any changes by the second chamber would send the bill back. That could delay the tight schedule the government wants.

The Politics and the Pushback

The government holds 76 of 155 deputies and 26 of 50 senators. That is not a majority, so it needs opposition votes.

Opposition parties PS, PPD, FA, PC, DC and Liberal are seeking to close ranks against Kast. FA and PC take the hardest line.

Constanza Martínez said her sector has a minority in both chambers. She says they must build ‘social and political force’ from the opposition.

Rodolfo Carter attacked the opposition as ‘very damaging.’ The government says it will negotiate project-by-project to pass the reform.

What It Means for Residents and Investors

For residents, the reform could mean more military presence in high-crime areas. It also promises tougher prison conditions for gang members.

Homicides fell 11.5% in 2025 from 2024. The rate is about 20% below the 2022 peak.

Investors may see the reform as a sign of stability. A stronger state response to crime could reduce business risks.

The fast-track timetable means decisions could come quickly. Watch the Senate vote in the coming weeks for the next signal.

Chile’s Crime Debate in Context

Chile’s government faces rising public worry over organized crime. President Kast’s reform aims to make security a state duty.

The proposal creates a new emergency power for grave security threats. This tool would let armed forces deploy in affected zones.

Homicides fell recently but remain above past levels. Violent robberies also dropped, yet public fear stays high.

The reform needs a four-sevenths quorum in both chambers. That forces the government to negotiate with opposition parties.

What Comes Next in Congress

The government wants an express two-to-three month timetable. The bill enters through the Senate with highest urgency status.

Opposition groups like PS, PPD, and FA are closing ranks. They lack majorities but can block or delay changes.

Broad support is essential to alter the constitution successfully. Kast must borrow votes from rival blocs to pass it.

Residents should watch for prison regime and asset forfeiture rules. Investors will track whether emergency powers affect business zones.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a constitutional reform?

A constitutional reform is a change to a country’s supreme law. It requires a special high quorum, like 4/7 in Chile’s Congress.

What is a state of exception?

A state of exception is a legal emergency status. It gives the government temporary extra powers, like deploying the armed forces.

When was the reform signed?

President Kast signed the reform on Monday, August 10, 2026. It was sent to the Senate that same day.

How long will approval take?

The government wants approval in two to three months. It requested ‘urgencia suma’ to force a fast vote.

Sources: Government of Chile (La Moneda); UPI; Chilean press reports.

World.title: Uruguay Beef Exports Hit by New China Suspension
World.content:
Uruguay · Business

Key Facts China suspended beef imports from Frigorifico Tacuarembo S.A. on 6 August 2026.

The suspension follows a second detection of imidocarb residues above the allowed limit.

Imidocarb is a veterinary drug used against bovine trypanosomiasis, a cattle disease.

China’s GACC flagged an earlier imidocarb case on 19 May 2026.

China took 42% of Uruguay’s beef export value in 2024 and 36% in H1 2025.

Uruguay’s beef exports to China reached about US$862.8 million by end-November 2025.

Uruguay’s total beef exports were US$2.68 billion in 2025, with 25 plants certified for China.

China halted imports from a major Uruguayan plant after a second drug residue finding. Here is what it means.

Cattle graze on open pasture; grass-fed beef is central to Uruguay’s export brand. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0)

Uruguay beef exports face a new hurdle after China suspended a major plant. The suspension began Thursday 6 August 2026.

Hitting Frigorifico Tacuarembo S.A. This is the second imidocarb residue case for the plant in 2026. You should know how this affects trade and what comes next.

What China Suspended and Why

China suspended beef imports from Frigorifico Tacuarembo S.A. on 6 August 2026. The plant is located in Tacuarembo, Uruguay, and is known as plant No 12.

This action came from China’s sanitary authorities, according to MGAP. It follows a second detection of imidocarb residues above the allowed limit.

The earlier imidocarb case was flagged by GACC on 19 May 2026. You should note this is a repeat issue for the same establishment.

Suspensions like this are serious for exporters. They stop all shipments to China until the problem is resolved.

The Residue Behind the Ban

Imidocarb is a veterinary drug used against bovine trypanosomiasis. This disease is also known as ‘tristeza bovina’ in Spanish.

The drug treats a cattle illness spread by ticks. You might hear it called an antiprotozoal agent.

China sets a maximum residue limit, or MRL, for imidocarb in beef. The plant exceeded this limit twice, triggering the ban.

Residue limits protect consumers from potential health risks. You should understand that even small exceedances can halt trade.

Why Uruguay Beef Exports Lean on China

Uruguay beef exports depend heavily on the Chinese market. China took 42% of Uruguay’s beef export value in 2024.

That share fell to 36% in the first half of 2025, per USDA FAS. You can see the trend is still significant.

Uruguay’s beef exports to China reached about US$862.8 million by end-November 2025. Total beef exports were US$2.68 billion in 2025.

This means China is a top buyer, not a minor partner. Any suspension affects overall revenue and producer confidence.

Tacuarembo, Uruguay’s Biggest Plant

Frigorifico Tacuarembo S.A. is described as Uruguay’s largest meat plant. El Pais and RealEstate-in-Uruguay both support this claim.

The plant is owned by Marfrig, a global meat company. It underwent expansion to become the largest industrial facility.

Being the biggest means high production volumes and many jobs. You can imagine the local impact of this suspension.

The plant’s size also raises stakes for trade relations. A halt here sends a strong signal to other exporters.

How Montevideo Responded

Uruguay’s agriculture ministry, MGAP, said it will investigate the episode’s origin. They also plan to reinforce controls across the chain.

This response aims to prevent future residue issues. You should expect stricter testing at farms and plants.

The government is working to restore confidence with China. They need to show the problem is under control.

No named quotes from INAC or industry officials were available. The focus is on MGAP’s official statement.

What It Means for Producers and Buyers

Producers at Tacuarembo face halted shipments and potential revenue loss. You might see short-term price pressure on Uruguayan beef.

Buyers in China will look for alternative suppliers. This could shift some trade to other countries like Brazil or Argentina.

The suspension may also affect Uruguay’s reputation as a reliable exporter. You should watch for future inspections and audits.

For now, 25 Uruguayan plants remain certified for China. But this case shows how fragile market access can be.

What Investors and Traders Should Watch

Watch how fast Uruguay resolves the imidocarb issue, as suspensions are usually lifted after plant fixes and audits. Historical patterns suggest a few weeks to months, depending on Chinese inspections.

Monitor price movements in beef futures and export contracts, as China’s reduced share could pressure prices. A prolonged ban on a major plant would tighten supply and potentially raise costs for other buyers.

Track MGAP’s investigation and any new residue testing protocols, which could affect all 25 certified plants. Stricter controls may slow export volumes but improve long-term market stability.

Expect China to remain a key buyer despite the dip, given its demand for Uruguayan beef. Traders should hedge against volatility by diversifying destinations and staying alert to policy shifts.

Frequently Asked Questions

What exactly did China suspend?

China suspended beef imports from Frigorifico Tacuarembo S.A., a major Uruguayan plant. The suspension began on 6 August 2026.

Why was imidocarb found in the beef?

Imidocarb is a veterinary drug used to treat bovine trypanosomiasis. It was found above the allowed limit in two separate cases.

How much does Uruguay export beef to China?

Uruguay’s beef exports to China were about US$862.8 million by end-November 2025. China took 36% of export value in H1 2025.

What happens next for the plant?

MGAP will investigate and reinforce controls across the chain. The plant must fix residue issues before exports can resume.

Sources: Uruguay’s MGAP; El País (Uruguay); USDA Foreign Agricultural Service; Uruguay XXI; La Diaria; CGTN.

World.title: China Pecan Tariffs: Mexico and US Face New Cash Deposits
World.content:
Mexico · Business

Key Facts China’s MOFCOM issued a preliminary anti-dumping determination on 10 August 2026.

Provisional cash-deposit measures take effect on 11 August 2026.

US exporters face a uniform 54.3% cash deposit rate.

Mexican exporters face rates ranging from 17.8% to 51.6%.

The covered product is fresh or dried pecans under HS code 08029990.

Mexico was the fifth-largest pecan producer worldwide in 2024.

Chihuahua accounted for 59.7% of Mexico’s national pecan production in 2024.

China’s MOFCOM imposed preliminary anti-dumping duties on pecans from Mexico and the US, with rates ranging from 17.8% to 54.3%.

A pecan grove; Chihuahua grows most of Mexico’s pecans. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons, public domain)

China pecan tariffs now threaten one of Mexico’s most export-focused crops. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) has imposed preliminary anti-dumping duties on pecans from Mexico and the United States.

With provisional cash-deposit measures taking effect on 11 August 2026.

What China Did and Why

China’s MOFCOM issued a preliminary anti-dumping determination on 10 August 2026. The agency found that dumped pecan imports caused material injury to China’s domestic industry.

The investigation began on 25 September 2025, following a complaint from local growers. MOFCOM acted under China’s Anti-Dumping Regulations and in line with WTO rules.

The provisional measures require importers to pay cash deposits on fresh or dried pecans. These pecans fall under Chinese tariff heading 08029990.

The deposits apply to shipments from both Mexico and the United States. This action is preliminary, not final, and a final determination will come later.

MOFCOM stated there is a causal relationship between the dumped imports and the injury. The agency will continue its investigation before issuing a final ruling.

The Cash Deposit Rates, Firm by Firm

US exporters face a uniform 54.3% cash deposit rate. No US company participated in the investigation, so all received the same rate.

Mexican exporters face rates ranging from 17.8% to 51.6%. The rates depend on whether companies cooperated with MOFCOM’s investigation.

San Enrique Agricultural Enterprises received a 23.0% rate. Alta Vineyards received the lowest rate at 17.8%.

Four other cooperating Mexican companies received a 22.2% rate. Non-cooperating Mexican companies face the highest rate of 51.6%.

These rates are provisional and could change after the final determination. Importers must pay the deposits when bringing pecans into China.

What the China Pecan Tariffs Mean for Mexico

Mexico is a major pecan exporter, and China is a key market. The new tariffs will make Mexican pecans more expensive for Chinese buyers.

An anti-dumping duty is a tax on imports sold below fair market value. A cash deposit is money importers must pay upfront, which may be refunded later.

The 17.8% to 51.6% range means some Mexican exporters will face significant cost increases. This could reduce their competitiveness in the Chinese market.

Mexico’s pecan sector is export-led and highly concentrated in northern states. Growers may need to find alternative markets or absorb the higher costs.

However, China was reported as the second-largest destination for Mexican pecans.

Chihuahua and the Growers on the Front Line

Chihuahua is Mexico’s leading pecan-producing state, accounting for 59.7% of national output in 2024. The state’s growers will feel the impact of these tariffs most directly.

Other major producing states include Sonora, Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Durango. These five states concentrate more than 97% of Mexico’s planted pecan area.

Mexico produced 167,777 tonnes of pecans in 2024, ranking as the fifth-largest producer worldwide. The United States is the world’s largest producer.

Chihuahua’s growers have relied heavily on exports, with the United States as the top destination. China has been the second-largest market for Mexican pecans.

The new tariffs could force Chihuahua’s growers to seek new buyers or negotiate better prices. Local agricultural authorities have not yet issued public statements on the tariffs.

The US Angle and What Comes Next

US pecan exporters face the highest rate at 54.3%, with no exceptions. This is because no US company participated in China’s investigation.

The tariffs come amid ongoing trade tensions between Washington and Beijing. The timing suggests a possible link to broader trade negotiations.

MOFCOM’s action covers both Mexico and the United States in a single determination. This is unusual, as most anti-dumping cases target one country.

The preliminary measures take effect on 11 August 2026, one day after the announcement. Importers must comply immediately with the new cash deposit requirements.

A final determination is expected later, which could adjust the rates. US and Mexican exporters may still have opportunities to present their case to MOFCOM.

How Exporters and Buyers Are Affected

Mexican growers now face cash deposits from 17.8% to 51.6%.

Cooperating firms get lower rates, while others pay the top rate.

This makes Mexican pecans pricier for Chinese buyers immediately.

Chinese importers must pay these deposits starting August 11, 2026.

Higher costs may reduce demand and shift purchases to other suppliers.

U.S. exporters face a uniform 54.3% rate, hurting their competitiveness.

Trade diversion could push Mexican growers to seek new markets.

Buyers might turn to domestic pecans or other nut sources.

This is preliminary, so final duties could change later.

Growers and buyers should watch for the final ruling closely.

What Investors Should Watch

Investors should monitor how Chinese buyers react to higher costs.

Watch for shifts in Mexico’s export volumes to other countries.

Check if Mexican firms appeal or adjust their pricing strategies.

The final ruling could lower or raise current deposit rates.

Keep an eye on U.S. trade relations and possible negotiations.

Pecan prices may fluctuate as markets adjust to new duties.

Look for updates from MOFCOM on the investigation timeline.

Investors should assess risks in companies reliant on China sales.

Diversification efforts by growers could open new opportunities.

Stay informed, as this trade action remains preliminary and evolving.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an anti-dumping duty?

An anti-dumping duty is a tax imposed on imported goods sold below their fair market value. It aims to protect domestic industries from unfair competition.

What is a cash deposit in this context?

A cash deposit is money importers must pay upfront when bringing goods into China. The deposit may be refunded or kept depending on the final ruling.

When do the new tariffs take effect?

The provisional cash-deposit measures take effect on 11 August 2026. This is one day after MOFCOM announced the preliminary determination on 10 August.

Will the rates change after the final determination?

Yes, the rates are provisional and could change. MOFCOM will continue its investigation and may adjust the rates in its final ruling.

Those two things do not belong together, and the gap between them is this week’s real story.

United States – Confidence That Insures Itself

A record, and a record

American shares closed at an all-time high on Friday, the broad index finishing at 7,757.64 after the strongest week since April. Over those five days it gained 3.58%, the technology index 5.19% and the industrial average 2.96%.

On Monday gold reached fresh record highs, trading near 4,400 dollars an ounce after 4,341 on Friday. Investors bought the rally and the insurance against it in the same week.

Nobody behaves like this when they are sure

A country that believed in its own recovery would not be paying record prices for the asset people hold when they stop believing in things. Bank of America reports investor bullishness at its highest since 2021, which makes the gold bid stranger rather than less so.

The national temper here is not optimism but hedged optimism, which is a different and more anxious animal. This is a market taking the trade while quietly buying protection from the person sitting next to it.

United States – Defending Somebody Else’s Currency

Euros sold to buy yen

On Friday 31 July the United States Treasury sold euros from its own reserves to buy Japanese yen, acting alongside Tokyo, and both governments confirmed it on 3 August. The yen had touched 163.73 to the dollar and strengthened to 157.57.

It was the first joint American and Japanese purchase of yen since 1998, and the first coordinated action between them since 2011, when the aim was the opposite. Before a press event at Camp David the Treasury Secretary was photographed with a notepad reading, plainly, buy Japanese yen five to ten billion.

A creditor nation getting nervous about its creditors

The reason was not friendship. Japan is the largest foreign holder of American government debt, and had it acted alone it might have had to sell those holdings to fund the purchase, pushing United States yields higher.

One economist called the American participation an element of self-preservation. A superpower quietly propping up another country’s currency to protect its own bond market is not a display of strength, and the gold price suggests investors read it the same way.

United States – Institutions Doubting Their Own Tools

A remedy that might kill the patient

Mozilla said on Monday that tougher antitrust remedies against Google could force it out of the market altogether. The company the competition case is meant to protect is warning that winning it could finish them.

That is what institutional self-doubt sounds like in practice. The tool no longer reliably produces the outcome it was built for.

A takeover fight everyone is picking sides in

California’s attorney general is facing calls for an investigation into his handling of the Paramount and Warner Bros. suit, while the owner of Regal Cinemas has come out in support of the merger and Paramount has offered theatrical releases to both AMC and Regal with its bid still live.

Cinema chains are now negotiating with the bidder rather than waiting for the regulator. When the parties stop expecting the referee to decide, they start doing deals in the corridor.

American shares closed at a record after their best week since April, and gold hit a record on the same trade — a country buying the rally and the insurance against it at the same time, and paying full price for both.

United States – A Country Unsure What Its Own Data Says

The weakness that may not be weakness

July’s employment report showed payrolls falling 23,000 against an expected gain of 80,000, with a further 103,000 revised out of the two previous months. It was the number that drove both the rally and the change in interest-rate expectations.

The largest single contributor was leisure and hospitality, down 40,000, which analysts attribute largely to the end of the football World Cup. Local government education accounted for much of the rest.

Everything now rests on Wednesday

Markets cut the odds of a September rate rise from about 60% to 40% and now see a hold as more likely than an increase, sending the ten-year yield to 4.65%. That entire repricing rests on a jobs figure whose biggest component may have been a sporting tournament ending.

July consumer prices arrive on Wednesday morning and producer prices on Thursday. A country that has already spent the gain is waiting to find out whether it was real.

Canada – Doing Everything Right, On Somebody Else’s Clock

The best month in two years

Canada added 75,100 jobs in July, taking unemployment to 6.4%, its lowest since July 2024. Canadian bond yields rose on the news, which is what happens when a market reads strength rather than trouble.

That is a country executing well. It is also a country that cannot convert the result into confidence.

Nine days, and no lever

A 50% American tariff on roughly 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods takes effect on 19 August, nine days from now. Nothing Ottawa has done in the labour market changes that date by an hour.

The mood here is not fear but a particular kind of tiredness, the exhaustion of performing well on a schedule you do not set. Canada has learned to post good numbers without being allowed to enjoy them.

The Week Ahead – Everything Held Until Wednesday

One number, three days of waiting

The industrial average edged lower on Monday and oil stayed elevated, with the strait through which much of the world’s crude passes still unresolved. Simon Property Group reported, and the week’s real events all sit later.

Consumer prices land Wednesday at half past eight, producer prices Thursday, retail sales Friday. Three days of a country holding still.

What it means from Latin America

A Federal Reserve that holds rather than raises keeps the dollar contained and emerging-market borrowing costs manageable, which is the single most useful thing Washington can do for the region right now. Gold at a record is simultaneously excellent news for Latin American producers and a warning about what the money is worried about.

The same Treasury fund used to buy yen was used less than a year ago to steady the Argentine peso before the midterms, at 2.5 billion dollars, repaid in full. Washington has rediscovered currency intervention as a tool, and Latin America was the first place it tried it.

The Bigger Picture The contradiction is the story, because American shares closed Friday at a record of 7,757.64 after their best week since April and by Monday gold was at a record too, near 4,400 dollars an ounce. Investor bullishness is at its highest since 2021 and the safest asset in the world has never been more expensive. Underneath that sits a Treasury that sold euros to buy yen on 31 July, because Japan holds more American government debt than anyone and might otherwise have had to sell it. And a rate repricing built on a jobs report whose largest single component was a 40,000 fall in leisure and hospitality after the World Cup ended. Canada meanwhile posted its best employment month in two years and cannot enjoy it, with a 50% tariff nine days out. For Latin American readers the practical read is a Federal Reserve more likely to hold than raise, a dollar under less pressure, and a gold price that is both a windfall and a warning. And with Africa and Asia tightening at the same time, that becomes a price signal for Latin American exporters.

Europe – The Record, and What Sits Underneath It

Warmest June and July ever measured

Western Europe averaged 21.62 degrees across June and July, the European Union’s climate service reported on Monday, 2.79 degrees above the 1991 to 2020 mean and above the previous record set in 2022. Its records run back to 1950.

The region has now had four separate heatwaves since May, which the service describes as exceptional. Eastern Europe and Scandinavia were markedly cooler, and for the continent as a whole July was only the eleventh warmest on record.

The soil is the number that matters

Surface soil moisture in Western Europe was clearly lower in July than during the drought July of 2022, with parts of Iberia, France, Germany, Austria, Hungary and Britain drier than average. The world’s oceans meanwhile recorded their warmest July on record at 20.96 degrees.

The service’s climate lead put the mechanism plainly, saying that when soils dry out they lose their ability to cool naturally, so heat builds more easily. Heat and drought, she said, are increasingly reinforcing each other.

The Rivers – Three Arteries Running Low

Shipping, irrigation and power at once

Levels on the Rhine, the Danube and the Seine are unusually low. Several countries have reported disruption to inland shipping, to irrigation and to electricity generation.

These are the arteries that move German chemicals, Dutch grain and Central European steel. When barges load light, freight costs rise across the whole corridor.

A continent discovering its own fragility

Europe has spent two decades treating its inland waterways as settled infrastructure. Three summers in five years have now shown that assumption to be wrong.

The mood is not alarm so much as a grudging recalculation. This is a continent adding a line to its cost base that was never there before.

Germany – Where the Weather Reaches the Accounts

Farms under pressure, output falling

Drought and heat are squeezing German agricultural businesses, and the farmers’ association is demanding faster action from government. German meat production has fallen again, with the decline particularly clear in poultry.

June was almost three degrees above average in Germany, with the southwest markedly warmer than the northeast. A second consecutive summer of this kind stops being weather and starts being a supply forecast.

Two numbers about German labour and tax

The trade union federation calculates that around two million employees are underpaid relative to the minimum wage each year, putting the cumulative shortfall since 2015 at roughly 64 billion euros against a statutory floor of 13.90 euros an hour. Separately, the finance minister has withdrawn a plan to tax associations more heavily after sustained criticism, striking the provision from the bill.

He said the intention had never been to reach small clubs but business associations and federations. A government retreating from a revenue measure it had just drafted says something about how little room it has.

Western Europe has just recorded its warmest June and July since measurements began, its soils are drier than in the drought of 2022, and the Rhine, Danube and Seine are all low enough to disrupt shipping — the summer has become a line in the cost base.

Spain – Two Hundred Thousand Hectares and a Revised Number

The fire season moves north

Nearly 200,000 hectares have burned in Spain since the start of the year. The European climate service notes that the fire season is extending northward, and that larger fires send smoke higher and further, affecting air quality thousands of kilometres away.

Spain is the European Union’s largest producer of olive oil and a major supplier of fruit and vegetables. What burns there is felt in food prices across the bloc.

Madrid revises Ceuta upward

The government now estimates that around 80,000 people entered the North African enclave of Ceuta irregularly during the surge of late July, up from a previous figure of 72,000. The territorial policy minister gave the revised number during a visit to the exclave on Monday.

Most of those who crossed returned to Morocco within 24 to 48 hours, and the surge occurred mainly on 30 July. Revising a figure upward by eight thousand two weeks later tells you how uncertain the counting was.

Three Continents – One Harvest Tightening

The same story from Lusaka to Seoul

The World Food Programme warned last week that a strengthening El Niño could push nearly 49 million more people into acute hunger by the end of 2027, with Southern Africa among the hardest hit. In Asia, China’s own state newspaper reported economies facing food security risks while Korean employers shortened the working day for heat.

Europe has now added its own record. Three continents are tightening their agricultural output within the same fortnight.

What that means for Latin America

This is not a weather story for Latin American readers, it is a price story. Simultaneous supply pressure across Europe, Africa and Asia points to firmer markets for soy, corn, beef, coffee, sugar and wheat.

Brazilian and Argentine exporters are the residual supplier when three other continents come up short. The risk sits on the other side of the same coin, since the weather system driving all of it does not stop at the Atlantic.

Energy – The Second Cost Line

Low water meets high fuel

The same low river levels disrupting freight are also affecting electricity generation, at a moment when European energy costs remain politically sensitive. Two constraints are arriving in the same quarter.

On the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran’s stated conditions continue to increase pressure on Washington, and nothing has been settled. Any resolution would ease European input costs immediately.

The quiet week that is not quiet

France, Italy and Britain produced nothing of substance on Monday, deep in the European holiday. That silence is seasonal rather than significant.

The costs accumulating in the meantime are not seasonal at all. Europe will return to its desks in September with a harvest, a freight bill and an energy question all worse than when it left.

The Bigger Picture Western Europe has recorded its warmest June and July since measurements began in 1950, averaging 21.62 degrees, 2.79 degrees above the long-run mean and beating the record set in 2022. Four heatwaves since May, soils drier than in the drought of 2022, and the Rhine, Danube and Seine all low enough to disrupt shipping, irrigation and power. In Germany the effect is already visible in the accounts, with farms under pressure and meat production falling again. In Spain nearly 200,000 hectares have burned this year, in a country that supplies much of the bloc’s olive oil, fruit and vegetables. For Latin American readers the significance is not the heat but the coincidence. Africa, Asia and Europe are all tightening agricultural supply within the same fortnight, which points to firmer prices for the region’s soy, corn, beef, coffee and sugar, and to a weather system that will not stop at the Atlantic. Colombia · News

A magnitude 7.4 quake tore through western Colombia on Monday morning, killing dozens and handing a president just three days in office his first national emergency.

The Colombia earthquake that hit on Monday, 10 August 2026 was one of the strongest the country has felt in years. It struck at around 7:34 a.m. local time, and by midday the death toll had passed five dozen.

The tremor was centered about 5 kilometers east of San José del Palmar, a small town in the jungle department of Chocó. The United States Geological Survey put it at magnitude 7.4.

Because the quake was so powerful, it was felt across much of the country and into neighboring Ecuador and Panama. Buildings swayed hundreds of kilometers from the epicenter, and frightened residents ran into the streets.

What we know about the Colombia earthquake

The USGS measured the quake at magnitude 7.4 and placed its focus 107 kilometers below the surface. The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre logged a slightly smaller magnitude of 7.2 at a similar depth.

That depth matters more than it sounds. A shallow quake concentrates its violence at the surface, while a deep one like this spreads the shaking over a much wider area but does less damage directly above.

It is the reason a monster 7.4 was felt from Quito to Panama City yet did not level whole towns. It is also why the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center ruled out any tsunami, saying the quake was too deep inside the Earth to move the sea.

The human toll

By the middle of Monday, local officials reported at least 69 deaths, and the number kept climbing as rescuers reached collapsed buildings. The dead included 40 in Risaralda, 27 in Valle del Cauca and two in Manizales.

Many more people were injured, and more than 20 municipalities reported damage. Collapsed or cracked buildings were confirmed in Cali, Pereira, Manizales and Quibdó.

Six airports suspended operations, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura. The closures cut off some of the fastest routes into the worst-hit areas just as help was most needed.

A president three days into the job

The disaster is the first major test for Abelardo de la Espriella, who was sworn in as president on Friday, 7 August 2026. He took office in Cali, breaking with tradition, and now that same city counts damaged buildings.

De la Espriella said he would take personal charge of the response and ordered a Unified Command Post, the body Colombia uses to coordinate agencies in a crisis. He suspended his agenda in Bogotá and said he would travel to Pereira, near the epicenter.

De la Espriella told Colombians they were “not alone” and that “the state is present and taking action.” He had campaigned on a hard line on security, not on a natural disaster in his first week.

He succeeded Gustavo Petro only this month, and the quake now frames the opening of his term. How his young government handles the rescue and the rebuilding will shape early opinion of it.

Help from abroad

The United States was quick to respond. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration “stands ready to support the people of Colombia” and was closely monitoring the disaster.

The tremor was also felt in Ecuador and Panama, though both reported only minor damage. For a region that sits on the restless edge of the Nazca and South American plates, Monday was a reminder of how quickly the ground can turn.

What it means for residents and travelers

For anyone in the region, the first effect was on travel. Six airports were shut, grounding flights into Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura and cutting the quickest routes into the disaster zone.

Big quakes are almost always followed by aftershocks, which can bring down walls already cracked by the first jolt. In the hardest-hit towns, damaged and leaning buildings were the main danger once the shaking stopped.

Colombia sits where the Nazca plate grinds beneath South America, which makes it one of the most seismically active countries in the region. A focus 107 kilometers down let the energy travel far, which is why the shaking reached Quito and Panama City.

Frequently Asked Questions

How big was the Colombia earthquake and where did it hit?

The United States Geological Survey measured it at magnitude 7.4, centered about 5 kilometers east of San José del Palmar in Chocó, at a depth of 107 kilometers. It struck at around 7:34 a.m. local time on Monday, 10 August 2026.

How many people died in the Colombia earthquake?

Local officials reported at least 69 deaths by midday Monday, with 40 in Risaralda, 27 in Valle del Cauca and two in Manizales. The toll was still rising as rescue teams reached collapsed buildings.

Which airports closed after the earthquake?

Six airports suspended operations, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura. The closures disrupted travel across western and central Colombia.

Did the earthquake cause a tsunami?

No. The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center said there was no tsunami threat because the quake was too deep inside the Earth.

Sources: U.S. Geological Survey; European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre; Pacific Tsunami Warning Center; Colombian departmental officials via The Associated Press; France 24; El Tiempo; Infobae; Portafolio; U.S. Department of State (Secretary Marco Rubio).

World.title: What You Actually Owe at Costa Rica’s Land Borders
World.content:
Costa Rica charges you exactly one fee to leave the country by land, and it is $8. That is the whole amount. If someone at a border post asks you for more than that or asks you to hand cash to a person rather than pay at a bank window or a kiosk, you are not looking at a government charge.

This matters right now because of a case working its way through the courts on the Caribbean side. A Fuerza Pública officer assigned to the Limón area had been suspended from duty since March 26 at the request of prosecutors in Bribri, the office whose territory covers the Sixaola crossing. The allegation against him was concusión which is an offense a public official commits by demanding money they have no right to collect.

He was shot and killed in Batán on Sunday. He was never tried, and the investigation into both the killing and the original allegation continues. But the case is a reminder that the fee structure at a land border is simple enough that you can memorize it, and that knowing it is your best protection.

The only fee Costa Rica charges you to leave

The land exit tax is $8 per person. It breaks down as $5 for the tax itself, $2 for phytosanitary scanning, and $1 for animal health inspection through SENASA. At the Central Bank’s reference rate on August 10, that is roughly ₡3,630. The tax exists because agricultural inspection at land crossings costs money, and Costa Rica funds it from the people who use those crossings. It has been in force since December 2013 under Ley 9154.

Everyone leaving on foot or by car pays it, every time. There is no residency exemption, no discount, and no reason for the amount to vary by crossing, by day of the week, or by how busy the line is. A single national law sets it, and the Banco de Costa Rica is the only institution authorized to collect it.

Costa Rica charges you nothing to enter by land. If you are asked for an entry fee coming back in, that is not a real charge either.

Pay it before you leave home

The easiest way to avoid the whole problem is to pay online before you travel. Go to bancobcr.com (In Spanish) and pay with any Visa or Mastercard, debit or credit, issued anywhere. You do not need to be a BCR customer, and the bank adds nothing on top of the $8. You will get a PDF receipt by email. You do not need to show it at the border, because immigration registers the payment automatically when your passport is scanned. Bring it anyway. A receipt in your hand ends an argument before it starts.

If you would rather pay in person, BCR collects at the border posts at Sixaola, Peñas Blancas, Tablillas and Sabalito, at its Paso Canoas branch 150 meters (about 165 yards) south of the crossing, and at its Liberia business center. Bring valid identification and the passport you will actually travel on. You can pay in dollars or colones at the day’s rate.

The payment does not expire on a date. It stays valid until your exit and your subsequent re-entry are recorded, so paying a few days ahead costs you nothing.

If someone asks you for more

The Banco de Costa Rica states plainly that the official rate is $8.00, and it publishes a channel for reporting overcharges. Write to usuarioscoimsa@bancobcr.com, or call 2211-1111, extensions 13711, 13726 or 20607. Pay online so there is nothing to negotiate at the window. Refuse to hand money to anyone who is not behind a bank counter or an official kiosk. Ask for a receipt for every payment and treat the absence of one as the signal it is.

Note the crossing, the approximate time and the window or booth number. If a uniformed official is involved, that detail is what makes a complaint actionable rather than a story. You will also find informal helpers at Sixaola and Paso Canoas offering to walk your paperwork through for a tip. They are not officials and they are not required. Nothing at either crossing needs an intermediary, and the exit tax in particular is a personal transaction that no third party can complete for you.

If you are driving across

Taking your own vehicle out is a separate process from the exit tax and costs more. You need a digital exit circulation card, arranged through BCR, and there is a bank fee plus fiscal stamps on top of the $8 you pay for yourself. Confirm the current amounts with BCR before you go rather than at the border. Many people crossing to Bocas del Toro skip this entirely and leave the car in the guarded lot on the Costa Rican side at Sixaola, since the onward trip runs by boat anyway.

Coming back in

Immigration decides how long you get, and the rules changed in November 2025 under a directive that sorts countries into four groups. If you hold a passport in the first group, which covers the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU states and about 60 countries in all, you can be given up to 180 calendar days. That period cannot be extended, though if the officer grants you fewer than 90 days you can apply for up to 90 more.

Second-group nationals get up to 30 days initially, extendable to a maximum of 90, and need at least 90 days of passport validity to enter at all. None of this is automatic. The officer at the window decides the number, and 180 days is a ceiling rather than an entitlement. Carry proof of onward travel within the period you are asking for.

Arriving without it is one of the most common reasons people are turned back, and a land crossing gives you fewer options than an airport when that happens. If you are leaving and returning specifically to reset your permitted stay, understand that nothing obliges an officer to grant you a fresh 180 days, and that the government has said publicly it is looking at this practice.

What happens on the Panama side

Panama sets its own fees and its own entry requirements, and they are not the same as Costa Rica’s. Panamanian immigration asks for a passport with at least six months of validity, onward travel out of Panama, and proof you can cover your stay — officially a minimum of $500, which you can show with cash, a credit card, a bank statement or an employment letter.

Amounts circulating online for the Panamanian side are years out of date and contradict each other, so check migracion.gob.pa or ask the Panamanian consulate before you travel. Bring small dollar bills. Apply the same rule you use in Costa Rica: pay at an official window and get a receipt for anything you hand over.

One more thing worth knowing at Sixaola. Panama runs an hour ahead of Costa Rica, and the two immigration posts keep their own hours. Arrive with enough of the day left that a slow line on one side does not strand you on the bridge between two closed offices.

World.title: Jannik Sinner Withdraws From Cincinnati Open With Knee Injury
World.content:
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the 2026 Cincinnati Open because of a right knee injury, removing another of the tournament’s biggest stars just days before the men’s main draw begins. Sinner announced Sunday that continuing discomfort in his right knee had left him unable to compete despite treatment and work with his medical team.

“My right knee has been bothering me,” Sinner said, adding that he had to accept that he was “not ready to compete yet.” The 24-year-old Italian will instead focus on getting healthy for the US Open, which begins August 30 in New York. The withdrawal is a significant blow for Cincinnati. Sinner won the tournament in 2024 and returned to the final last year, where Carlos Alcaraz took the title after Sinner retired during the opening set.

Sinner had been expected to arrive in Ohio as the No. 1 player in the world and one of the leading favorites for the title. Instead, he joins Alcaraz among the major names missing from the men’s field. Alcaraz withdrew earlier this week because of the right wrist injury that has kept him out of competition since April.

Sinner’s absence also raises questions about how much competitive preparation he will have before the final Grand Slam of the season. He has not played since winning Wimbledon in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final to capture the fifth Grand Slam singles title of his career. Sinner had already withdrawn from the Canadian Open, meaning Cincinnati was positioned to provide his most important match preparation on North American hard courts before the US Open.

Reports from Europe in recent days had already raised doubts about his participation in Cincinnati. Sinner underwent medical examinations and treatment for the knee problem before ultimately deciding against traveling to compete. The injury does not currently appear to have changed his intention to play the US Open. Sinner made clear Sunday that preparing for New York is now the priority.

“I’m now focusing on getting ready for the US Open,” he said. Sinner’s withdrawal also changes the Cincinnati draw before play begins. Stefanos Tsitsipas, the 2022 Cincinnati finalist who had originally been listed in qualifying, is expected to move into the main field in Sinner’s place.

For Cincinnati organizers, losing both Sinner and Alcaraz removes the two players who contested last year’s championship match and two of the sport’s biggest attractions. Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic remain among the leading names scheduled to compete in the ATP Masters 1000 tournament.

The Cincinnati Open men’s main draw begins August 13 and runs through August 23. For Sinner, however, the immediate concern has shifted from defending ranking points or adding another Masters 1000 title to making sure his knee is ready for New York. With the US Open only three weeks away, his recovery will now be one of the biggest stories heading into the final Grand Slam of the year.

World.title: Playa Blanca Parking Lot Closes Amid Costa Rica Beach Access Dispute
World.content:
Those heading to Playa Blanca at Punta Leona will face another change in how they reach one of Costa Rica’s most popular Central Pacific beaches after the parking area directly in front of the beach was temporarily closed. The closure stems from a disagreement involving Punta Leona Beach Club & Nature Resort and the Ministry of Health’s local office in Garabito over requirements connected to the parking operation and sanitary facilities.

Punta Leona said it is working to address the requirements while seeking clarification of the technical criteria behind the measure. In the meantime, the resort plans to make an auxiliary parking area available and reinforce its shuttle service carrying visitors to and from Playa Blanca.

The development does not mean Playa Blanca itself has been closed. Public access to the beach remains available, but visitors arriving by car should expect different parking arrangements while the dispute is resolved. The closure adds another chapter to a long-running and increasingly complicated debate over public access to Playa Blanca.

In June, the Municipality of Garabito removed barriers controlling access through Punta Leona after municipal officials maintained that the road leading toward the beach is public. The move opened the route to visitors who are not hotel guests or members of the resort. Punta Leona has disputed the municipality’s interpretation and maintains that issues involving the road and surrounding property should ultimately be resolved through the courts.

Parking quickly became one of the biggest practical problems created by increased access. There are relatively few places for vehicles near Playa Blanca, and authorities have warned drivers not to park along the access road. Traffic Police officers have previously removed license plates from vehicles parked illegally in the area after cars obstructed traffic.

Private parking has therefore become an important part of visiting the beach by car. Before the latest closure, the Punta Leona parking facility was one of the main options available to visitors. The service had been offered for ₡20,000 for eight hours and included access to bathrooms. Other private parking operators and transportation services are also available around the area.

The latest disagreement highlights a larger challenge surrounding public beach access in Costa Rica. While the country’s beaches are public, reaching them can sometimes be difficult when surrounding land is privately owned or when roads, parking and visitor infrastructure are limited.

Playa Blanca has become one of the clearest examples of the difference between having a legal right to visit a beach and having the infrastructure necessary to accommodate large numbers of visitors. The situation has drawn additional attention because Playa Blanca is widely considered one of the Central Pacific’s most attractive beaches, known for its lighter-colored sand and sheltered waters.

Its location near Jacó, Herradura and Carara National Park also makes it easily accessible for anyone staying along the Central Pacific coast. For now though, beach goers planning a trip to Playa Blanca should not assume the parking arrangement they previously used remains available. Those driving to the area should confirm parking options before arriving and avoid leaving vehicles along the access road.

There is currently no announced date for reopening the parking area directly in front of Playa Blanca.

World.title: International News: Western Europe records hottest summer start as heatwaves and wildfires intensify
World.content:
International News: Western Europe records hottest summer start as heatwaves and wildfires intensify

By Zoila Palma: Western Europe has recorded its hottest first two months of summer on record, with the region facing devastating wildfires, severe drought and another heatwave expected this week. The European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service said the average temperature for June and July reached 21.62 degrees Celsius, about 2.79 degrees above the average and surpassing the previous record set in 2022.

July was also the hottest month ever recorded for the world’s non-polar oceans, with record temperatures reported across the Atlantic and western Mediterranean, CNN reports.

Scientists warned that unusually warm seas are putting marine life and coastal communities at risk, while Europe’s extreme heat has been intensified by persistent drought.

Climate experts said dry soils lose their ability to provide natural cooling, allowing temperatures to rise further.

The extreme conditions have also fueled Europe’s worst wildfire season on record, with more than 1.23 million acres burned, mainly across Spain, France and Italy, according to an EU report.

Hundreds of thousands of people have been displaced, while smoke from the fires has worsened air quality across wider areas. Soil moisture levels in western Europe were significantly lower in July than during the severe drought of 2022, with France, Spain and parts of Germany and the United Kingdom recording exceptional or record rainfall and soil moisture deficits.

World.title: International News: Strong El Niño could bring greater weather impacts and improve seasonal forecasting
World.content:
International News: Strong El Niño could bring greater weather impacts and improve seasonal forecasting

By Zoila Palma: An unusually strong El Niño is rapidly developing in the tropical Pacific and could become the strongest recorded since at least 1950, according to computer model projections.

The climate pattern is already beginning to influence weather around the world, giving forecasters increased confidence in predicting potential conditions over the next one to two years, CNN reports.

El Niño occurs when ocean temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific become warmer than average, releasing large amounts of heat into the atmosphere and altering weather patterns far beyond the Pacific.

Scientists caution, however, that a record-strength El Niño does not necessarily mean every region will experience more extreme weather. Instead, a stronger event increases the likelihood that typical El Niño-related effects, known as “teleconnections,” will occur.

Potential impacts include drought in Indonesia and Australia, a drier-than-normal summer monsoon in India and varying risks of drought and heavy rainfall across parts of Africa.

Experts say the unusually strong and persistent signal could make seasonal weather patterns more predictable and provide governments with valuable time to prepare for potential heat waves, droughts, floods and disruptions to food supplies.

World.title: International News: Almost three-quarters of England declared in drought
World.content:
International News: Almost three-quarters of England declared in drought

By Zoila Palma: Nearly three-quarters of England has now been officially declared in drought as the country continues to experience historically dry and hot weather.

The National Drought Group said 71.3 percent of England is experiencing flash drought, with severe pressure on water resources affecting public supplies, agriculture, navigation and the environment.

The East Midlands, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire, Kent and East Sussex, and Solent and the South Downs were the latest regions placed under drought status. The North East and Yorkshire have been moved to prolonged dry weather status, the stage before drought, leaving no region in England classified as having normal water conditions.

The worsening water crisis follows provisional figures showing that England and Wales experienced their driest July since records began in 1836, with 19 English counties recording no rainfall during the entire month.

World.title: Taiwan, Belize strengthen Climate Resilience through Disaster Risk project
World.content:
Taiwan, Belize strengthen Climate Resilience through Disaster Risk project

By Zoila Palma: Taiwan and Belize are strengthening their partnership on climate resilience and disaster preparedness through initiatives aimed at improving flood monitoring and early warning systems.

In recent years, the Taiwan Technical Mission has partnered with the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change to establish nine flood monitoring stations and an early warning system covering flood-prone areas along Belize’s river basins.

Building on this mechanism, Taiwan and Belize officially launched the “Belize Multi-Hazard Risk Management Capacity Building Project” in February 2026.

The project seeks to expand Belize’s existing disaster prevention mechanisms to cover at least 70 percent of disaster-prone areas across the country.

Taiwan said it remains committed to working with Belize to strengthen the country’s capacity for disaster mitigation while reducing climate-related risks and vulnerabilities.

World.title: National Hurricane Center monitoring 3 disturbances in Atlantic
World.content:
National Hurricane Center monitoring 3 disturbances in Atlantic

By Zoila Palma: The National Hurricane Center (NHC) is monitoring three weather disturbances across the Atlantic, with one system having a 60 percent chance of developing into a tropical depression over the next seven days.

The first disturbance is located a few hundred miles south of the Cabo Verde Islands and is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. The system is expected to move westward and merge with a tropical wave currently over West Africa. The NHC gives it a 20 percent chance of formation within 48 hours and a 60 percent chance within seven days.

A second disturbance, associated with a tropical wave in the central tropical Atlantic, is located roughly midway between West Africa and the Lesser Antilles. Some gradual development is possible through midweek as it moves westward, but unfavorable upper-level winds are expected to limit development later in the week. It has a 10 percent chance of formation over both the next 48 hours and seven days.

The third disturbance is a trough of low pressure located several hundred miles northwest of Bermuda. It is expected to move eastward north of Bermuda, with a 10 percent chance of development over the next 48 hours and seven days.

The NHC said the system is expected to reach cooler waters later this week, ending its chances of development after Wednesday.

World.title: International News: Mexico, Peru to reestablish diplomatic relations
World.content:
International News: Mexico, Peru to reestablish diplomatic relations

By Zoila Palma: Mexico and Peru will reestablish diplomatic relations following an agreement described by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum as an act of “good will” by the Peruvian government.

Sheinbaum said the decision followed Peru’s granting of safe passage to Chávez, which she described as a gesture toward Mexico.

“With this [act of good will], relations with Peru are going to be reestablished,” Sheinbaum said during her Friday morning press conference, Mexico News daily reported.

Sheinbaum also reiterated Mexico’s support for former Peruvian President Pedro Castillo, whose 2022 removal from office she has previously described as a “coup.” She said Peru’s new government is aware that Mexico will continue defending Castillo.

World.title: BCWU says 84% of members no longer support BTL’s proposed acquisition of SMART
World.content:
BCWU says 84% of members no longer support BTL’s proposed acquisition of SMART

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Communications Workers’ Union (BCWU) says an overwhelming majority of its members have withdrawn their support for Belize Telemedia Limited’s proposed acquisition of Speednet Communications Limited, the company which operates SMART.

In a press release issued on Monday, August 10, the union said that following an emergency membership meeting on August 6, 84 percent of its members indicated that they no longer support the acquisition as it is currently proposed.

According to the BCWU, members had initially supported the acquisition during a BTL employee town hall on January 22, but only on the “express understanding” that concerns raised by the union would be adequately addressed. Those concerns included job security for existing BTL employees, the financial implications of the transaction, governance and disclosure issues, the integration of SMART employees, and whether those workers would be able to join the BCWU.

The union said it had also sought assurances that any acquisition would be conducted through a phased process with meaningful consultation involving the National Trade Union Congress of Belize (NTUCB). The BCWU says discussions continued with BTL management, but members remain concerned about what they consider insufficient information and consultation surrounding the proposed deal.

The development comes days after BTL’s Board of Directors approved management’s proposal to acquire 100 percent of Speednet’s issued share capital. BTL has placed the proposed investment at approximately $80 million, while stressing that the transaction is not yet final and remains subject to continued due diligence, negotiations and final approval of a Share Purchase Agreement. BTL has also said the transaction would not require additional borrowing or funding from the Social Security Board.

BTL has maintained that acquiring Speednet could reduce duplication of telecommunications infrastructure, improve reliability, expand connectivity and allow greater investment in underserved areas. Earlier this year, the company also told the public that job protection, current pricing and regulatory compliance were among the issues being considered as part of the proposed transaction.

The proposal has faced sustained scrutiny from unions and the business community. The Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry has called for the process to be halted pending greater financial disclosure and safeguards for competition, warning about the implications of bringing the country’s two major telecommunications providers under one ownership structure.

The BCWU says it will now align itself with the NTUCB in determining its next steps, insisting that BTL employees are stakeholders in the process and that their voices must be heard.

World.title: Smart opens new showroom in Caye Caulker
World.content:
Smart opens new showroom in Caye Caulker

By Zoila Palma: Smart officially opened its new showroom in Caye Caulker today offering residents and visitors access to Smart’s telecommunications services and special grand opening promotions.

The new showroom is located on Calle del Sol and features special offers to mark the opening, including a free SIM card for the first 10 customers.

Customers can also take advantage of Smart’s “Double Up or Triple Up” promotion, receiving double credit on purchases from $1 to $29.99 and triple credit on purchases of $30 or more.

The new showroom provides Caye Caulker residents with a convenient location to access Smart services and stay connected.

World.title: BWE organisers respond to viral fight video, reaffirms commitment to patron safety
World.content:
Videograb showing a brawl at a Best Weekend Ever beach event on Sunday, August 10, 2026.

ST ANN, Jamaica – The directors of party series Best Weekend Ever (BWE) has expressed disappointment and regret over a physical altercation involving patrons at its beach event on Sunday.

Videos of the incident have been widely circulated on social media, showing a group of men engaged in a brawl.

In a media release Monday, the party organisers said, “Best Weekend Ever has never condoned, and we abhor the proliferation of violence of any kind at our events.

“We are extremely disappointed and sincerely regret that this unfortunate and isolated situation has occurred,” the release continued. “We have contacted the family of those affected and the individuals involved in the altercation have been clearly identified, and the relevant actions will be pursued by the designated authority.”

According to the directors, over the years, BWE has established a strong track record of providing safe, well-managed entertainment experiences for thousands of patrons.

“The safety and security of our guests remain a priority, and this incident is not reflective of the culture of Best Weekend Ever or the experience we work diligently to provide,” they said.

The directors also sought to clarify that, contrary to some narratives circulating, the MC at the event “brought attention to the incident to allow the appropriate intervention to take place and we have made our team available to the relevant authorities to assist in the process of ensuring this does not reoccur.”

According to the release, throughout the staging of Best Weekend Ever 2026, the events have been enjoyed safely by thousands of patrons with improved traffic management and movement between events.

“We are also grateful for the positive feedback from patrons which is an indication of the high level of satisfaction with the production of the event series,” the organisers said.

“Additional security measures have been put in place for the final event being staged today,” they added. “We thank our patrons, partners, security teams and stakeholders for their support as we continue to remain committed to delivering an environment where everyone can celebrate responsibly and safely.”

World.title: Tropical depression could form in Atlantic by the end of the week
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — The United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is advising that a tropical depression could form in the Atlantic during the latter half of this week.

The NOAA says an area of low pressure located a few hundred miles south of the Cabo Verde Islands is producing disorganised showers and thunderstorms.

As this system moves slowly westward, a tropical wave currently over west Africa is expected to merge with it in a couple of days.

Environmental conditions are forecast to be more conducive for development by midweek, and a tropical depression could form during the latter half of this week while the system moves westward to west-northwestward across the central tropical Atlantic.

Formation chance through 48 hours is low at 20 per cent but formation chance through seven days is medium at 60 per cent.

World.title: Bold Bruce
World.content:
Former Prime Minister Bruce Golding

NEW YORK, USA — Former Jamaican Prime Minister Bruce Golding has earned the backing of many within the Diaspora community here for what is being described as his “bold, factual and truthful position” on the souring relationship between Jamaica and America, two staunch allies.



Speaking in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania last week, Golding expressed hopes that “the United States will soften the tone of its relationship with Jamaica and rekindle the strong, decades-old bond between both nations which Jamaicans cherish.

Saying that current demands by Washington are “at odds with the very essence of true friendship”, he pointed to the many challenges facing the island as established rules are being discarded and “new rules are being handed down, not after discussions and negotiations, but unilaterally by social media postings at 2:30 in the morning when most of us are asleep”.

The former Jamaican leader, who stepped away in 2011 and handed over the reins to now Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness, was addressing the annual Team Jamaica Bickle Independence Gala on Emancipation Day, August 1, 2026.

The gala celebrated Jamaica’s 64th anniversary of Independence and raised funds in support of Jamaican and other Caribbean athletes’ participation in the yearly Penn Relays in the US, a must-stop on the annual sports calendar for speedy Jamaican high school students.

Golding appeared to be voicing sentiments many Jamaicans in his US audience feel but could not express themselves. Some murmured among themselves that he must not fear losing his US visa.

Called to ask his view Sunday, Golding said he did not wish to trivialise the matter and he had said enough on the subject.
