NEW DELHI: Indiaâs installed clean energy generation capacity has crossed the 300GW mark, taking the country past 60% of its target of having 500GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.According to data released by renewable energy ministry, total non-fossil capacity stood at 300.5GW as on July 31, accounting for over 54% of total installed power generation capacity of around 552GW. Solar accounts for the largest share at 164.6GW, followed by large and small hydro at 57.2GW and wind at 58.1GW. Bio-power contributes nearly 11.8GW, while nuclear energy accounts for 8.8GW.The ministry said that a record 55.3GW of non-fossil capacity was added in 2025-26, including 44.6GW of solar and 6GW of wind capacity. Solar-led capacity addition rose from 2.8GW in 2014 to nearly 165GW now, while wind capacity has increased from 21GW to over 58GW during the same period.The rise in renewable capacity has also pushed up clean power generation, which increased from about 191 billion units in 2014-15 to 477.8 billion units in 2025-26.The ministry said domestic manufacturing capacity for renewable energy equipment has also expanded, with the approved list of models and manufacturers for solar PV modules crossing 200GW, compared with 2.3GW in 2014, helped by the production-linked incentive scheme for high-efficiency solar modules.Govt is also implementing National Green Hydrogen Mission to build capacity for production and use of green hydrogen and its derivatives, with the aim of reducing emissions from hard-to-abate sectors and cutting dependence on imported fossil fuels.

Having taken off with 43 eligible countries, the facility is now available to nationals of 172 countries.E-visa is presently issued under 17 sub-categories; namely tourist visa, mountaineering visa, business visa (six types), medical visa (four types), student visa (two types), transit visa, miscellaneous visa and group visitor visa (cruise).

World.title: Protesters march to Jharkhand Assembly; 5 injured in clashes
World.content:
Thousands of students and job aspirants from across Jharkhand marched towards the State Assembly in Ranchi on Monday (August 10, 2026), breaking through several barbed barricades and reaching the Assembly gates as their indefinite strike over alleged irregularities in government recruitment examinations entered its 17th day.

At least five protesters were injured, including one who suffered a head injury, after the police resorted to baton-charge and dispersed the crowd.

Also read: Jharkhand students protest updates on August 10, 2026

At present, the protesters are continuing their sit-in at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in the capital, seeking resolution of their demands.

The protesters are demanding cancellation of the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) examination and a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in the recruitment process. The march came a day after the Jharkhand government agreed to cancel three examinations, including the preliminary examination of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission Combined Civil Services.

As the protest continued, former JPSC chairman L. Khiangte was arrested in connection with the investigation. Mr. Khiangte, a former Chief Secretary, resigned as JPSC chairman on July 22 after the State CID took over the probe. The Enforcement Directorate has also begun investigating the alleged irregularities in multiple recruitment examinations, including JSSC-CGL, after taking cognisance of a State CID FIR and other complaints under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

The protest, which began around 10.30 a.m. near the old Assembly complex in Dhurwa, was largely peaceful initially. Carrying the Tricolour, placards and portraits of Bhagat Singh, Ambedkar, former Chief Minister Shibu Soren, and activist Nirmal Mahato, they walked towards the Assembly, chanting slogans against the government and demanding action. Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahato, who has been on a hunger strike for several days, was brought to the site on a stretcher. He followed the march in an ambulance for a brief while.

Tension arose after noon as protesters broke through barricades approached the new Assembly building, where the monsoon session was under way. The police then used water cannons, fired tear gas and resorted to baton-charge to disperse the crowd. Protesters retaliated by throwing bottles, slippers and shoes at the police. Several students also appeared unwell and some collapsed amid the intense heat.

Despite the police action, the JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch and JLKM leaders said their protest will not end till their demands are met. The agitation continued into the night, with protesters holding a sit-in near the Assembly complex. The police again used batons to disperse them and began chasing protesters out of the area, according to volunteer Sudhir Mahto.

A large number of security personnel from the Jharkhand Police, Jharkhand Jaguar, the Rapid Action Force and district forces, along with riot-control vehicles, were deployed in the area.

City Deputy Superintendent of Police Ajay Aryan denied that the police had resorted to a “deliberate lathi-charge”. “No force was used but the police had to push back to control the crowd and ensure that no one is injured. We won’t call it lathi-charge,” he said.

Mr. Aryan said police personnel had been given strict instructions not to use force. He said tear gas was fired from the side to minimise its impact.

Ranchi Superintendent of Police Paras Rana said the police action came after the protesters pushed the barricades. “Two constables sustained head injuries and required sutures,” he said.

Despite the clashes, protesters described the march a success and said they would continue their agitation until their demands are met.

World.title: Protectors turn predators: how son preference fuels female foeticide rackets in Maharashtra
World.content:
A man once tasked with saving Maharashtra’s daughters has now been unmasked as one of their most prolific predators.

For decades, Dr. Chandrakant Gunda Gaikwad sat comfortably within the upper echelons of the State health establishment, serving as a district civil surgeon and assistant director. He was also part of the government’s ‘Save the Girls’ campaign for years.

Retirement did not signal an end to his medical career, but marked the expansion of a dark underground enterprise. Dr. Gaikwad was arrested by the Kolhapur police on July 31 for allegedly orchestrating a sophisticated female foeticide ring. During interrogation, he allegedly admitted to performing around 200 to 250 illegal abortions, the police said.

The racket operated out of Kolhapur in western Maharashtra, the home district of State Health Minister Prakash Abitkar. The Minister called it a “serious matter” that a former health official was involved in such a crime. He announced that the State will soon introduce a new law to invoke the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act against female foeticide, ensuring that doctors, family members, pharmacists, and anyone else supporting the crime face prosecution.

However, when mediapersons pressed the Minister about how implicated doctors and individuals routinely escape punishment and continue running their rackets after securing bail, he had no concrete answer. It underscored a grim reality: culprits easily slip through the cracks and accountability remains elusive.

According to Sunanda Patil, an octogenarian and resident of Kolhapur, female foeticide “is nothing new”. She said women face two choices: empty their wombs if it is a girl, or keep giving birth until a son is born. She chose the second option, delivering three daughters before finally having a son. She considers herself lucky that her husband stopped there.

Quiet tragedies

For daily wage worker Maloji Kharat and his agricultural worker wife Lankabai, the reality was starkly different. By 38, Ms. Lankabai had 21 pregnancies and struggled to recall the names of all her children. Of her 11 surviving children, nine are girls. The other 10 died either shortly after birth or during delivery. When their story was reported a few years ago, the couple vanished from public view.

Beed district in the Marathwada region has long carried a dark reputation for illegal abortion rings. The most notorious was run by Dr. Sudam Munde and Dr. Saraswati Munde from Parali who operated a sex determination racket for years.

In one of the most chilling revelations, investigators found that the Mundes fed aborted female foetuses to a pack of dogs to hide the evidence, reportedly aborting up to 20 female foetuses a day for decades.

Beed-based activist Manisha Tokale noted that it has been over a decade since the Munde case, yet illegal abortion networks continue to operate in secret. The issue makes headlines briefly when a case is uncovered, she said, before things slip right back to normal.

This generational pressure drives quiet tragedies across the State. After delivering two sons, Renu (name changed) became pregnant a third time. Her husband, a daily wage worker, expected another boy. Fearing that her family history of having only daughters meant she would carry the same genes, he routinely took her for ultrasound tests.

“We went, had a sonography, and the family suggested abortion,” Ms. Renu said, without needing to specify that the third child was a girl. Phrases like “khali karun ye (empty it and come back)” or “tapasun baghu (let us check)” echo across both rural and urban Maharashtra. When she went to a private clinic in Beed for the abortion, the doctor botched the procedure. She said the clean-up was not done properly, leaving her with lasting physical pain and nowhere to turn for justice.

According to Roopa Shah, founder of the Kolhapur-based Dilasa Samajik Vishwast Sanstha, female foeticide happens everywhere in the State without exception.

Society’s mindset has not changed, regardless of whether people live in rural or urban areas, or are rich or poor, she said.

Having spent three decades fighting crimes like child marriage and female foeticide, Ms. Shah feels conventional measures have utterly failed. Because the police, courts, administration, and government have not been able to stop these atrocities, she believes the time has come for women to take a stand themselves. “It is not easy though,” she said.

Deep-rooted bias

The National Family Health Survey 2019-21 offers a window into the mindset of this social fabric. Maharashtra has shown a strong preference for sons. While 9% of women and 12% of men express a desire for more sons than daughters, only 4-5% of women and men want more daughters. A large majority of women and men wish to have at least one son while fewer desire at least one daughter. These figures capture a deep-rooted gender bias in the State, one that starts at birth and follows girls throughout their lives.

“Those who survive have to carry the burden of being a girl forever,” said Dhondabai Ningule, a resident of Dharashiv district.

In Marathi households, names like Dhondabai, derived from dhonda (stone), or Nakushi (unwanted) are often given to girls born merely as stopgap arrangements until a son arrives, serving as a constant, grudging reminder from their families of their unwanted existence.

World.title: Day after JNU nixed discussion on Khalid’s book, students’ union holds event outdoors
World.content:
A day after Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) cancelled permission to hold an auditorium discussion on a book by former student Umar Khalid, the students’ union went ahead with the plan and held the talk outdoors on Monday. Despite the rain, students turned out in large numbers for the event held from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. outside the School of Social Sciences 2 to discuss Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power. The talk was held amid protests by the RSS-linked Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, whose members chanted slogans calling Mr. Khalid a “terrorist”. The former JNU student is lodged in Tihar Jail in the 2020 north-east Delhi riots ‘larger conspiracy’ case and has been awaiting trial for nearly six years. Some students raised objections to the absence of tribal community members from the panel to discuss a book on Adivasis.

'Hypocritical stance’

Students from other colleges also attended the discussion. Delhi University student Aryan Singh said while he was at first sceptical about travelling all the way due to reports about the last-minute cancellation, he decided to come anyway. “I had to turn up because he [Mr. Khalid] has been waiting six years for a trial. It is hypocritical that the same JNU where he completed his research is trying to erase his thesis,” he said. ABVP member Rajeshwar Kant Dubey said, “We have clarified our stance. If the government thinks that Umar Khalid is a terrorist, then who is the JNUSU to give him a clean chit? Th The discussion featured Professor Prabhu Mahapatra, historian Uma Chakravarti, Shuddhabrata Sengupta, Harsh Mander and Banojyotsana Lahiri. The panellists spoke about the book, the method, and Mr. Khalid’s approach to the subject. Volunteers sold copies at the venue. JNU student Aniket, who purchased the book, said, “I genuinely wanted to read the thesis to see how he perceives the world. Secondly, I wanted to see how a good academic thesis is written, especially as many are now filled with plagiarism and AI slop.” Following the discussion, JNUSU joint secretary Danish Ali said it was difficult to organise the talk because of pressure from the administration. “We had all the necessary permissions, and it was cancelled at the last minute on a Sunday, which is not even a working day for them [administration]”. On Sunday, the administration announced the cancellation of the discussion scheduled at the auditorium of the School of Social Sciences 1 citing “non-disclosure of full facts about the programme” and inviting criticism from the JNUSU. Birsa Ambedkar Phule Students’ Association president Kranthi Kumar said that while they oppose the incarceration of political prisoners and stifling of dissent, they agree with the objections regarding the absence of Adivasi teachers and students from the panel.

World.title: SP fears BSP the most, says Akash Anand, asks voters to be wary
World.content:
Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national coordinator Akash Anand on Monday claimed the Samajwadi Party (SP) fears his party the most. “Samajwadi Party fears BSP the most. It was [party chief] Mayawatiji who worked the most for the uplift of Dalits. That’s why SP members keep shouting ‘PDA, PDA’,” he said at a party workers’ conference in Hathras, referring to the SP’s Pichchda, Dalit, Alpsankhyank or Backwards, Dalits and minorities plank. “Mayawatiji always cautions people from all walks of life to be wary of the deceptive SP and its narrow casteist politics,” added Mr. Anand.

Targeting BJP

The BSP leader also accused the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Uttar Pradesh government of failing on employment, education and law and order, and alleged that more than ₹7,000 crore had been spent on s over the past decade to “hide its shortcomings”. “More than four lakh government posts are lying vacant in the State while several competitive examinations witnessed paper leaks,” he said.

World.title: Punjab passes nine Bills in a day; Oppn. calls it a ‘display of majoritarian arrogance’
World.content:
Opposition parties in Punjab lashed out at the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government after nine Bills were passed in the House on Monday, describing the exercise as a “display of majoritarian arrogance”.

The State Assembly passed nine Bills pertaining to various sectors, including education, infrastructure, taxation, and employment, rural development and environmental protection.

The Bill included the Punjab Common Infrastructure (Regulation and Maintenance) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Punjab Regulation of Fee of Un-aided Educational Institutions (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Punjab Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Bill, 2026, the Punjab Panchayati Raj (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Punjab Protection of Trees Bill, 2026.

The House also passed three Bills pertaining to universities, including the Cloud University, Hoshiarpur Bill, 2026, the MS Digital University, Patiala Bill, 2026 and the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Bill, 2026.

‘Gross insult’

Bharatiya Janata Party’s Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon called it “a gross insult to Punjab’s legislative system and democracy”. He said passing Bills that could have far-reaching consequences for the lives of the people of Punjab without giving legislators adequate time to read, understand, and scrutinise is not law-making. “Rather, it is a display of the arrogance of the majority,” he said.

“If nine Bills are introduced in the House and passed immediately on the same day, when will any legislator read their provisions, when will they understand them, and when will they discuss them with the people of their respective constituencies?,” he quipped.

Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring in a post on X said: “On the very last day of the Assembly session, Congress MLAs were handed nine Bills this morning. This is nothing short of a joke with democracy. The government expects the Opposition to study, scrutinise and debate nine bills without even giving us adequate time to read them. This is not legislation, this is an attempt to bypass democratic scrutiny. Why is the Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann so scared of debate? We strongly oppose this hypocrisy and this blatant disregard for democratic legislative procedure.”

World.title: Suvendu admits police negligence in custodial death of TMC worker
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday visited the residence of Trinamool Congress (TMC) worker Birju Keot, who died in police custody at Halisahar in North 24 Parganas district, and announced compensation for his family.

Keot died in police custody on August 8, and his family has alleged that the police tortured him to death. The Chief Minister said a magistrate-level investigation would be conducted into the death in police custody “as per protocol” laid down for custodial death.

Mr. Adhikari said the investigating officer behind the arrest of the deceased has been suspended, and the officer-in-charge of the police station has been “closed” to Barrackpore Police lines. The State government has announced a compensation of ₹10 lakh and a job for the wife of the deceased.

Complaint to CM

Mr. Adhikari said the death had occurred in custody, and that police negligence was “clear as daylight”. Jenny Sharma Keot, wife of Birju Keot, and a former TMC councillor, said more than compensation, she wants justice for her husband. She submitted a complaint to the CM.

“I have expressed gratitude to the family on behalf of the government. They did not allow anyone to do politics over the death. The former Chief Minister [referring to Mamata Banerjee] came. But the family did not even meet her. The deceased’s elder brother told the former Chief Minister that they want justice, and only the administration can grant the family justice. They have trusted the government and the administration. This is a big debt to us,” the West Bengal Chief Minister said.

Vehicle attacked

Ms. Banerjee, the TMC chairperson and former CM, had visited the residence on Sunday. During the visit, her vehicle was attacked, and she claimed it was a conspiracy to kill her. Locals gathered at the site and raised slogans against Ms. Banerjee.

Mr. Adhikari said the police had provided Ms. Banerjee adequate protection, and the sloganeering was a result of public anger.

Supporters of Ms. Banerjee held protests across the city on Monday. Trinamool MLAs who have stayed with the former Chief Minister also staged a protest in the State Assembly over the attack.

World.title: Haryana power employees defer strike by two months after government assurances
World.content:
The Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Struggle Front on Monday deferred its three-day Statewide strike, scheduled from August 11 to August 13, by two months following an agreement with the Haryana government on several demands of power employees.

The decision was taken after a more than five-hour meeting between representatives of the Joint Struggle Front and the State government, chaired by Energy Minister Anil Vij.

As part of the understanding reached at the meeting, the government deferred the proposed launch of the Agriculture Distribution Company (DISCOM), which had been scheduled for August 15. Mr. Vij said there was currently no such proposal before the Ministry of Power and assured the employees’ representatives that the government would not take the matter forward in future without consulting the Joint Struggle Front and other stakeholders.

He said that although the proposal had been announced by the Chief Minister in the budget speech, no concrete action had been initiated at the departmental level so far. Mr. Vij added that he had also not held any formal discussion with the Chief Minister on the issue.

On the issue of a proposed parallel electricity distribution licence for Nuh and Gurugram, the government agreed to oppose the petition filed by a private company before the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC). The Energy Department had opposed the proposal from the outset and that the department’s objection had been approved at his level, said Mr. Vij.

The government also assured the Joint Struggle Front that no tender would be issued for the smart metering scheme in future. The Minister said consumers would continue to have the option of choosing between prepaid and postpaid smart meters.

Following the assurances, the Joint Struggle Front gave the government two months to implement the decisions agreed upon during the meeting.

World.title: 2,500 homeless children mapped across Delhi ahead of ‘Child Beggar-Free Delhi’ campaign
World.content:
The Delhi Police has mapped around 2,500 children found begging at public places and major road intersections to support the Delhi government’s soon to be launched ‘Child Beggar-Free Delhi’ campaign, which aims to rescue and rehabilitate them. The campaign will be implemented across all 13 districts.

The survey was conducted by the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC) from July 1 to July 31 as part of ‘Child Safety Month’.

Speaking to The Hindu, Deputy Commissioner of Police (SPUWAC) Neha Yadav said the survey focused exclusively on children who were completely shelterless, including those living on the streets or under flyovers without even a jhuggi to stay in. Yadav said children’s latitude and longitude coordinates, and photographs will be shared with the Department of Women and Child Development and the Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) to help initiate the ‘Child Beggar-Free Delhi’ campaign. The survey found that most of the children were located in West Delhi.

DCP Yadav said the proposed campaign will address both the homelessness of children and their vulnerability to crimes like snatching and working as couriers for drug peddlers. “If these children are taken in another direction and provided shelter and education, these crimes can also be controlled to an extent,” she said.

On Saturday (August 8), Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government, in coordination with the DCPCR and non-governmental organisations, would counsel families, understand their difficulties and provide better alternatives for such children rather than forcibly removing them from the streets. The drive will also seek to identify and prosecute organised gangs allegedly forcing children into begging, while ensuring that the children receive support to secure their future, Gupta said.

World.title: Govt leaves petrol, diesel prices unchanged for Aug 11
World.content:
The government on Monday kept the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel unchanged as Platts prices were not published on August 10.

Petrol will continue to be sold at Rs327.62 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 11.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact ‘entirely for defensive purposes’, not aggression: PM Shehbaz
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday affirmed that the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz recalled that he, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact in Makkah on Friday.

The prime minister stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

“Its purpose is definitely not that any aggression occurs. It is entirely for defensive purposes, for peace, tranquillity and progress in the region,” he affirmed.

“I believe this agreement is a source of strength not just among these three countries, but for the entire Muslim ummah,” he noted.

PM Shehbaz particularly felicitated Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar as well as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir on the signing of the agreement.

Efforts for the joint defence pact had been underway for “many years and materialised this Friday”, the prime minister said.

He noted that while Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already entered the “Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement” in September 2025, Islamabad and Ankara also had “arrangements for decades” between them.

PM Shehbaz recalled that the Pakistani nation and the army had been honoured to “defend the world’s holiest places” of Makkah and Madina for years along with the Saudi forces.

“Last year, with Allah’s grace, this arrangement was officially recognised so that a proper agreement was signed. Friday’s agreement is another extension of it, with a trilateral agreement signed.”

In a statement issued by the Foreign Office earlier in the day, Dar felicitated the nation on the agreement’s signing. He reiterated his comments from Sunday wherein he said the pact was defensive in nature and not directed against any country.

Dar also noted that the term of treating an attack on one of them as an attack against all three was “consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter”.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait, Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

‘Once in power, AJK govt will offer dialogue to those willing’

Speaking on Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), PM Shehbaz favoured dialogue with protesters who have been at odds with the authorities over the 12 seats reserved for refugees and other issues, leading to a tense situation in the region for the past two months.

He said that once the new government comes to power in AJK — with PML-N already claiming a two-thirds majority — the matter of continuing talks with the protesters “will progress”.

The prime minister declared that those “who only want to cause anarchy will not be allowed to do so, but those who want to peacefully and patiently discuss the situation, the new government will provide a chance for that”.

“In any respected society, no permission can be given for lawlessness. If there is any demand or any matters, they should be resolved through talks at a table,” he said.

PM Shehbaz went on to say that the government had “clear evidence that those who purposefully worsened the situation there were working on the directives of the enemy”.

He recalled that despite that, the government had held a multi-party conference in Muzaffarabad before the elections, with only one political party being absent — apparently referring to the PTI which has boycotted the polls.

“Every aspect was discussed there, and […] those who wanted refugee seats to be changed, reduced or abolished were advised to let the elections go on as planned and bring forward their case in the new assembly,” he said, adding that this would resolve the matter as per the constitution of AJK.

“All matters were settled, but they remained adamant on this and needlessly insisted, which unfortunately worsened the situation,” the prime minister said.

Speaking about the ongoing elections in AJK, PM Shehbaz asserted that Kashmiris have “overwhelmingly voted” for his PML-N.

The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats out of a total 45 — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The third phase of elections in Poonch Division began today.

The prime minister noted that based on the results from Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions, along with the seats reserved for refugees from India-held Kashmir, the PML-N has “almost established a majority”.

“This vote is a vote of trust in Mian Nawaz Sharif and for his leadership. I am hopeful that once we set up a government there, under his leadership, AJK will once again set out on the journey to progress and prosperity,” he said, thanking those who voted for his party.

‘Terrorists being annihilated day and night’

At the federal cabinet meeting, PM Shehbaz also touched upon the issue of terrorism in the country and mentioned the lives lost in recent terrorist attacks.

He noted that terrorists escalated their activities in “some areas of Pakistan in the past few days”.

The premier recalled the August 2 Swat suicide bombing that claimed 17 lives and the martyrdom of Deputy Superintendent of Police Diyar Khan in an attack on a Hangu police checkpost.

He paid tribute to the sacrifices of the personnel, including Captain Hamza Akram and Major Hafiz Ihsan Elahi, who were martyred during operations in Hangu and North Waziristan, respectively.

The prime minister affirmed that “Fitna Al Khawarij are being annihilated day and night”, referring to terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

“These sacrifices will not go in vain and will bear fruition. One day will come when Pakistan will once again be free from terrorism and will move rapidly towards peace and progress,” PM Shehbaz said.

The prime minister also expressed his condolences over the death of PML-N MNA Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar, describing him as a “longtime friend”.

“He was a person who was a supporter in bad times,” he said, adding that he and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif knew Channar since 1985. The cabinet also prayed for the elevated ranks of the martyrs and Channar.

World.title: 3rd phase of AJK elections: PML-N poised for gains in Poonch amid rigging allegations
World.content:
The PML-N appeared set to gain at least one seat in Poonch division, where four constituencies went to the polls on Monday amid allegations of rigging, violence and disruption, with polling suspended at some places.

The biggest upset was the defeat of Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan in LA-14 (Dhirkot), a constituency from where he, and before him his uncle and father, had been elected in all nine elections since 1985.

His defeat also appeared to underscore the political decline of what was once the largest and longest-ruling party in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), but was reduced to a marginal force following the emergence of the PML-N in 2010.

Khan was defeated by Sajid Iqbal Abbasi, who contested his first election on the ticket of the little-known Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party, by a margin of more than 21,000 votes, according to unofficial and unverified results from 213 of the 214 polling stations.

Observers attributed Abbasi’s victory largely to his hands-on efforts for the development of the constituency and the welfare of its residents, which, they said, had helped him build a personal support base over the years.

PML-N’s Raja Faisal Azad and PPP’s Raja Mubashar Ejaz secured 3,000 and 2,800 votes, respectively.

In another closely watched contest in LA-17 (Haveli), a neck-and-neck fight was under way between Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore and PML-N candidate Engr Chaudhry Mohsin Aziz. Initial reports suggested that Aziz had established a sizeable lead, but it later emerged that results from nearly two dozen polling stations were still awaited.

Independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, who had initially been tipped to finish second, was trailing far behind.

In LA-15 (Bagh Central), Jamaat-i-Islami’s Brig (retd) Dr Mohammad Khan was initially reported to be heading for victory, but the contest later narrowed to a two-way race between PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas and PPP’s Sardar Ziaul Qamar. Late-night unofficial and unverified results showed Qamar establishing a clear lead of 2,000 votes over Mr Minhas.

Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) president and former AJK prime minister Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who had won the constituency in the 2021 election on a PTI ticket, appeared to be out of the race.

In LA-16 (Bagh East), PML-N’s Sardar Mir Akbar was leading PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman, who is the father of the PPP candidate in LA-15 and has served as an AJK minister in several PPP governments. Akbar had secured 14,900 votes, while Mr Qamar had polled 10,960.

Results from 14 polling stations were awaited.

Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Citing law and order concerns, the Election Commission had decided to postpone polling in Bagh and Sudhnoti districts that was originally set for today.

Polling began at 8am and continued until 5pm in four Poonch constituencies. The PPP, which has accused the PML-N of rigging in the previous phases, continued to make similar allegations on Monday as well.

In response, PML-N leaders said the PPP had no evidence for its claims, and reiterated their confidence to form the government in AJK based on the seats it has already secured so far.

The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. On the other hand, the PPP has only won 10 constituencies so far.

The third phase of the AJK elections was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Government officials had anticipated clashes in some areas today, while the Election Commission had classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive.

“Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier

Malpractice, rigging allegations

Polling in previous phases of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging, scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — the main contenders in AJK but allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words.

The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging and electoral malpractices in the previous phases. It continued to allege rigging in Haveli and Bagh as well.

In a series of posts on X, the PPP shared complaints it said it had filed to the Election Commission.

In one of the complaints, the PPP alleged that roads leading to the Banni Marasira area had been blocked, where PML-N supporters were illegally stamping ballot papers at 12 polling stations in the LA-15 constituency.

“The commission is requested to consider the two acts together rather than separately, because the second is made possible by the first,” the party said, adding that officials, voters, polling agents and party workers were unable to reach the polling stations “to see what is being done inside”.

The party also claimed delays in polling at LA-15’s polling station no.87 in Thub. It also alleged that polling at stations no.143 and 144 in Hatala Pader did not commence on time due to the non-arrival of polling staff.

The PPP also alleged that its polling agent was “forcibly removed” from LA-15’s station no.158 in Makhdoom Kot. Similarly, PPP’s agents had also been removed from polling stations no.8-14 in Bani Maldhara and PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers at those stations, the party alleged.

At around 12:45, the party claimed on X that workers of Jamaat-i-Islami had gathered to “capture” 26 polling stations in the constituency — nos.31-38, nos.70-79 and nos.180-186. It said the police had initially arrived but then withdrew.

“The stations are, therefore, unguarded at this moment, with an organised body assembled against them.”

It urged the Election Commission to determine on whose orders police had withdrawn and direct the law enforcers to return to the station.

The PPP also posted a blurry video, which it said was of PML-N workers “attacking” the polling station set up at the Boys Middle School in LA-15 Central Bagh.

Regarding LA-16, the party claimed that its polling agents were not being allowed inside stations no.119 and 120 while PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers inside the stations in the agents’ absence.

The PPP further alleged delays in polling at stations no.61 and 141 of the constituency.

It made similar allegations regarding polling stations no.109 and 110 in LA-16 Bagh-III Sharqi. Moreover, the party accused “armed individuals associated with the PML-N” of opening fire at polling station no.179, Kot Chinalla in the constituency and disrupting the election process.

“The polling agents of the PPP have been removed from the station. It is further alleged that ballot papers are being stamped lawfully,” the PPP added.

In LA-17, the party alleged that its agents had been “forced out” from the polling station in Mullah Basti, Kahuta City by PML-N workers.

PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman expressed reservations after reports of rigging and malpractices emerged, saying that preventing polling agents from entering polling stations in LA-16 raised “serious questions” about the transparency of the election process.

In a statement, she demanded that an explanation be sought from the presiding officers of stations nos.119 and 120 on the matter.

The senator also called for the Election Commission to take notice of the reports of PPP’s polling agent being removed from station no.158 in LA-15.

Rehman further demanded alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortage of polling staff and material, calling on the authorities to ensure that free and transparent elections were held at all polling stations without any disruption.

PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari also accused the PML-N of continuing rigging in the third phase of the elections. He highlighted that his party was regularly informing the Election Commission about the alleged rigging via phone.

But, “the chief election commissioner and the election commission secretary’s reply to all of our complaints has been that nothing has happened and everything is good,” he claimed.

When Dawn approached the Election Commission regarding Bokhari’s claim, Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel said any complaint that he or the chief election commissioner received was being attended and responded to, and the Quick Response Force (QRF) was also moved over it.

‘AJK’s people have supported PML-N’

Responding to PPP’s allegations, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said the rival party had not provided any proof for its claims.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad flanked by Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, Sanaullah denied that a comparatively high turnout could be considered proof of rigging.

The PML-N leader explained that a strong family and tribe system in AJK prompted people to show up for their relatives.

“Our opposing candidate Chaudhry Yasin was complaining yesterday that in his opposing candidate’s union council (UC), 80pc votes were cast, whereas in his own UC, 96pc votes were cast,” Sanaullah claimed.

Sanaullah asserted that balloting had gone fairly smoothly in Bagh and Haveli today.

He, however, detailed a few reported incidents. In Haveli, people tried to snatch documents from the polling agents in one station, but the Quick Response Force (QRF) promptly responded and resolved the situation without incident, according to Sanaullah.

In Bagh, some people, whom Sanaullah claimed were PPP workers, tried to halt polling at three stations. QRF responded there as well and resumed polling, the minister added.

Meanwhile, Muqam urged PPP to review the number of people attending their rallies instead of accusing others of rigging, insisting that PPP lacked support from the people of AJK.

“AJK’s people have supported PML-N,” Muqam asserted.

Disputing PPP’s recent stance that it was against phased elections, Muqam said the party had mentioned no reservations when the election schedule was first announced.

Sanaullah also backed Muqam, saying that PPP had not raised concerns when the Election Commission had originally sought consent from all parties for phased elections.

He further claimed that upon PPP’s insistence, the electoral watchdog had scheduled voting on the 12 refugee seats in the second phase of the elections.

Sanaullah contended that PPP did not want election results from the refugee seats in the rest of Pakistan to impact its numbers in AJK polls since PPP had not even canvassed in those places.

Speaking about the recent unrest in the region, Sanaullah expressed hope that the protests would end once the third phase of elections concludes, as protesters had “only aimed to stop elections”.

The new AJK government, which he said PML-N would form with a two-thirds majority, will respond to the protesters’ “valid demands”, the PML-N leader added.

However, he also warned that those who “took up arms and instigated the people of AJK, while acting on the directions of the enemy… will have to face the law and answer for their crimes”.

In response to a reporter’s question about PPP’s claim that PML-N only had numbered days of rule in the Centre, Sanaullah expressed hope that after the AJK elections, PPP would “open-heartedly” congratulate PML-N.

Meanwhile, PML-N’s AJK chapter secretary general Tariq Farooq — who also emerged as the winner in LA-7 recently — said allegations of “rigging, violence, coercion, or fake voting” emerging from the constituency of Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore were a “serious question of constitutional governance”.

“This is no longer merely an electoral dispute. It becomes a serious question of constitutional governance, democratic values, and the sanctity of the people’s vote,” Farooq wrote on X.

“I find it difficult to believe that the prime minister of Azad Jammu & Kashmir could consider himself above the Constitution, the law, and basic ethical obligations merely to secure his own election,” he said, without providing further details.

The PML-N candidate asserted that “public mandate must be secured through a free, fair and transparent election, not through power, influence or state authority”.

Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test

In Monday’s polls, AJK PM Rathore, who is from the PPP, and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls.

Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine.

In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council.

Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals.

Aziz, whose father Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign.

Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans.

Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister.

The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties.

In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), ex-PM Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist.

Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.”

Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan.

Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition.

In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively.

The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC).

Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following.

Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe.

Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position.

Additional reporting by Tariq Naqash

World.title: PTI leadership, TTAP on board for September 27 long march to Islamabad: Sohail Afridi
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday said PTI’s political leadership and its ally, the Tehreek Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP), were on board with the call for a long march to Islamabad on September 27.

Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, CM Afridi said, “The PTI’s political leadership across the country and its ally, the TTAP, are all on board with the long march, and they collectively agreed on September 27 as the date for it.”

Responding to a question about Imran Khan’s sister Aleema Khan’s reservations over the date, he said she was a “non-political individual” and would agree to the date once the PTI apprised her of all the facts and figures.

CM Afridi also denied allegations by a PTI member currently residing outside Pakistan that he had met Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi before finalising the date for the long march.

“That allegation was rubbish. At the time of the alleged meeting, I was at KP House in Islamabad, contrary to the claim that I had met him in Peshawar,” he said.

In response to a question, CM Afridi also rejected the impression of a communication gap between the party’s leadership and workers.

Talking about the ‘D-Chowk, D-Chowk’ slogans during the recent Peshawar rally, he said institutions that were not granting political space to the PTI should understand that the party’s leadership had taken on a great burden by seeking to resolve issues through mutual understanding.

“However, not just in KP but across Pakistan, particularly the youth, no one will be able to contain them when they come out on Sept 27, because I can see passion and a ray of light in their eyes,” the chief minister said.

During the interview, the KP chief minister also criticised the federal government led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for economic inefficiency and bad governance.

He said that if he met the PTI founder at Adiala jail and was instructed to defer the Sept 27 date for the long march, he would agree.

CM Afridi added that he would also follow Imran’s instructions if asked to pave the way for talks.

At the outset of his interview, Afridi said the PTI had no option but to protest as its grievances were not being heard by the authorities.

“People say that the PTI does politics of chaos, unrest and protests; however, it would not have resorted to these if it had been heard by the authorities.”

He claimed Imran had been jailed unlawfully. “The PTI founder is in solitary confinement and denied his rights. No one is allowed to meet him — not me, his family, lawyers or personal physicians.”

After exhausting all constitutional and legal means, he said, the PTI had no other option but to protest.

“We are holding a peaceful protest. The Constitution allows us to do so, so the authorities will have to hear us.”

He reiterated that the PTI wanted justice for its founder and wanted his cases to be heard on merit, with access to his personal doctors and quality medical treatment.

He further claimed that the KP police had faced interference from the federal government and other institutions.

The chief minister also distanced the provincial government from cases registered against journalists in KP, saying it would never allow such actions.

On a proposal to create new provinces in Pakistan, CM Afridi said it was the PTI founder’s vision to establish new administrative units across the country.

“But the question is: who will create them? Only a government with a mandate can do so,” he said, adding, “We support the call for creating new administrative units, but only through a government brought to power by the people.”

Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023 — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in the £190m case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

An accountability court in Islamabad had sentenced Imran and Bushra to 14 and seven years in prison, respectively, on Jan 17, 2025, in the case. Subsequently, both had challenged their convictions before the IHC.

World.title: New investigation team initiates formal proceedings into Mir Raza Ali murder
World.content:
A new investigation team formed by the Sindh IGP on Monday initiated formal proceedings into the murder of business owner Mir Raza Ali, following the findings of a second post-mortem examination.

Owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

The deceased’s family, along with their lawyer, Jibran Nasir, met members of the new investigation team at the DIG Crime office. The team also met investigators from the previous team and obtained records related to the case.

DIG Crime and Investigation Amir Farooqi, who heads the new team, told Dawn that the investigators heard the family and their lawyer in detail about the circumstances surrounding Ali’s murder.

“The police will keep the family informed of all steps being taken to solve the case,” he said.

He said the new team had obtained the investigation records from the previous team to review the entire case file.

Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said earlier today that the provincial government had deferred the decision on the formation of a judicial commission to probe the Mir Raza Ali murder case.

Lanjar made the announcement on X, saying that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab had spoken to Ali’s family, who had expressed “confidence in the new police team” constituted to investigate the case and was of the view that it should conduct the probe.

“Therefore, the decision of establishing a judicial commission has been deferred for the time being,” the home minister said.

While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report after the exhumation and a second postmortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

Controversy fueled by ‘miscommunication’

Sindh Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho said that the investigation into the murder should be conducted in a better manner, expressing hope that the new investigation team would consider all available evidence.

Speaking to the media in Sukkur, he said the government, public and police were all concerned about the case and stressed the need to examine it “with an open mind and open heart”.

He said action had been taken against officers found guilty of misconduct and negligence during the investigation.

IG Odho said the controversy surrounding Ali’s murder had been fuelled by “miscommunication”.

“I have strictly instructed the entire investigation team to keep communication open and transparent this time, whether with the deceased’s family or the media,” he said.

On Sunday, PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission to probe the case, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Lanjar and Wahab had reached Ali’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar had said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case.

However, Jibran Nasir, the family’s lawyer, posted on X that they had not requested or consented to any judicial commission.

“Nor do we believe it’s required at this stage. A new investigation team has been formed, which the family will meet tomorrow. The Sindh government should not try to create hurdles/confusion in the name of ‘facilitation,’“ he said.

He had earlier also objected to the initially constituted police team probing the case and demanded that it be replaced.

Speaking to the media on Saturday after the results of the second autopsy came out, he had said that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team.

Subsequently, the Sindh inspector general of police’s office notified on Sunday the reconstitution of the investigating team probing the case. The order to this effect said the new investigation team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem.

The same day, Karachi police chief Azad Khan also suspended Sharea Faisal Sub-divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after Ali’s body was found.

The city police chief also ordered the case be transferred to Zaman Town Police Station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was initially registered.

Controversy over autopsy

The latest developments in the case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel last week that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday.

After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said.

She said the body bore “injuries in the right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in the mouth and throat”.

World.title: At least 100 killed after powerful earthquake hits western Colombia
World.content:
At least 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia early on Monday, knocking down buildings across several cities and injuring at least 87 more, with still others trapped in the rubble.

The quake struck just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis, with memories still fresh of devastating twin earthquakes in neighboring Venezuela in June.

The Colombian geological service and its American counterpart, the US Geological Survey, put the magnitude at 7.4. Colombia had initially put it at 6.6.

The quake, according to USGS, struck at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar, in Choco, a sparsely populated province on Colombia’s Pacific Coast, but was felt in major cities nationwide.

“Significant casualties and damage are likely and the disaster is potentially widespread,” the agency warned.

The highest reported death toll was in the western province of Risaralda in Colombia’s coffee-growing region, where Governor Juan Diego Patino, speaking by phone to Caracol Television, reported 42 fatalities.

In the province’s capital of Pereira, social media images showed a building with a cracked facade crash to the ground, sending up a dark cloud of dust and debris as onlookers on the street darted away. The impact also toppled one of the towers atop a Gothic-style cathedral in Manizales, and forced nurses in Cali to wheel patients outside in hospital beds, social media and television images showed.

Residents and emergency personnel dig through the debris of a partially collapsed building after an earthquake, in Pereira, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — Reuters

In Pereira, Mayor Mauricio Salazar said 18 people had died. “The situation is critical,” he told Caracol Radio.

In nearby Manizales, Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas said three people were killed.

One person died in Buenaventura, Colombia’s main Pacific port, when a building collapsed, trapping several people, Mayor Ligia del Carmen Cordoba said.

Cali, one of Colombia’s biggest cities, was among the worst hit, though authorities have yet to confirm deaths there. Mayor Alejandro Eder told Caracol at least 30 buildings had collapsed and rescue crews were working at 10 of them.

“At this point, two people have already been rescued alive, one elderly woman and one young girl. There are more people trapped,” Eder told Blu Radio earlier. “We have at least 12 critical points and 25 collapsed structures that we are responding to.”

He added that the city had asked authorities in Bogota and Medellin to send disaster teams to support rescue efforts.

Caracol showed firefighters and Colombian Red Cross workers carrying a survivor on a stretcher from one collapsed building.

“The building completely collapsed. It sounded like a bomb. It was horrible,” Juan Carlos Osorio told Caracol Television as he helped remove debris from a collapsed structure in Cali. “All of us neighbors are working together, forming human chains. We need heavy equipment. There are many people trapped.”

An elderly woman is carried on furniture near a collapsed building after an earthquake in Cali, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — AFP

Colombian officials said they did not fear a tsunami after the early-morning quake, which was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela.

It prompted building evacuations in Bogota, AFP reporters saw, while news footage showed collapsed buildings elsewhere in the country.

The governor of Colombia’s Choco province wrote on X that there were injuries and serious damage to buildings in the department’s capital Quibdo.

News outlets aired footage of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Pereira and Manizales in a tourist region called Eje Cafetero.

‘Strong, really strong’

“There is no electricity or cell phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house,” Martha Estrada, a 66-year-old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP.

Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia’s third largest city, also reported “major damage” that was being evaluated with drones. At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city, with people trapped inside, the mayor said.

The city has requested teams from Bogota and Medellin to aid in rescue efforts, he added.

People look for survivors amid the rubble of a collapsed building after an earthquake in Cali, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — AFP

“The quake was very, very strong,” said Valeria Polo, a 29-year-old content creator in Bogota.

Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said. These airports serve Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, the agency wrote on X.

Colombia’s newly inaugurated President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency.

“The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed,” he said in a national address around midday from Bogota. “The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble.”

De La Espriella, a right-wing politician who has never before held elected office, earlier said in a video filmed while flying to Bogota that he was suspending his planned activities to lead emergency coordination efforts out of the capital.

Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings.

News outlets aired footage of some buildings with their facades ripped off by the quake.

In Bogota some people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw.

Land of earthquakes and landslides

Smaller earthquakes are not uncommon in Colombia, which is crisscrossed by three ranges of the Andean mountains. However, it is landslides which have historically been the deadliest natural disasters in the country, with the Armero disaster in 1985 killing some 25,000 people.

Cities in the country’s coffee region, including Armenia and Pereira, suffered a devastating 6.2 magnitude quake in 1999, which killed more than 1,000 people.

Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage, mostly on the coast near the capital, Caracas.

World.title: Police in India's Jharkhand fire tear gas, use batons to disperse youth protesters
World.content:
Police in eastern India used tear gas, batons and water cannon to disperse thousands of youth protesters as they marched on the state legislature in Jharkhand state on Monday over alleged wrongdoing in civil service examinations, TV footage showed.

Students and unemployed youth in Jharkhand, one of India’s poorer states, launched the protests late last month over the alleged wrongdoing, including recruitment test paper leaks.

The protest follows weeks-long youth-led demonstrations in the capital, Delhi, also linked to exam paper leaks, which led to the resignation of the country’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan last month.

Police and paramilitary forces used tear gas, pellet guns and batons in Delhi to scatter some 50,000 youth protesters, some of whom clashed with police. The demonstrations were seen as a reflection of their anger over corruption in education, a lack of opportunities and unemployment.

The demands of protesters in Jharkhand include an overhaul of the state’s examination system, cancellation of some tests and an investigation by the federal police.

At least six protesters were on hunger strike, including student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, 33, who has been fasting for more than a week.

“We want the whole system to change,” Mahto said, as quoted by Indian media, demanding an end to the use of a private company that conducts tests for state civil service.

The protest began on July 25 and intensified after thousands gathered at a stadium in the state capital, Ranchi.

On Monday, they marched on the state legislature, climbing over police barricades, holding placards, waving the national flag and shouting slogans, amid high security.

Some pushed against barricades and scuffled with police, who responded by firing tear gas rounds, using water cannon and beating them with batons, TV footage showed.

Police said they had to use mild force after some protesters became violent.

“We showed minimal aggression for a really short time because they are just students,” Ranchi city police chief Paras Rana told ANI news agency.

“I appeal to everyone to be peaceful and not be violent. Your demands are reaching the government; do not show aggression.”

The state government ruled by a regional party opposed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi has held talks with the protesters. It said a majority of their demands had been accepted and that it was open to more talks.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Peshawar High Court grants transit bail to Noreen Niazi in Peca case
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Monday granted transit bail to Noreen Niazi, the sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in a case registered under the Peca Act 2016, directing her to appear before the relevant Islamabad court on or before August 20.

In July, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) registered a case against Noreen, accusing her of passing derogatory and inflammatory remarks against state institutions during a podcast interview and in subsequent clips shared on X.

A single-member PHC bench comprising Justice Arshad Ali heard Noreen’s petition, represented by a panel of lawyers, including Ali Zaman, Amir Zeb and Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah

In its order issued on Monday, the bench stated that the petitioner had approached the court seeking transit bail in connection with a first information report (FIR) registered against her at the NCCIA police station in Islamabad on July 27 under various provisions of the Peca Act 2016 and the Pakistan Penal Code, enabling her to approach the competent court.

The order noted that the petitioner had claimed to have been falsely implicated in the case and that, except for the bare allegations contained in the FIR, there was no other cogent evidence on record to connect her with the alleged offence.

“In the circumstances of the case, the petitioner’s request, being reasonable, merits consideration,” the order noted, adding that “consequently this application is accepted and the accused petitioner is granted ad-interim transit pre-arrest bail provided she furnishes bail bonds in the sum of Rs80,000 with two sureties,” it said.

The bench also directed the petitioner to approach the competent forum in Islamabad for bail on or before August 20, as the PHC order would be effective till that day.

Meanwhile, the counsels for the petitioner argued that their client was innocent and falsely implicated in the case registered at the NCCIA police station.

They said the local police were trying to arrest their client with mala fide intentions, to humiliate and unjustly harass her for some ulterior motive.

The counsels also said the allegations contained in the FIR were false and politically motivated, and were based on an erroneous interpretation of statements allegedly attributed to their client.

Talking to reporters after the hearing, Noreen said she came to know about the NCCIA case against her after arriving in Peshawar.

“I did speak inside in my house, which I do not have recollection of, and someone got that to them and they made a case against me,” she claimed.

Noreen further alleged that cases had been lodged against her other sisters and that now one had been registered against her as well. “Too many cases are being registered across Pakistan, and no one knows why they have been lodged. The case against me is the same,” she said.

In response to a question, she said they had never been to Peshawar, so the question of their interfering in KP affairs did not even arise.

Earlier, the Lahore High Court had also granted her an interim protective bail, directing her to approach a relevant Islamabad court.

Before registering an FIR, the NCCIA had summoned Noreen to appear before it on July 20 over allegations of disseminating “false, offensive and inflammatory” content against state institutions.

While the notice did not specify the content in relation to which Noreen has been summoned, it was issued after the clip of her making claims in relation to last year’s brief military conflict between Pakistan and India was widely shared on social media.

In the clip, she is seen alleging during an interview that the conflict was “orchestrated” to improve the image of Pakistan’s military. She claimed the “drama” was played out in collaboration with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, questioning why Modi would have refrained from further attacking Pakistan otherwise.

In this connection, she went on to allege that the objective was to get Israel recognised by Pakistan, linking US President Donald Trump’s praise of Pakistan’s leadership with Israel’s recognition as well.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar.
