A better term would be depth of focus, but it's called field. The depth of field is influenced by the interplay of the aperture, the focal length of the lens, and the position of the subjects within the scene. Bokeh: “Bokeh” is a word for the overuse of extreme depth of field. Just kidding. It's a Japanese word to describe the blur quality of the out-of-focus portions of an image. You might hear a photographer say an image has “smooth bokeh.” Just nod and back away slowly. Kidding, really. This means that the blurry portion of the image is nice and smooth, without harsh circles or a jittery sense of blur. Got it? OK, now run.

Point-and-Shoot vs. Interchangeable Lens

Photograph: Scott Gilbertson

If you want to step up from a camera phone, I'd suggest skipping over point-and-shoot cameras and going to an interchangeable lens system. The reason is that most point-and-shoot cameras are only moderately better than a phone. Some aren't even as good as your phone. You do get a zoom lens in many cases, which is a step up, but it's not much of a step, especially for the price.

Tech.title: The Rise of the 1 am Job Interview
Tech.content:
When Tim Millard received an email about interviewing for a media relations job in January, six months into his job hunt, he assumed he’d speak to a human. When he was instead instructed to record himself answering a series of questions on camera, he felt a familiar pang of resignation—one that had followed him throughout the job hunt.

“I figured, I have to do this if I want to be considered for the job,” Millard tells WIRED. So, that evening, the Atlanta-based communications and marketing expert tidied his living room and set up his laptop. The email had left the timing for the interview open-ended, and he figured he might as well get it done as soon as possible. “What else was I going to do at 9:30 at night?”

The questions were pretty standard for the role. How would Millard pitch a story to the media? How would he cultivate relationships with local journalists? But the setup was bizarre. He sat in front of his laptop, watching as a question popped up on the screen. He had roughly half a minute to think about his response.

“Once the 30 seconds was up, ‘ding!’ Now you have two minutes to record your answer,” Millard said. “It felt so out of this world.”

Millard received an automated rejection email in March. But the experience unknowingly wedged him into a trend currently reshaping the modern job search. As automated video interviews and AI become a bigger part of the recruitment process, so do late-night interviews.

Tech.title: August Is a Stargazer’s Dream, With a Solar Eclipse, Meteors and a Planet Parade
Tech.content:
August is proving to be a dazzling month to head outside and gaze up at the sky. Among the many remarkable events to marvel at is a planetary parade, with six planets visible at once.

The show starts this Wednesday evening, Aug. 12, and continues until Aug. 17 or 18, depending on your location. This planet parade includes Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, Uranus, Saturn and Neptune, and as with most prior parades, the planets line up on a nice curve, so it should be a little easier to see all of them. The parade is visible across the US and Canada.

You need to wake up early for this one, as the best time to see the planet parade is just before sunrise. This is due to Jupiter and Mercury not popping up above the eastern horizon until about 15 to 20 minutes before the sun. The good news is that Mercury and Jupiter are right next to each other and typically quite visible. A pair of binoculars should help immensely, but make sure to be careful since the sun will follow Mercury and Jupiter over the horizon in pretty short order.

The rest of the planets are much higher in the sky and present less of a visual risk. Mars is higher in the eastern sky and is visible without the need for visual aids. Uranus will be higher in the eastern sky, trending south. Following that curve, you can see Saturn in the southern sky as a yellowish dot. Neptune is nearby at the end of the line. Uranus and Neptune require a telescope or high-powered binoculars to view, and if you want a superior view of Saturn, that amplification will help too.

Before Wednesday, Jupiter trends too close to the sun to be safely visible, and after around Aug. 17-18, Mercury ends up too close to the sun to be viewed safely. Before and after that date, you can still see a five-planet parade for quite some time.

Venus is also technically visible at night. It sets along the western horizon just after sunset, so it’s not visible at the same time as Mercury and Jupiter. However, if you don’t mind pulling an all-nighter, you can see all seven planets in the sky on the same night.

Do I need any amplification devices for this?

The inclusion of Neptune and Uranus means that you will need some sort of amplification device to see all the planets. Binoculars work, as both Uranus and Neptune can be seen (albeit faintly) with a good pair, and they’ll also help you see Mercury before sunrise.

A telescope is a much better tool since you can more easily see the rings of Saturn along with the other planets. We don’t recommend using a telescope to find Mercury, since you may accidentally catch the sun, which is not a good idea.

The Perseids meteor shower and the planet parade are visible at exactly the same time. Stellarium

Part of a triple feature coming Wednesday

If you’re looking for one single day to go out and view the sky for the rest of the year, there’s a compelling case for Aug. 12. The planet parade ramps up, then continues for the next week. It is always fun to see a bunch of planets from the solar system in a single night, but in terms of thrill, it’s arguably the least interesting thing happening that night..

The Perseids meteor shower is set to peak on the evening of Aug. 12, which means those who go out to see all the planets can virtually guarantee some meteor sightings as well, since Perseids is one of the most active meteor showers of the year. In a fortuitous turn of events, the Perseus constellation, the point from which the Perseid meteors appear to originate, is right next to Mars and Uranus. That means you can scout out the parade and see meteors at the same time since they’re in the same part of the sky. The timing and placement don’t get much better than that.

If that isn’t cool enough, nature has one more thing to toss into the equation: Aug. 12 is also the date of the next solar eclipse. North America is largely sitting this one out, but if you draw a line from Washington state to North Carolina, all the states north of that line will get at least a partial solar eclipse with about 20% coverage. Since the sun isn’t completely covered, proper safety measures for solar eclipse viewing are highly advisable to avoid eye injuries.

Three prominent celestial events happening in one 24-hour span are pretty rare, so if you’re up for it, it’s a great day to look up.

Tech.title: Report: Analyst Shatters Expectations of an All-Glass iPhone
Tech.content:
If you were hoping for an all-glass iPhone, a new report from Barron’s might shatter that dream. The financial news source reports that Jefferies analyst Edison Lee believes development on an all-glass mobile device has come to a halt.

According to the report, Lee thinks the device was canceled because of “poor production yield,” or not enough defect-free units being successfully made during production.

An Apple representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The device was rumored to launch in the fall of 2027 to celebrate the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, and Barron’s reports it could have cost an eye-watering $2,060.

Rumors of an all-glass iPhone began after Apple filed for a patent in 2019 on an electronic device with a “six-sided glass enclosure.” The device in the patent resembles an iPhone, with app icons on one side and a way to signal to others that you’re on a call on the other side. The device also has curved glass panels and seemingly no cutouts.

“We believe the plan was to extend the all-glass features to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further raising their average selling price and margin,” Lee wrote, according to Barron’s.

For more on Apple, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and everything the company announced at its Worldwide Developers Conference in June.

Tech.title: Valve Warns Steam Machine Buyers About Scam Messages After Cyberattack
Tech.content:
If you’ve been holding out on buying Valve’s ludicrously expensive home console, you may have saved yourself from more than an empty wallet. European customers who ordered a Steam Machine or Steam Controller may be the victims of a personal information data breach after one of Valve’s hardware distribution partners was hit by a cyberattack.

CEVA Logistics, the company that helps organize Valve’s European supply chain, informed its partner of the data breach on Aug. 7. A Valve spokesperson told CNET that the company spent the weekend assembling a list of at-risk customers, notifying them about the attack via email on Monday morning.

“Though CEVA is still investigating the attack, we wanted to at least send out messaging to all customers we can assume were affected based on what we currently know,” the spokesperson said.

What Valve currently knows is that the personal information revealed by the cyberattack is likely all delivery-related. CEVA told Valve that the breach revealed customers’ names, countries, street addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. According to Valve, “payment information, passwords and Steam Guard codes” are all safe, since CEVA doesn’t have access to this data.

Because phone numbers and email addresses linked to Steam accounts are openly circulating, Valve warned against phishing attacks that may be looking for additional personal information in the coming days.



“Expect fake messages – email, SMS or phone – that mention your hardware order and appear to come from Steam, Valve or a delivery company,” Valve wrote in its email to affected customers. “They may quote your address back to you to prove they’re genuine. They may ask you to confirm a delivery, pay a small customs or redelivery fee or sign in somewhere to ‘verify’ your order. Treat all of them as fake.”

Valve reminded customers that Steam’s support team only handles issues on the official help page and never sends messages over Steam chat or through third-party services. Company employees will also never ask for a customer’s password or Steam Guard codes.

The finer details of the attack currently remain unclear, as there’s no official information available on how many customers were affected, how much data was stolen or how the cyberattack infiltrated CEVA Logistics’ systems. In its statement, Valve said it is “pressing CEVA for the full scope” of the breach.

Alongside CEVA’s internal investigation, authorities in the Netherlands are looking into the attack. A spokesperson for the Dutch data protection authority told TechCrunch that the agency has received data breach reports from at least 10 companies in relation to the hack.

In addition to the data breach, FreightWaves reported operations at eight of the company’s warehouses have been affected by the cyberattack, causing potential delays or cancellations to customer orders in the coming days.

CEVA Logistics did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Tech.title: How to Watch Made by Google, the Pixel 11 and Watch 5 Event
Tech.content:
The Pixel 11, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and the Pixel Watch 5 will be unveiled in just two days at the Made by Google event on Wednesday, Aug. 12. We also expect to see the debut of the standard Pixel 11 smartphone. As the date nears, leaks and rumors have been spreading like wildfire, but we still won’t know everything until Google takes the wraps off everything later this week.

Like last year, Google has tapped a series of celebrities to host. It confirmed that comedian Trevor Noah will be hosting, with additional stars like Stephen Curry and Ayami Nakajo to make appearances.

While the next generation of the Pixel phone lineup may not be a major departure from its predecessor, there’s still a lot to look forward to. Below, we’ll go through what to expect and how to watch it on Wednesday.

How to watch the Made By Google event

The Made by Google event will take place on Aug. 12 at 3 p.m. PT. You can stream the event from the Made By Google YouTube account below.

New Pixel 11 phones

The primary devices to be showcased at this Made by Google event will be the next generation of Pixel phones, and we already know a fair amount about them. Rumors suggest the only devices to expect are the standard Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, the foldable Pixel 11 Pro Fold and the Pixel Watch 5.

The Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold scored 8.3 in our review last year. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

Design-wise, don’t expect the new Pixel family of phones to look much different from their predecessors. Leaked images show largely the same phone design DNA that we’ve seen since the Pixel 9 lineup, with only small tweaks and refinements. Those looking for a more dramatic change to its appearance may have to wait for the Pixel 12.

We can assume that the new Pixel 11 phones will have boosted internals, like a new Tensor G6 chipset, though we wouldn’t expect it to blow the current Tensor G5 chip out of the water by any means. Interestingly, when Google launched the Pixel 10A earlier this year, the processor wasn’t updated, so it will be curious to see what the company does with its flagship phone lineup. Performance of Google’s homemade chips has lagged behind the competition, especially graphically, but the tech giant’s priority has primarily been to enhance the on-device AI capabilities of its phones, providing as much raw computational power as possible.



Google’s Pixel 10 Pro XL packed a suite of new features. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Rumors suggest changes to RAM and storage in the base model. In particular, a rumor reported by DealLabs says that Google is getting rid of the 128GB storage option and making baseline storage 256GB, which would be a welcome change. What’s not so welcome is that we can likely expect all phones in the Pixel 11 lineup to be about $100 more expensive across the board, given the global RAM shortage and other tech giants raising their phone prices, including Samsung.

The only real new feature Google is teasing is a new notification light on the backside of the device. Previously rumored to be named Pixel Glow, the feature is now said to be called HiLight when it debuts, according to the latest leak of a French marketing graphic for the phone. The feature will light up when your favorite contacts are calling or when you’re talking to Gemini when the phone is face down. How much more functionality, if any, HiLight has in store is unknown.

On the software side, we expect to see more features from Gemini Intelligence that were announced during the Google I/O conference earlier this year. While the latest Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 family of devices ships with the most current agentic AI features, the Pixel phones are always the first devices in line that show off Google’s latest AI advancements, and they’ll certainly be packed to the gills with it.

All of the Pixel 11 devices will ship with Android 17 out of the box.

Google’s Pixel Watch impressed us. Celso Bulgatti/CNET

Pixel Watch 5

Alongside the Pixel 11 series of phones, we’re also expecting to see the introduction of the Pixel Watch 5. We were impressed with last year’s Pixel Watch 4, so hopefully Google continues down a successful path with the Watch 5.

At this point, we know very little about the changes to the latest generation of Google’s smartwatch. Based on leaks and rumors, the design remains essentially unchanged since the first Pixel Watch, and that’s a good thing — it’s one of the best watch designs you can find.

One of our first glimpses of the device allegedly came from someone who found it underwater while scuba diving. Whether this was planned by Google or a complete coincidence, the very strange leak of the new watch certainly looks the same as before.

We can expect upgraded internals, but exactly how much of a boost the Pixel Watch 5 will get over its predecessor remains to be seen. Rumors suggest that all models of the watch, like the Pixel 11 family, will also see a price increase.

What else could Google announce?

While this Made by Google event is undoubtedly for the Pixel family of phones and the new watch, there’s a chance we could see even more from the tech giant on Aug. 12.

Pixel Tag

To compete with the likes of Apple’s AirTag, Google may introduce its own Bluetooth tracking device, dubbed the Pixel Tag. A leaked image of the device appeared over at 9to5Google, showing a small, oblong tracker that will likely support Google’s Find Hub network. Whether the Pixel Tag will make it to the show remains to be seen, but if it does arrive, we hope that it will support Ultra-Wideband for precision item tracking.

Android XR glasses

The product certainly won’t carry the Pixel name, but Google’s been talking about XR glasses for some time now, and there’s a possibility we get to hear more about some of the upcoming products.

We already know that both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster will be among the first brands to release Android XR glasses, which got a reaffirmed fall 2026 release window at the recent Samsung Unpacked event, putting Gemini’s impressive multimodal AI capabilities right in front of your eyes.

Googlebooks

It would make more sense for Google to have its own event for the upcoming Googlebook line of laptops, but we could still get a sneak peek during next week’s event.

The Googlebook may end up having the best operating system to go with the next Pixel phones, as they both run Android and should provide a more seamless experience working across each other. It’s no wonder the new laptop line could be the ultimate laptop for Android fans when it arrives. And they should be arriving soon, too. Lenovo recently shared some images of its upcoming Googlebooks, so it’s possible they could make an appearance.

Tech.title: Get Ready for a Lunar Eclipse That Will Be Visible All Over North America
Tech.content:
It’s a great summer to look to the skies. August looks to be one of the best months for skygazing in recent memory, and the hits just keep on coming. In addition to a planet parade, a meteor shower and a solar eclipse, a lunar eclipse is set for the end of August for those in North and South America.

The eclipse coincides with the full moon, which occurs on the evening of Aug. 27. Per Time and Date, the eclipse begins at 9:23 p.m. ET and lasts until 3:01 a.m. ET, for a total of about 5 and a half hours. The Old Farmer’s Almanac reports that August’s full moon peaks in brightness at 12:18 a.m. ET on Aug. 28, which means this is all happening at the same time.

Most of the world gets to see this partial lunar eclipse, but the eastern and central US have the best seats. NASA/JPL-Caltech

The path is pretty large and includes all of North and South America, along with all of Africa and Europe, seeing at least part of the action. It’s not a full lunar eclipse, even if you’re in the best spot. NASA says that about 93% of the moon will be covered, which means you’ll still see a sliver of the moon along with a “rusty, coppery tint” along the edge that’s covered. Time and Date bumps that figure up to 96%, so it’s likely somewhere between the two.

Those in the eastern US and the eastern half of the Midwest will have the best seats in the house for this one. People along the Rocky Mountains will have a better view than most, with the West Coast and Alaska getting at least a partial eclipse. Unlike solar eclipses, which can be dangerous to view, a lunar eclipse is perfectly safe to watch with the naked eye. In fact, using a telescope or binoculars is encouraged so you can see the eclipse more clearly.

Since it’s not a total lunar eclipse, August’s Sturgeon Moon doesn’t qualify as a blood moon. It’s close enough that it’ll certainly look like one, though. This is due to the way sunlight interacts with Earth’s atmosphere. The atmosphere scatters blue light away, which is known as Rayleigh scattering. This leaves only red and orange light to pass through. It’s bent by the Earth’s atmosphere and lands on the moon, giving it a reddish appearance.

The Perseids is summer’s most active meteor shower. Preston Dyches/NASA

Part of an action-packed August

The partial lunar eclipse caps off what should be a very active month for sky enthusiasts. Somewhat strangely, most of the action takes place over just two days. The first day is Aug. 12, which features a planet parade, the peak of the Perseids meteor shower, and for those fortunate enough to be in the path, a solar eclipse that might take place at sunset. That’s a lot of activity for just one day. You do have 15 days to sleep it off if you want to catch the lunar eclipse on the evening of Aug. 27.

This is also the best month of 2026 to view Venus, which is taking a vacation from its spot near the sun, making it much easier to see in the evening after the sun goes down.

Tech.title: A Lucky Few Will See a Rare Sight During the Upcoming Solar Eclipse
Tech.content:
It’s been two years since the last total solar eclipse, but another one is coming this Wednesday — and with it, a special rare bonus. Some people will get to see the solar eclipse during sunset, giving them an extraordinary view. The only problem is, you may have to jet off on a summer vacation to see it.

The total eclipse will only grace the shores of a few countries. According to NASA, the total eclipse on Aug. 12 will hit Greenland, Iceland, the northern half of Spain and one corner of Portugal. Spain is at the tail end of the eclipse, and as such, it will occur later in the day at around sunset, giving viewers in Spain a spectacular sight.

Other countries in Europe and Africa will also get quite a show. Most of Europe and a sizable portion of northern Africa are still getting a partial solar eclipse, which will happen around sunset. That means tens of millions of people will be in the right place to see a partial or total solar eclipse at sunset.

Russia is the luckiest country this time around. The eclipse starts at sunrise near the uninhabited Taymyr Peninsula, streaks across the world all day, and then Russians on the other side of the country are in the path for the partial solar eclipse at sunset, making Russia the only country that will see the eclipse at both sunrise and sunset.

How often do sunset eclipses happen?

Sunset eclipses don’t occur very often, at least where people can see them. There are two reasons for this.

The first is that solar eclipses usually only last for a few hours, and the timing for that being right at sunset isn’t terribly common.

The other reason is that solar eclipses have long paths, and sometimes those paths cut through the ocean or places where people don’t live. In the last 15 years, only a handful of total eclipses sit in that Venn diagram of occurring late enough in the day to happen at sunset, while also taking place where humans can see it.

The most recent sunset eclipse in North America was in 2014, but it was only a partial eclipse. South America’s most recent one was in July 2019, where people in Chile and Argentina had the best view of a total solar eclipse happening at sunset, while most of the rest of the country had a partial view. Asia’s most recent was in December 2019.

In short, this is a once-in-a-decade event for most of the world.

The path of this year’s solar eclipse takes it across the northern portions of Earth before ending in Europe. North Americans won’t see much. NASA

Will this eclipse be visible in North America?

North America is pretty far from the main action, but a few states are in the path. The math is a little complicated, but if you look at a map of the US and draw a line from Alaska to North Carolina, all the states north of that line will get a little bit of an eclipse (less than 20% coverage), and all the states south of that line are sitting this one out.

If you live in the path and want to check it out, be sure to adhere to proper solar eclipse viewing safety protocols so that you don’t harm your eyes.

Tech.title: I’ve Tried These College Dorm Devices At Home. Here’s What I Recommend
Tech.content:
It doesn’t take much to give dorms powerful smart upgrades that are useful — and stylish — for anyone packing up for move-in day. I’ve kept my eye out for devices that fit well in dorms during my testing, including the latest smart speaker with big sound, an AI table lamp that learns your mood and pocket-size security for your precious belongings.

Good news: These devices are all subscription-free, and I’ve avoided any high-budget items to help with your budget. See what’s the ideal fit for your college dorm or university apartment.

Lepro A1 table lamp

Lepro can come up with so many interesting color cycles for this lamp. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

When I tested this spiraling table lamp, I found its use of AI prompts fun and incredibly versatile. The lamp can use voice or text ideas to suggest all kinds of light schemes, including colors, patterns, movement and much more. You can say anything from “Star Wars” to “workout mode” to get several interesting ideas. It can also sync to music if you prefer.

The light patterns can create soothing glows, dancing party swirls and everything in between. From studying to cozy vibes, all you have to do is describe the mood and pick your favorite option from what AI comes up with. Check out more of my experiments with this foot-high light in my full review.

Google Home speaker

This new speaker is larger than past Nest versions but smaller than the Nest Audio.

I recently tried out the Google Home Speaker, and found it has some of the best sound in the $100 range, with a surprisingly strong bass level, easily enough to fill a dorm room. It’s also easy to set up with the Google Home app. The speaker can connect to a variety of music streaming services, including Spotify and Tidal, as well as apps like Netflix and Google Plus.

In addition to playing music, the Gemini for Home features a speaker that allows you to set timers, reminders and calendar events with a “Hey, Google.” It can also answer any question from what info it pulls from the internet. And the speaker can control many of the other smart devices listed here with the right voice commands. That’s all for free — the subscription versions of Gemini aren’t really necessary in a dorm.

Tapo smart surge protector

Tapo’s surge protector is filled with smarts. Tapo

Tapo’s surge protector protects from electrical surges, sure, but each plug and USB port can also connect to a smart home app and allow you to name it, then turn it on/off remotely or with voice commands. This power strip is an important add-on for a desk where students may do a lot of work on a computer alongside other devices — including those on my list.

Amazon Echo Spot

Amazon’s smart clock can do a little bit of everything. Amazon

Amazon makes many smart speakers and displays, but the Echo Spot is one of the best suited for a dorm room. It’s designed to serve as an alarm clock, with a top screen that can show you the music playing, the weather, the time and more. Unlike an alarm app on your phone, it can perform gradual wake-ups with glowing lights and growing music, too, or do the same to help you fall asleep.

Like the Google speaker, you can connect Alexa to a variety of music services, including Spotify, Apple Music, Tidal and many others. Via Alexa app connections, you can also use voice commands for timers, alarms, reminders and compatible smart device controls.

Aqara P100 multipurpose sensor

Aqara’s sensor is far easier to place and use than older models offering similar, but more limited, capabilities. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Most security sensors aren’t designed for dorms, but this new Aqara model is made for nearly everything. On its own, it can connect to the Aqara app and give you alerts whenever anything is opened or closed — like a door, a closet, a drawer, a lid and so on. You can place the small sensor on nearly anything with adhesive strips and know when it’s opening, ideal for securing certain spots in a dorm.

If you want to add an Aqara hub device, like the Aqara M3 hub, the sensor can do much more, like detecting tampering, vibration, tilting and more movements. However, you may not want to pay extra for a hub or an Aqara camera that adds these capabilities, so open/close sensing can be sufficient.

Wiz Connected Color smart bulb

Wiz smart light bulbs offer an impressive range of tunable colors. Chris Wedel/CNET

Not every dorm room needs a dazzling smart lamp. However, if the dorm has normal light sockets, you can upgrade it with a very affordable Wiz light bulb. These cost only around $10 but let you adjust color and brightness to whatever you want, whenever you want it. That’s useful for late-night study sessions, morning wakeups and much more. Plus, it also supports voice assistants and scheduling options if you like to tinker.

Lockly Wi-Fi smart safe

Lockly’s biometric safe is an excellent option for smaller home safes. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Most home safes are far too large to lug into a dorm. Lockly’s safe is small enough to carry with you, but it offers high-quality security and a useful biometric thumbprint reader, too. I tried smashing it open with hammers and screwdrivers, but the safe easily resisted my efforts. It’s small enough to fit in a drawer, on a shelf, under a bed, in a closet and many other spots. Just remember to replace the batteries every year or so.

K-Mini Mate Coffee Maker

This tiny Keurig cup coffeemaker is super speedy, too. Keurig/CNET

You can’t beat this tiny coffee maker for size or price (it’s currently on sale for $50). The one-cup coffee maker is only 4 inches wide and takes just a couple of minutes to brew 12 ounces. It’s a lifesaver when time is very short, and it travels well, too.

For more info you may find useful in similar cases, visit my recommendations for the best security devices for renters and the best security that can move with you.

Tech.title: T-Mobile Shifts to 3-Year Phone Installments with New ‘2.0’ Mobile Plans
Tech.content:
If you’re thinking of buying a new phone through T-Mobile, you’ll now be paying less per month, but for a year longer than its previous deals. The carrier has ditched its 24-month payment plans in favor of 36-month installment plans. It also rebranded its major phone plans and offers student plans with the option of adding 5G home internet service.

In an environment in which everything costs more, all three major wireless phone carriers have introduced plans to draw in customers who want to reduce what millions of people see as an essential expense. In recent months, AT&T introduced its modular Build-A-Plan, and Verizon cut prices and then rolled out its Simplicity plan. Now it’s T-Mobile’s turn.

An extended phone flex

Before Aug. 6, when you purchased a new phone through T-Mobile, you could buy it outright or pay a monthly installment over 24 months. The new Equipment Installment Plan Flex 36 option lets you make those payments over 36 months, reducing the monthly amount.

What makes EIP Flex 36 different from the company’s EIP Standard plan (which remains an option as EIP Standard 36) is that all upfront costs are rolled into those three years of payments — the device, taxes and fees — making the initial cost zero. Even with most 0% finance plans, customers must pay taxes on the cost of the phone and pay an activation fee.

T-Mobile’s press release says the EIP Flex 36 option for “well-qualified customers” has, “for a limited time, 0% APR.” When I inquired if “limited time” implied that the rate could go up, a T-Mobile representative confirmed the rate would remain the same during the life of the term. The fine print does note that the rate could be between 0 and 24% depending on a customer’s creditworthiness.

Going forward, the financing options for new customers will be to choose a 36-month EIP plan or pay the full cost of the device. If you want to pay off a phone earlier than the full term, that’s an option, too.

‘2.0’ unlimited plans (that feel more like 1.1)

In software, a full-number version increment implies an update that’s bigger than small tweaks; it’s why your iPhone was recently updated to iOS 26.6, applying fixes and security updates, while iOS 27.0 was just released in beta, with major new features — such as Siri AI — and is expected in September.

Along with EIP Flex 36, T-Mobile is updating its unlimited postpaid mobile plans to 2.0 versions: Experience Beyond 2.0, Experience More 2.0, Essentials 2.0 and Essentials Saver 2.0.

However, the 2.0 in this case appears to be a formality to pair with the EIP Flex 36 and EIP Standard 36 installment plans: The features and base pricing remain the same as the Experience Beyond, Experience More and Essentials plans.

T-Mobile says that customers already on those plans can stay where they are, or switch to the 2.0 versions if they want to take advantage of the 36-month financing option.

As part of the switchover, T-Mobile also retired its Better Value plan, which was introduced less than a year ago and billed as a “limited time” option. Better Value was almost identical to Experience More, but with more generous high-speed mobile hotspot and international data amounts.

Student Perks plans

Now that it’s August, with the academic year about to begin, college-bound kids (and their parents) are likely figuring out what they need to pack for school — and that includes mobile phone plans. For those who want their mobile independence, T-Mobile has launched Student Perks discounts that can cost as little as $30 a month (for the Essentials Saver plan with AutoPay enabled). A limit of two students can be on the account.

And for those living off-campus in need of fast internet for all-night writing sessions, T-Mobile is offering a Student Perks bundle of 5G Home Internet for $30 a month. The deal also includes up to $200 back in virtual prepaid card credit when signing up for the service.
